summary: Automated Evidence Collection and Monitoring for Industrial Transformation and Recycling Facilities
content: Automated Evidence Collection and Monitoring for Industrial Transformation and Recycling Facilities

caName: Automated Evidence Collection and Monitoring for Industrial Transformation and Recycling Facilities
description:
A contract for research services to design, prototype and evaluate data pipelines for collecting, structuring, validating and monitoring evidence from heterogeneous public data sources. The pipelines should combine deterministic data engineering (API and database extraction, parsing), machine learning, and large language models (LLMs) with human expert validation. The contract will be structured in two broad packages.
Work-package 1 supports INCITE (https://innovation-centre-for-industrial-transformation.ec.europa.eu). It shall develop a pilot to identify and update project-level information on emerging and established techniques for decarbonisation, depollution, resource efficiency and circular economy in industrial and livestock installations, covering technology, maturity, financing, performance and dependencies.
Work-package 2 shall develop and tests methods to build and maintain a facility-level dataset of circular-economy installations in EU Member States. This covers facilities that recover, sort, process or recycle waste and by-products into secondary materials, including their location, capacities, technologies, ownership, inputs, outputs and commercial links.
Both work-packages are exploratory pilots: the aim is to demonstrate and rigorously evaluate workflows, not to deliver a production platform. The contractor must deliver documented prototype pipelines, validated datasets, a quantitative evaluation of accuracy, coverage and cost, and a feasibility assessment for continuous updates and scale-up.
In terms of the technical approach, the contractor is expected to propose a hybrid architecture, choosing the most appropriate technique for each task and justifying it on accuracy, cost, reproducibility and maintainability. For example:
•	Structured sources (e.g. EU funding databases such as CORDIS, Innovation Fund and LIFE; the EU Industrial Emissions Portal; national permit registries; Eurostat) can be accessed deterministically via APIs, bulk downloads or database extraction wherever possible.
•	Machine learning and rule-based methods can be used for classification, deduplication, geocoding and entity resolution across sources.
•	LLMs can be used mainly to extract structured information from unstructured documents (permits, company websites, press releases, scientific publications, sustainability and financial reports). Agent-based workflows can be used in cases where multi-step search is necessary.
title: Automated Evidence Collection and Monitoring for Industrial Transformation and Recycling Facilities

summary: Transport Poverty Hub Website and Dashboard: Design and Development of a Geospatial Dashboard and Website to Identify and Monitor Transport Poverty Indicators in the EU
content: Transport Poverty Hub Website and Dashboard: Design and Development of a Geospatial Dashboard and Website to Identify and Monitor Transport Poverty Indicators in the EU

caName: Transport Poverty Hub Website and Dashboard: Design and Development of a Geospatial Dashboard and Website to Identify and Monitor Transport Poverty Indicators in the EU
description:
The aim of this contract is to design and develop a new Transport Poverty Hub website, a web platform dedicated to the analysis and visualisation of transport poverty indicators across the European Union (EU). The platform will strengthen the capacity of the Joint Research Centre (JRC) to monitor and evaluate transport accessibility, availability, and affordability, thereby informing effective policymaking and stakeholder engagement. Transport poverty is defined in Article 2(2) of Regulation (EU) 2023/955 establishing the Social Climate Fund, and Member States are required to address it in their Social Climate Plans; the Hub will make the corresponding evidence base publicly available.

The new Transport Poverty Hub will feature a user-friendly interface equipped with advanced geospatial data visualisation tools, enabling the exploration of transport poverty indicators at various scales, from neighbourhood to regional and national level. The platform will support interactive dashboards, dynamic map features, and downloadable reports generated by the platform, allowing users to conduct high-resolution analyses on the different transport access modes (walking, cycling, driving, public transport) and socio-economic factors affecting transport equity.

The development involves implementing a robust architecture designed for supporting EU official languages, together with a data model and interface designed to accommodate the progressive extension of geographical coverage to all EU Member States and the inclusion of multiple geospatial indicators. The contract also covers the creation of modular components aligned with the EU’s eUI design standards, designed for reusability across other JRC platforms and for consistency with other European Commission (EC)’s data initiatives and web presence.

By engaging external expertise, the JRC draws on professional web development and geospatial design capacity not available in-house, for a public web platform that will bring EU transport poverty analysis to policymakers and citizens. All results produced under the contract, including source code, methodologies, and documentation, will be owned by the EU, with pre-existing and third-party materials licensed as necessary; components will be built to EU design standards and reused across other JRC platforms as needed.
title: Transport Poverty Hub Website and Dashboard: Design and Development of a Geospatial Dashboard and Website to Identify and Monitor Transport Poverty Indicators in the EU

summary: Assessment of the Performance and Effectiveness of Farmer Cooperatives and Farmer Groups in the Cocoa Sectors of Ghana and Ivory Coast
content: Assessment of the Performance and Effectiveness of Farmer Cooperatives and Farmer Groups in the Cocoa Sectors of Ghana and Ivory Coast

caName: Assessment of the Performance and Effectiveness of Farmer Cooperatives and Farmer Groups in the Cocoa Sectors of Ghana and Ivory Coast
description:
The primary objective of this contract is to conduct a comprehensive, large-scale study on the current state and effectiveness of cocoa farmer cooperatives and farmer groups in Ghana and Côte d’Ivoire (incorporating but not limited to cooperative societies in Ghana and COOP CA and COOP simplifié in Côte d’Ivoire). This study will represent the first nationally representative analysis of cocoa cooperatives and farmer groups across the two countries. It will uniquely combine data collection at two levels: (1) the organizational governance and operational management of cooperatives and farmer groups, and (2) the individual farmer members, including their engagement, benefits, and challenges. By integrating insights from behavioural economics, collective action theory, organizational studies, and development economics, the study will adopt an interdisciplinary approach to evaluate how structural, managerial, and behavioural factors influence cooperative performance and farmer outcomes.

The reason for purchasing this service is to generate actionable insights that enable stakeholders, including farmers, cooperatives, policymakers, and certification bodies, to enhance the effectiveness and sustainability of cocoa production systems in Ghana and Côte d’Ivoire. Specifically, the study aims to assess the readiness of cocoa cooperatives for ARS1000 certification, evaluate cooperative governance and member engagement, and investigate household-level investment strategies, including investments in sustainable agricultural practices or household assets. The ultimate goal is to identify critical barriers and opportunities to strengthen cooperative capacity, improve resource allocation, and reduce the financial and operational burdens of compliance with sustainability standards, thereby contributing to a more sustainable cocoa production system in the region.
title: Assessment of the Performance and Effectiveness of Farmer Cooperatives and Farmer Groups in the Cocoa Sectors of Ghana and Ivory Coast

summary: Supply, Installation and maintenance of a PEM Electrolyser for Hydrogen Production at JRC Ispra
content: Supply, Installation and maintenance of a PEM Electrolyser for Hydrogen Production at JRC Ispra

caName: Supply, Installation and maintenance of a PEM Electrolyser for Hydrogen Production at JRC Ispra
description:
The procurement entails the design, manufacturing, delivery, installation, and commissioning of a Proton
Exchange Membrane (PEM) electrolysis system for hydrogen production at the JRC Ispra site. The core of the system 
is a 50 Nm3/h electrolyser (which must be upgradable to 100 Nm3/h) that delivers hydrogen at an outlet pressure 
of 30 barg. The main equipment will be delivered in a containerized/skid version divided into three specific areas: 
a control panel area with the AC/DC converter, a water purification unit, and an ATEX­classified area containing
the stacks and gas purification treatment. In addition to the containerized unit, the scope of supply includes several 
external components: ­ An MV/LV transformer ­ A thermal management system (dry cooler) ­ A low­pressure hydrogen
storage system consisting of a cylinder rack at 30 bar with a total volume of 5 m3 ­ A gas blender installed on the 
outlet piping after the storage Finally, the procurement includes a comprehensive service package covering the
Factory Acceptance Test (FAT), Site Acceptance Test (SAT), ATEX verification, staff training, two years of spare parts,
and a 3­year maintenance contract. Reason for Purchasing The primary objective of this procurement is to produce 
green hydrogen by harnessing the renewable energy generated from the JRC Ispra site's internal photovoltaic (PV) 
plant. Currently, the site has a 1.35 MWp PV installation, which is planned to be expanded to 2 MWp and eventually
3 MWp in the future. Instead of using battery systems, the JRC intends to use the excess energy from this PV plant 
to power the electrolyser for self­consumption. The hydrogen produced will then be blended into the natural gas 
pipeline (up to a 10% volume blend) to feed the site's co­generators. A dedicated technical sizing analysis concluded 
that a modular 2x250 kW electrolyser is the optimal choice, as it offers the best compromise between the available
PV power, the number of operating hours, and the demand from the co­generators across current and future PV
expansion scenarios
title: Supply, Installation and maintenance of a PEM Electrolyser for Hydrogen Production at JRC Ispra

summary: Evidence reviews for the European Commission Initiatives on cancer screening and care
content: Evidence reviews for the European Commission Initiatives on cancer screening and care

caName: Evidence reviews for the European Commission Initiatives on cancer screening and care
description:
The Disease Prevention Unit of the European Commission’s (EC) Joint Research Centre has been assigned with tasks in the field of cancer prevention and rare diseases that include the development of new European guidelines and quality assurance schemes for the six most prevalent cancer sites (breast, cervical, colorectal, gastric, lung and prostate cancer) representing over 50% of the cancer burden in the European Union. 
The purpose of this procurement procedure is to provide continuity for the collection, analysis and assessment of the underpinning evidence informing the EC initiatives, following a uniform methodological framework.

The purpose of Lot 1 is to perform mapping exercises (e.g. background or scoping reviews, identification of existing guidelines) and evidence reviews, including systematic reviews, synthesis and critically appraisal of evidence, and definition of Evidence to Decision frameworks (EtDs) for the development and update of guideline recommendations, with emphasis, but not exclusively, on breast, colorectal, cervical and lung cancer.

The purpose of Lot 2 is to perform mapping exercises (e.g. background or scoping reviews, identification of existing quality indicators) and evidence reviews, including systematic reviews, synthesis and critically appraisal of evidence, and definition of quality indicators worksheets and requirements for the development and update of quality indicators and requirements with emphasis, but not exclusively, on breast, colorectal, cervical and lung cancer.
title: Evidence reviews for the European Commission Initiatives on cancer screening and care

content: Framework service contract for the collection of meteorological and hydrological in-situ data in support to the Copernicus Emergency Management Service (CEMS) Flood Early Warning Systems

caName: Framework service contract for the collection of meteorological and hydrological in-situ data in support to the Copernicus Emergency Management Service (CEMS) Flood Early Warning Systems
description: The objective of this framework contract is to continue the operation of the CEMS "Hydrological and Meteorological Data Collection Centers" (METEO and HYDRO) in support to the flood early warning and monitoring component of the Copernicus Emergency Management Service (CEMS) which continues as full operational service as defined in article 51(1.b)) of the regulation (EU) 2021/696 of the Union Space Program. Meteorological and hydrological observations constitute a key input for the European and Global Flood Awareness Systems (EFAS and GloFAS) of the Copernicus Emergency Management Service (CEMS). The role of METEO and HYDRO is to collect meteorological (Europe only) and hydrological in-situ observations in near real time (METEO only) as well as for historic periods, quality control and post-process the collected observations, manage and expand the data provider networks and further enhance the data collection.  CEMS implementation is an interservice arrangement between DG JRC, DG DEFIS and DG ECHO (Ares (2021) 2234141). JRC is in charge of preparing and implements the CEMS work programs, manages dedicated budgets and supervises the implementation of service tasks.
title: Framework service contract for the collection of meteorological and hydrological in-situ data in support to the Copernicus Emergency Management Service (CEMS) Flood Early Warning Systems

summary: Enhancing JRC Modelling Tools for Active Mobility Modes and Affordability: Comprehensive Network Characterisation and Transport Poverty Indicators.
content: Enhancing JRC Modelling Tools for Active Mobility Modes and Affordability: Comprehensive Network Characterisation and Transport Poverty Indicators.

caName: Enhancing JRC Modelling Tools for Active Mobility Modes and Affordability: Comprehensive Network Characterisation and Transport Poverty Indicators.
description: The aim of this contract is to strengthen the analytical capabilities of the Joint Research Centre (JRC)'s modelling tools for assessing accessibility to relevant destinations (including employment, healthcare, and education services). This enhancement shall focus on active mobility modes, such as walking and cycling, which are integral to developing sustainable transport systems and which complement public transport models and analyses. By improving the characterisation of active modes and transport networks in the European Union (EU), the project shall enable analyses for specific vulnerable profiles and enhance the accuracy of results, to effectively inform related policy decisions. The contract will have to provide methodological support to the JRC for generating high-resolution (down to a 100-metre-by-100-metre scale) indicators that capture the multidimensional nature of transport poverty. Such indicators shall incorporate affordability considerations and help assess, for instance, vulnerability to increases in fuel prices or public transport fares across the EU. Finally, the contract shall support the development of the Transport Poverty Hub.  External support allows the JRC to draw on the state-of-the-art knowledge of researchers active in the emerging field of characterisation of active mode networks and the integration of affordability into transport poverty indicators. The methodologies, scripts and documentation produced under the contract remain with the JRC so that the resulting capability can be maintained, extended, and re-used in-house.
title: Enhancing JRC Modelling Tools for Active Mobility Modes and Affordability: Comprehensive Network Characterisation and Transport Poverty Indicators.

summary: AI readiness in the EU enlargement region: mapping actors, frameworks and dynamics
content: AI readiness in the EU enlargement region: mapping actors, frameworks and dynamics

caName: AI readiness in the EU enlargement region: mapping actors, frameworks and dynamics
description:
The overall objective of the study is to assess the preparedness of EU enlargement countries for the development and governance of Artificial Intelligence in relation to EU strategic priorities.
Specific objectives include:
-	Assess the readiness of enlargement countries to address opportunities and challenges related to AI development and adoption.
-	Analyse the specificities of the AI industry ecosystem, including companies, universities, and research institutes.
-	Review relevant national policies and strategic initiatives related to AI and digital technologies.
-	Evaluate regulatory preparedness, including the degree of alignment with EU regulatory frameworks.
-	Identify key sectors and fields of application of AI.
-	Provide targeted recommendations for supporting AI ecosystem development and regulatory convergence with the EU.
The contractor will pursue these objectives throughout the entire duration of the contract, ensuring a consistent, systematic, and evidence-based approach to delivering the intended analytical and policy-relevant outputs.
The EU enlargement economies covered by this contract are: Ukraine, Moldova, Türkiye, Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, Kosovo, Albania, North Macedonia.
title: AI readiness in the EU enlargement region: mapping actors, frameworks and dynamics

summary: Sale of 7.7 g of Radium-226  for medical applications
content: Sale of 7.7 g of Radium-226  for medical applications

caName: Sale of 7.7 g of Radium-226  for medical applications
description: The European Commission, Joint Research Centre (JRC) in Karlsruhe (Germany) plans to sell approximately 7.7 grams of Radium-226 (Ra-226), a valuable resource from its our strategic inventory utilised for cutting-edge research and development in nuclear medical applications. This includes applications in the production of Actinium-225 (Ac-225) for the use of targeted alpha therapy. Following a surge of demand for Ac-225, Ra-226 material serves as a crucial source material for producing it as well as other valuable medical radioisotopes, such as Lead-212 (Pb-212). With a growing demand and limited supply for Ra-226, the JRC Karlsruhe wants to contribute to the medical isotope supply chain. The expertise along with the state-of-the-art assets at JRC Karlsruhe, equips it to contribute effectively to this critical field. This sale is meant to bolster the availability of Ra-226 for medical applications and further the advancement of nuclear medicine.

summary: New European Bauhaus Label
content: New European Bauhaus Label

caName: New European Bauhaus Label
description: The Commission Communication on the NEB (COM(2025) 1026) adopted on 16 December 2025 (https://new-european-bauhaus.europa.eu/new-european-bauhaus-vision-implementation_en) announced that the Commission will ‘develop a NEB Label to reward NEB projects and practices and increase their visibility with potential promoters and investors.’ The Commission is now moving forward to the implementation of this action, and intends to develop a NEB Label with the aim to: - Provide visibility and formal recognition to projects in the built environment that successfully embody the values and principles of the New European Bauhaus. - Establish a common and evidence-based European reference framework for high-quality, sustainable, inclusive and beautiful NEB projects, promoting a shared understanding of what the NEB represents in practice. - Support NEB projects and initiatives to access the market and investment/funding opportunities, also by reinforcing the credibility of the NEB aligned projects among public authorities, practitioners, investors and citizens. The ultimate objective of the procurement is the delivery of an eligibility framework, an assessment methodology and scoring system underpinning a NEB Label, as well as to carry out the testing and validation of the abovementioned deliverables. The methodology should build, to the greatest extent possible, on criteria already developed through existing NEB tools and initiatives, as well as on established recognition schemes such as the NEB Prizes. These criteria should be reviewed, harmonised and adapted to the specific objectives of the Label, while introducing new criteria where necessary to address aspects not yet covered.
title: New European Bauhaus Label

summary: Clean Energy in the EU Enlargement Region – An Overview of Players, Strategies and Trends
content: Clean Energy in the EU Enlargement Region – An Overview of Players, Strategies and Trends

caName: Clean Energy in the EU Enlargement Region – An Overview of Players, Strategies and Trends
description:
The overall objective of this contract is to assess the preparedness of EU Enlargement countries (Ukraine, Moldova, Türkiye, Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, Kosovo, Albania and North Macedonia) for the development and governance of clean energy solutions in line with EU strategic priorities such as the European Green Deal, Fit for 55 and REPowerEU.
Specific objectives include:
◦	Readiness assessment – Evaluate how well enlargement countries can seize opportunities and address challenges linked to clean energy deployment and decarbonisation. 
◦	Ecosystem analysis – Map the specificities of the clean energy industry ecosystem, covering companies, universities, research institutes and innovation hubs that are active in renewables, energy storage, smart grid and related technologies. 
◦	Policy and strategic review – Examine national policies, roadmaps and strategic initiatives that promote the clean energy transition and the integration of renewable resources into the energy system.
◦	Regulatory preparedness – Analyse the degree of alignment with EU regulatory frameworks (Renewable Energy Directive, EU Taxonomy, Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism, etc.) and identify gaps. 
◦	Sectoral identification – Pinpoint the key sectors and application fields where clean energy technologies (i.e. solar, wind, hydro, biomass, hydrogen, storage, demand side management) have the greatest potential impact. 
◦	Recommendations – Deliver targeted, evidence-based recommendations to strengthen clean energy network development and promote regulatory convergence with the EU.
The contractor will pursue these objectives throughout the contract period, ensuring a consistent, systematic and evidence-based approach to producing the required analytical and policy relevant outputs.
title: Clean Energy in the EU Enlargement Region – An Overview of Players, Strategies and Trends

summary: EU-wide Monitoring Study on End of Waste (EoW) Criteria and Market Impacts for Iron, Steel, Aluminium and Copper Scrap
content: EU-wide Monitoring Study on End of Waste (EoW) Criteria and Market Impacts for Iron, Steel, Aluminium and Copper Scrap

caName: EU-wide Monitoring Study on End of Waste (EoW) Criteria and Market Impacts for Iron, Steel, Aluminium and Copper Scrap
description:
The overarching goal of this study is to provide an EU-wide assessment of the uptake, implementation/enforcement disparities of EoW criteria for iron, steel, aluminium and copper scrap and the impacts for the EU internal market. Specific objectives of the contract include:
- Update evidence on the uptake of EoW criteria, trade volumes, price differentials and cross‑border movement of compliant versus non‑compliant scrap.
- Identify fragmentation in interpretation, enforcement and verification across Member States, and assess the resulting legal‑certainty and market‑distortion risks.
- Quantify cost‑benefit dynamics for all actors in the metal‑scrap value chain, highlighting distributional impacts and barriers to wider adoption.
- Detect misuse of EoW status for circumvention of waste‑shipment controls and evaluate its implications for domestic recycling capacity and EU strategic raw‑material security.
- Provide improvement options to harmonise EoW criteria implementation, close loopholes and consider the establishment of an EU‑wide EoW monitoring mechanism.
Specialised analytical expertise is essential to deliver the high‑quality, evidence-based analysis required to support forthcoming legislative and strategic actions on the EU raw‑materials agenda and the circular economy.
JRC would like to assess the capability of the market to deliver what is required, and, consequently, the feasibility of the procurement. Therefore, economic operators are invited to participate in a survey at the following link: https://ec.europa.eu/eusurvey/runner/Market-Research_Metal-scrap_EoW_study
title: EU-wide Monitoring Study on End of Waste (EoW) Criteria and Market Impacts for Iron, Steel, Aluminium and Copper Scrap

content: Operational Support to In-Season Crop Monitoring and Yield Forecasting Activities (MARSOP7)

summary: Effectiveness of fiscal incentives on businesses and consumers to adopt circular economy practices (acronym: FISCAL-CE)
content: Effectiveness of fiscal incentives on businesses and consumers to adopt circular economy practices (acronym: FISCAL-CE)

caName: Effectiveness of fiscal incentives on businesses and consumers to adopt circular economy practices (acronym: FISCAL-CE)
description:
The aim of this contract is to address the following central research question: To what extent do fiscal incentives and disincentives (taxes and tax discounts for example) play a role in encouraging businesses and consumers to embrace circular economy practices?
Within this framework, the contractor shall:  
1)	Develop a Comprehensive Database of fiscal incentives affecting circular economy outcomes that have been implemented across European countries over time. These instruments include taxes, charges, subsidies, deposit-refund schemes, Pay-As-You Throw and other economic incentives aimed at influencing production and consumption behaviour, meeting the aims of circular economy. The main focus shall be taxes, using (Milios, 2021) and the Policy INstruments for the Environment - OECD database (Policy INstruments for the Environment - OECD database by OECD - Issuu: https://issuu.com/oecd.publishing/docs/pine_database_brochure) circular economy category for cross-cutting domains and other suitable sources as a guide to define the fiscal instrument types and uses in the EU (MS, regions, and cities)
2)	Further the JRC Concept for Measuring Effectiveness by suggesting suitable and proven methods of analysis such as dynamic modelling (Thombs, et al., 2025) and identifying dependent variables such as CMUR and GHG and other suitable independent variables based on literature review and assessment of existing databases including JRC’s databases. The goal would be to know the availability, quality, location, and accessibility of data on circularity indicators such as waste prevention, reuse, repair, recycling, secondary material use, avoidance of landfill and incineration and resource productivity. 
3)	Conduct Analysis using panel-data and econometric methods to assess the extent to which different instruments (taxes first) contribute to measurable improvements in circularity indicators such as waste prevention, reuse, repair, recycling, secondary material use, avoidance of landfill and incineration and resource productivity. Comparative case studies of MS selected instruments and jurisdictions (can be regions or cities) will complement the quantitative analysis, examining how policy design, implementation, enforcement, and institutional context shape their effectiveness. Other methods may be suggested. 
4)	Propose a method for evaluating combined effects of mixed policy approaches if data availability allows.
5)	Provide feedback that allows JRC to evaluate current landscape and make solid recommendations for “EU-wide” approach (guidelines) to CE taxation and other fiscal incentives. 
Resources:
•	Milios, L. Towards a Circular Economy Taxation Framework: Expectations and Challenges of Implementation. Circ.Econ.Sust. 1, 477–498 (2021). https://doi.org/10.1007/s43615-020-00002-z .
•	Policy INstruments for the Environment - OECD database
Thombs, R.P., Zhang, W., Sovacool, B.K. 2025 Do decarbonization policies work? Evidence from a global meta-analysis - ScienceDirect (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0140988326000241)
title: Effectiveness of fiscal incentives on businesses and consumers to adopt circular economy practices (acronym: FISCAL-CE)

description:

caName: Modelling Pathways for a Sustainable and Agroecological Transition of Food Systems in Africa
description: The aim of this contract is to contribute to a project that models several pathways for a sustainable transition of food systems in three African countries (Senegal, Kenya and Mozambique), supporting the European Commission's Green Agriculture agenda. The contractor will be responsible for fine-tuning scenarios for sustainable transition of food systems, supporting the development of models for agroecological transition at both country and farm levels (including development of local modelers capacity), engaging stakeholders, disseminating and communicating project results, as well as providing management and coordination services. The stakeholder engagement will involve local organizations, including civil society, researchers, and policy makers, as well as regional organizations in Africa, to ensure a comprehensive and inclusive approach. A key dimension of the project is to engage with policy makers from the outset, to ensure a good understanding and uptake of the project's lessons and recommendations, and to facilitate the integration of the project's findings into policy decisions. This contract is necessary to support the project's objectives, which require specialized expertise and services to model sustainable food systems transitions, engage with stakeholders, and effectively manage and coordinate the project's activities, ultimately contributing to the Commission's goal of promoting sustainable agriculture and food systems in Africa.

summary: Supply, Installation and maintenance of a PEM Electrolyser for Hydrogen Production at JRC Ispra
content: Supply, Installation and maintenance of a PEM Electrolyser for Hydrogen Production at JRC Ispra

caName: Supply, Installation and maintenance of a PEM Electrolyser for Hydrogen Production at JRC Ispra
description: The procurement entails the design, manufacturing, delivery, installation, and commissioning of a Proton Exchange Membrane (PEM) electrolysis system for hydrogen production at the JRC Ispra site. The core of the system is a 50 Nm3/h electrolyser (which must be upgradable to 100 Nm3/h) that delivers hydrogen at an outlet pressure of 30 barg. The main equipment will be delivered in a containerized/skid version divided into three specific areas: a control panel area with the AC/DC converter, a water purification unit, and an ATEX-classified area containing the stacks and gas purification treatment. In addition to the containerized unit, the scope of supply includes several external components: - An MV/LV transformer - A thermal management system (dry cooler) - A low-pressure hydrogen storage system consisting of a cylinder rack at 30 bar with a total volume of 5 m3 - A gas blender installed on the outlet piping after the storage Finally, the procurement includes a comprehensive service package covering the Factory Acceptance Test (FAT), Site Acceptance Test (SAT), ATEX verification, staff training, two years of spare parts, and a 3-year maintenance contract. Reason for Purchasing The primary objective of this procurement is to produce green hydrogen by harnessing the renewable energy generated from the JRC Ispra site's internal photovoltaic (PV) plant. Currently, the site has a 1.35 MWp PV installation, which is planned to be expanded to 2 MWp and eventually 3 MWp in the future. Instead of using battery systems, the JRC intends to use the excess energy from this PV plant to power the electrolyser for self-consumption. The hydrogen produced will then be blended into the natural gas pipeline (up to a 10% volume blend) to feed the site's co-generators. A dedicated technical sizing analysis concluded that a modular 2x250 kW electrolyser is the optimal choice, as it offers the best compromise between the available PV power, the number of operating hours, and the demand from the co-generators across current and future PV expansion scenarios.
title: Supply, Installation and maintenance of a PEM Electrolyser for Hydrogen Production at JRC Ispra

content: NL-Petten: Vervanging van de bekledingspanelen van gecorrodeerd staal op de technische vloer op het dak van gebouw 312, met inbegrip van de bijbehorende werkzaamheden en reparaties.

caName: NL-Petten: Vervanging van de bekledingspanelen van gecorrodeerd staal op de technische vloer op het dak van gebouw 312, met inbegrip van de bijbehorende werkzaamheden en reparaties.
description:
De bestaande stalen bekledingspanelen van de technische vloer van gebouw 312 hebben een vergevorderd stadium van corrosie bereikt als gevolg van langdurige blootstelling aan de zeer agressieve kustomgeving. De combinatie van zoute lucht, hoge vochtigheid en door wind aangedreven vocht heeft de materiaaldegradatie aanzienlijk versneld.
Vanuit veiligheidsoogpunt brengt progressieve corrosie de structurele integriteit en bevestigingssystemen van de panelen in gevaar, waardoor het risico op losraken, vallende elementen en binnendringing van water in de interne componenten toeneemt.
Vanuit functioneel oogpunt vermindert de verslechtering het vermogen van de bouwschil om adequate weersbescherming te bieden, wat kan leiden tot verdere schade aan isolatie, onderbouw en interne installaties. 
Vanuit esthetisch en institutioneel oogpunt heeft de zichtbaar aangetaste gevel een negatieve invloed op het algemene uiterlijk van de faciliteit, wat niet strookt met de normen die worden verwacht van een goed onderhouden, langlopend publiek goed.
De voorgestelde vervanging is daarom een noodzakelijke maatregel om de veiligheid te herstellen, de duurzaamheid op lange termijn in een categorie van corrosieve blootstelling aan de kust te waarborgen en de functionele en visuele integriteit van het gebouw te behouden.
title: NL-Petten: Vervanging van de bekledingspanelen van gecorrodeerd staal op de technische vloer op het dak van gebouw 312, met inbegrip van de bijbehorende werkzaamheden en reparaties.

summary: Provision of services to support economic modelling of climate change and energy policies: Modelling of non-CO2 greenhouse gases, air pollutants, and LULUCF offsets
content: Provision of services to support economic modelling of climate change and energy policies: Modelling of non-CO2 greenhouse gases, air pollutants, and LULUCF offsets

caName: Provision of services to support economic modelling of climate change and energy policies: Modelling of non-CO2 greenhouse gases, air pollutants, and LULUCF offsets
description:
The European Green Deal is the roadmap for making the EU’s economy sustainable. It is a set of policy initiatives with the overarching aim of making Europe climate neutral by 2050.
 
The "Economics of Climate Change, Energy and Transport" Unit (JRC.C.6) of the Joint Research Centre supports the European Commission’s European Green Deal by performing economics-based research in several areas related to energy and climate change. This work includes the development of a reference toolset of economic models and the completion of associated research activities to improve the models' reliability and robustness. The JRC.C.6 Unit is based in Seville, Spain.
 
JRC.C.6 is seeking to strengthen its socio-economic research and modelling capabilities by expanding its coverage of modelling areas and by updating and improving its existing models and toolsets.
 
The unit JRC.C.6 maintains, develops and applies a number of quantitative tools to analyse the impact of different policies on the energy demand and supply sectors, as well as tools for macro-economic modelling. This toolset comprises the EU and global partial equilibrium models POTEnCIA and POLES including their corresponding databases (notably JRC-IDEES), and the global general equilibrium model JRC-GEM-E3.

All these tools are able to provide model output in terms of CO2 emissions. The comprehensive modelling of climate change mitigation scenarios requires additional information as regards non-CO2 greenhouse gas emissions as well as on emissions and sinks related to land use, land use change and forestry offsets (LULUCF). Besides, climate action can have important co[1]benefits in terms of reduced emissions of air pollutants and of improved air quality. 

This Framework Contract aims at supporting the operation of the abovementioned set of models by providing the JRC with data, methods and results relevant for the analysis of non-CO2 greenhouse gas emissions, emissions of air pollutants (including air quality impacts), and LULUCF offsets.
title: Provision of services to support economic modelling of climate change and energy policies: Modelling of non-CO2 greenhouse gases, air pollutants, and LULUCF offsets

summary: Assessment of the Performance and Effectiveness of Farmer Cooperatives and Farmer Groups in the Cocoa Sectors of Ghana and Cote d’Ivoire
content: Assessment of the Performance and Effectiveness of Farmer Cooperatives and Farmer Groups in the Cocoa Sectors of Ghana and Cote d’Ivoire

caName: Assessment of the Performance and Effectiveness of Farmer Cooperatives and Farmer Groups in the Cocoa Sectors of Ghana and Cote d’Ivoire
description:
The primary objective of this contract is to conduct a comprehensive, large-scale study on the current state and effectiveness of cocoa farmer cooperatives and farmer groups in Ghana and Côte d’Ivoire (incorporating but not limited to cooperative societies in Ghana and COOP CA and COOP simplifié in Côte d’Ivoire). This study will represent the first nationally representative analysis of cocoa cooperatives and farmer groups across the two countries. It will uniquely combine data collection at two levels: (1) the organizational governance and operational management of cooperatives and farmer groups, and (2) the individual farmer members, including their engagement, benefits, and challenges. By integrating insights from behavioural economics, collective action theory, organizational studies, and development economics, the study will adopt an interdisciplinary approach to evaluate how structural, managerial, and behavioural factors influence cooperative performance and farmer outcomes.

The reason for purchasing this service is to generate actionable insights that enable stakeholders, including farmers, cooperatives, policymakers, and certification bodies, to enhance the effectiveness and sustainability of cocoa production systems in Ghana and Côte d’Ivoire. Specifically, the study aims to assess the readiness of cocoa cooperatives for ARS1000 certification, evaluate cooperative governance and member engagement, and investigate household-level investment strategies, including investments in sustainable agricultural practices or household assets. The ultimate goal is to identify critical barriers and opportunities to strengthen cooperative capacity, improve resource allocation, and reduce the financial and operational burdens of compliance with sustainability standards, thereby contributing to a more sustainable cocoa production system in the region.
title: Assessment of the Performance and Effectiveness of Farmer Cooperatives and Farmer Groups in the Cocoa Sectors of Ghana and Cote d’Ivoire

content: EO data products and Near-Real-Time services for HAB-Hub project

caName: EO data products and Near-Real-Time services for HAB-Hub project
description: The HAB-Hub Pilot project (PP33) aims to assess, improve and scale-up existing Earth Observation (EO) data, services and methodologies to detect in near-real-time (NRT) harmful algal bloom (HAB) events in European waters. The project will evaluate at a pan European scale the performance of methods and products already applied in existing operational EU services as well as phytoplankton bloom monitoring systems worldwide. The assessment will be carried out in retrospective mode, testing the capacity of alternative systems of successfully detecting and documenting past bloom events. The best performing system should then be evaluated during a NRT 6-month experiment. The purpose of this forthcoming contract is to provide the EO data needed for the assessment in retrospective mode, to develop a web-based platform (or dashboard) that will host the NRT experiment and will display and disseminate its results, and to run the NRT experiment with the appropriate data.

description:
EUROMOD is the tax-benefit microsimulation model of the European Union (EU), which covers in a consistent manner the tax-benefit systems of all EU Member States. The model allows to study the effects of taxes and social benefits on household incomes and work incentives for the population of each country and for the EU as a whole. EUROMOD is unique in its area as it features great flexibility in the scope of its simulation and ensures cross-country consistency of the modelling approach and comparability of the results. The model is widely used by the Commission services in the European Semester context and other EU policy initiatives. Additionally, the model represents a valuable research infrastructure for the academic community in the area of fiscal policy analysis, with highly cited research conducted using EUROMOD being published in top journals.
The contracts are intended to provide the Commission with services that support the development and update of the microsimulation model EUROMOD for 26 EU country-specific modules. The modules are as follows:

Das Angebot umfasst die Erstellung von genehmigungsfähigen Vorprüfunterlagen, die Unterstützung des Genehmigungsverfahrens, die Erstellung der Ausschreibungsunterlagen und die Unterstützung bei der Vergabe für den Bau und die Inbetriebnahme des Spaltstofflager Flügel-M des JRC Karlsruhe. Auf Basis einer vorhandenen Konzeptplanung sind folgende Unterlagen und Nachweise zu erbringen: 
a) die Entwurfsplanung mit den notwendigen Systembeschreibungen, Auslegungsberechnungen (Wärmeabfuhrrechnungen, Abschirmrechnungen, Kritikalitätsrechnungen und Standsicherheitsnachweisen nach KTA 2201), Pläne und Zeichnungen sowie die sicherheitstechnischen Nachweise zur sicheren Lagerung und Handhabung (Einrichtungen zum Transport von und zum Lager sowie Be- und Entladung des Lagers) entsprechend der in der Genehmigung aufgeführten Spaltstoffmengen des Flügel M, 
b) die Erstellung der VPU auf Basis der Entwurfsplanung und die Unterstützung des Genehmigungsprozesses bis zum Abschluss des Genehmigungsprozesses,
c) die Erstellung der Fertigungsunterlagen, 
d) die Erstellung der Ausschreibungsunterlagen zur Umsetzung und Unterstützung bei der Vergabe.
title: Erstellung von Vorprüfunterlagen zur Genehmigung und Errichtung eines Spaltstofflagers im Laborflügel M

content: Framework service contract for operating the "Hydrological Forecast Centre - Analytics and Dissemination" in support to the Copernicus Emergency Management Service (CEMS) Flood Early Warning Systems

caName: Framework service contract for operating the "Hydrological Forecast Centre - Analytics and Dissemination" in support to the Copernicus Emergency Management Service (CEMS) Flood Early Warning Systems
description: The objective of this framework contract is to operate the CEMS "Hydrological Forecast Centre - Analytics and Dissemination" (DISS) service in support to the flood early warning and monitoring component of the Copernicus Emergency Management Service (CEMS) which continues as full operational service as defined in article 51(1.b)) of the regulation (EU) 2021/696 of the Union Space Program. The role of DISS is to analyse on a daily basis the flood forecasts of EFAS and GloFAS, inform the relevant users and provide an overall user management and support.   The CEMS implementation is an inter-service arrangement between DG JRC, DG DEFIS and DG ECHO. JRC is in charge of preparing and implements CEMS work programs, manages dedicated budgets and supervises the implementation of service tasks.

description:
La presente procedura ha per oggetto l'affidamento dei servizi di trasporto collettivo da e per il Centro Comune di Ricerca (JRC) sito di Ispra. La procedura è divisa in sette lotti, che saranno l'oggetto di sette contratti quadro distinti.
I lotti da 1 a 6 prevedono un servizio di trasporto da e per il JRC mediante percorsi predeterminati, resi noti nella procedura di gara che coprono diverse città della regione, compresa la città di Milano.
Il lotto 7 prevede invece un servizio di trasporto collettivo per percorsi occasionali su richiesta, destinato a coprire principalmente le esigenze di trasporto dei visitatori che si recano nel sito del JRC di Ispra (per conferenze, riunioni, ecc.).
Il servizio di trasporto è fruibile da tutto il personale del JRC e da eventuali altri passeggeri coinvolti nelle attività del sito del JRC. I servizi devono essere forniti 5 giorni alla settimana, con un viaggio di andata e ritorno, che arriva al sito JRC la mattina e ritorna dal sito JRC la sera verso le varie destinazioni predeterminate a seconda delle linee di trasporto.
Il servizio di trasporto passeggeri è necessario in quanto il sito del JRC di Ispra si trova lontano dalle principali reti di trasporto e anche dalle principali città della regione. Per questo motivo il servizio è indispensabile per il JRC e deve essere eseguito senza interruzioni.

content: Provision of Occupational Health, Safety and Enviornmental expertise to JRC Petten

caName: Provision of Occupational Health, Safety and Enviornmental expertise to JRC Petten
description: The Joint Research Centre (JRC) Petten plans to award a Framework Service Contract for the provision of Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) and Environmental Management expertise. summary: NL-Petten: The supply and installation of air handling units, replacing the existing ones in buildings 308 and 309.
content: NL-Petten: The supply and installation of air handling units, replacing the existing ones in buildings 308 and 309.

caName: NL-Petten: The supply and installation of air handling units, replacing the existing ones in buildings 308 and 309.
description:
The European Commission's Joint Research Centre (JRC) in Petten intends to replace the existing Air Handling Units (AHUs) and associated HVAC infrastructure located in buildings 308 and 309. The current ventilation systems are obsolete and have reached the end of their operational lifespan. Furthermore, preliminary technical assessments have indicated that the existing air renewal capacity is insufficient to maintain optimal indoor air quality for the occupants.

To ensure a healthy, safe, and productive working environment, this procurement aims to upgrade the facilities. The primary objective is to improve indoor air quality, while simultaneously improving the overall energy efficiency of the buildings.

The scope of this contract encompasses the supply, installation, and comprehensive commissioning of the new air handling systems and related infrastructure to provide a fully functional delivery. This includes the safe removal and disposal of the existing AHUs, roof support frames, humidification systems, and redundant cabling or piping, ensuring continuous operation of the buildings during the transition. The technical project involves replacing the units with new, highly energy-efficient equipment featuring heat recovery systems. Additionally, the contract covers the complete adaptation of the hydraulic system to operate under a new, lower-temperature regime, the installation of humidification systems, installing structural supports on the roofs, and the execution of all necessary electrical works. Finally, it requires the full integration of the new instrumentation and controls with the existing Siemens Building Management System (BMS), alongside essential auxiliary tasks such as ductwork cleaning.
title: NL-Petten: The supply and installation of air handling units, replacing the existing ones in buildings 308 and 309.

summary: The transformation of EU farms under the AI revolution
content: The transformation of EU farms under the AI revolution

caName: The transformation of EU farms under the AI revolution
description: The aim of the contract is to understand how EU farms may transform over the next 10 to 30 years during the “AI revolution,” with the goal of identifying how AI-driven farms may operate and the potential structural transformations and disruptions in EU agriculture. To achieve this, the study will develop an analytical framework combining farm typologies, AI scenarios, and focus questions to assess how different types of farms may evolve under alternative AI pathways. Representative farm typologies will reflect the diversity of EU farming systems in terms of production orientation, land use, size, labour structure, and resource allocation, while AI scenarios will outline possible technological developments over the next 10–30 years based on literature and expert knowledge. The study will analyse how farms may adapt their management and organisation under each scenario and identify potential transformations and disruptions at the farm level, including changes in land, labour, capital, assets, data, and market integration. The analysis will rely primarily on qualitative methods, drawing on literature and expert input through interviews, focus groups, workshops, and desk research, with validation by stakeholders and domain experts.
title: The transformation of EU farms under the AI revolution

summary: Provision of services to support economic modelling of climate change and energy policies: Modelling of non-CO2 greenhouse gases, air pollutants, and LULUCF offsets
content: Provision of services to support economic modelling of climate change and energy policies: Modelling of non-CO2 greenhouse gases, air pollutants, and LULUCF offsets

caName: Provision of services to support economic modelling of climate change and energy policies: Modelling of non-CO2 greenhouse gases, air pollutants, and LULUCF offsets
description:
The European Green Deal is the roadmap for making the EU’s economy sustainable. It is a set of policy initiatives with the overarching aim of making Europe climate neutral by 2050.
 
The "Economics of Climate Change, Energy and Transport" Unit (JRC.C.6) of the Joint Research Centre supports the European Commission’s European Green Deal by performing economics-based research in several areas related to energy and climate change. This work includes the development of a reference toolset of economic models and the completion of associated research activities to improve the models' reliability and robustness. The JRC.C.6 Unit is based in Seville, Spain.
 
JRC.C.6 is seeking to strengthen its socio-economic research and modelling capabilities by expanding its coverage of modelling areas and by updating and improving its existing models and toolsets.
 
The unit JRC.C.6 maintains, develops and applies a number of quantitative tools to analyse the impact of different policies on the energy demand and supply sectors, as well as tools for macro-economic modelling. This toolset comprises the EU and global partial equilibrium models POTEnCIA and POLES including their corresponding databases (notably JRC-IDEES), and the global general equilibrium model JRC-GEM-E3.

All these tools are able to provide model output in terms of CO2 emissions. The comprehensive modelling of climate change mitigation scenarios requires additional information as regards non-CO2 greenhouse gas emissions as well as on emissions and sinks related to land use, land use change and forestry offsets (LULUCF). Besides, climate action can have important co[1]benefits in terms of reduced emissions of air pollutants and of improved air quality. 

This Framework Contract aims at supporting the operation of the abovementioned set of models by providing the JRC with data, methods and results relevant for the analysis of non-CO2 greenhouse gas emissions, emissions of air pollutants (including air quality impacts), and LULUCF offsets.
title: Provision of services to support economic modelling of climate change and energy policies: Modelling of non-CO2 greenhouse gases, air pollutants, and LULUCF offsets

description: The JRC would like to procure a new gas detection system, consisting of oxygen and hydrogen detectors (approx. 12 oxygen detectors and approx. 4 hydrogen detectors, exact numbers depending on the technology used), and a central control unit, for its High-Pressure Gas Testing Facility (GASTEF) to replace an outdated one. The GASTEF facility is used for the experimental assessment of safety and performance of systems and components under pressurised hydrogen, and the gas detection system has a safety purpose for the facility. summary: TECHNICAL SUPPORT FOR THE DEVELOPMENT AND UPDATE OF EUROMOD – 26 LOTS
content: TECHNICAL SUPPORT FOR THE DEVELOPMENT AND UPDATE OF EUROMOD – 26 LOTS

caName: TECHNICAL SUPPORT FOR THE DEVELOPMENT AND UPDATE OF EUROMOD – 26 LOTS
description:
EUROMOD is the tax-benefit microsimulation model of the European Union (EU), which covers in a consistent manner the tax-benefit systems of all EU Member States. The model allows to study the effects of taxes and social benefits on household incomes and work incentives for the population of each country and for the EU as a whole. EUROMOD is unique in its area as it features great flexibility in the scope of its simulation and ensures cross-country consistency of the modelling approach and comparability of the results. The model is widely used by the Commission services in the European Semester context and other EU policy initiatives. Additionally, the model represents a valuable research infrastructure for the academic community in the area of fiscal policy analysis, with highly cited research conducted using EUROMOD being published in top journals.
The contracts are intended to provide the Commission with services that support the development and update of the microsimulation model EUROMOD for 26 EU country-specific modules. The modules are as follows:
Lot 1: Support to EUROMOD for Austria
Lot 2: Support to EUROMOD for Belgium
Lot 3: Support to EUROMOD for Bulgaria

summary: Supply of Integrated System for Measuring and Communication Analysis of Mono- and Bi-directional Electric Vehicle Charging Processes
content: Supply of Integrated System for Measuring and Communication Analysis of Mono- and Bi-directional Electric Vehicle Charging Processes

caName: Supply of Integrated System for Measuring and Communication Analysis of Mono- and Bi-directional Electric Vehicle Charging Processes
description:
The JRC  needs a new, fully integrated test system for both mono- and bi-directional  electric vehicle (EV) charging. The system must:
a. Support IEC 62196-2 (Type 2 AC) and IEC 62196-3 (CCS Type 2 DC) plugs and allow manual or automated testing based on predefined use-cases.
b. Perform time-synchronous voltage and current measurements and decode communication and power signals, using ISO 15118-20 (and future amendments) as the communication baseline.
c. Simulate both a standard-compliant charging station and a standard-compliant EV, enabling bidirectional interaction with a real counterpart.
d. Include power-rectification and sink racks for tests up to ≤150 kW DC (175 kW 3-phase AC is already available).
e. Provide a backend communication emulator (e.g., OCPP 2.1) to record and analyse its impact on the charging and discharging processes.
The supply will include a two-year warranty and maintenance period, followed by an additional year of maintenance.
title: Supply of Integrated System for Measuring and Communication Analysis of Mono- and Bi-directional Electric Vehicle Charging Processes

description:
Het Gemeenschappelijk Centrum voor Onderzoek (GCO) te Petten heeft behoefte aan een aangaan van een overeenkomst met een partij die ondersteuning biedt bij het onderhoud van de werktuigbouwkundige installaties van het GCO. Tevens dient de toekomstige contractant een werkvoorbereider beschikbaar te stellen die voornamelijk op eigen locatie werkzaam zal zijn ter ondersteuning van de uitvoering van dit contract. Daarnaast kan inzet nodig zijn van een hulpmonteur of een STEK-monteur op de locatie van het GCO. 
Het bestellen en aanleveren van materiaal ten behoeve van het onderhoud, kleine werken en projecten is eveneens onderdeel van het contract.

content: Hiring of vehicles for compliance verification testing

description:
The JRC is involved in the activity of vehicle market surveillance as required by EU Regulation 2018/858, In-Service Conformity testing following Regulation 2028/1832 (and amendments) plus forward looking research activities on vehicle behaviours. To this purpose, the JRC needs to hire vehicles selected on the basis of defined criteria (e.g. risk assessment criteria or substantiated complaints, performance characteristics, advanced features, etc.) that will be subjected to tests to verify the compliance of the vehicles with the applicable environmental performance, safety related requirements or performance features. The tests are in general those prescribed for the type approval of the vehicle and are typically carried out either in dedicated laboratories or, on the road and safety test tracks. The tests are meant to reproduce typical driving conditions so that the vehicles are not abused.

 https://ec.europa.eu/eusurvey/runner/Rental. Please note that responding to this survey is not a prerequisite for submitting an offer should a call be launched.

The current option for the contracting authority, as indicated in point 3.1.8, is to establish a framework contract without reopening competition. However, subject to the outcome of the market survey, the contracting authority may opt for a framework contract with reopening of competition.

summary: Modelling Pathways for a Sustainable and Agroecological Transition of Food Systems in Africa
content: Modelling Pathways for a Sustainable and Agroecological Transition of Food Systems in Africa

caName: Modelling Pathways for a Sustainable and Agroecological Transition of Food Systems in Africa
description: The aim of this contract is to contribute to a project that models several pathways for a sustainable transition of food systems in three African countries (Senegal, Kenya and Mozambique), supporting the European Commission's Green Agriculture agenda. The contractor will be responsible for fine-tuning scenarios for sustainable transition of food systems, supporting the development of models for agroecological transition at both country and farm levels (including development of local modelers capacity), engaging stakeholders, disseminating and communicating project results, as well as providing management and coordination services. The stakeholder engagement will involve local organizations, including civil society, researchers, and policy makers, as well as regional organizations in Africa, to ensure a comprehensive and inclusive approach. A key dimension of the project is to engage with policy makers from the outset, to ensure a good understanding and uptake of the project's lessons and recommendations, and to facilitate the integration of the project's findings into policy decisions. This contract is necessary to support the project's objectives, which require specialized expertise and services to model sustainable food systems transitions, engage with stakeholders, and effectively manage and coordinate the project's activities, ultimately contributing to the Commission's goal of promoting sustainable agriculture and food systems in Africa.
title: Modelling Pathways for a Sustainable and Agroecological Transition of Food Systems in Africa

description: Il Centro comune di ricerca o Centro comune di ricerca (JRC), sito di Ispra, copre un'area di circa 166 ha con 30 km di strade. Le superfici pavimentate (strade, cortili, ecc.) hanno una superficie di circa 300,000 metri quadrati e gli edifici sono circa 300. Gli edifici sviluppano una superficie totale di circa 200,000 metri quadrati. I locali comprendono anche le residenze e i servizi esterni (Nursery, Club House, ecc.) e alcune parti comuni degli edifici ALER in via Esperia, Ispra. Circa 2.000 persone, interne o esterne, sono presenti quotidianamente al JRC di Ispra. Tutti i locali devono essere puliti regolarmente, la raccolta dei rifiuti deve essere garantita allo stesso modo dei roditori e del controllo degli organismi nocivi. Di conseguenza, è necessario un contratto per garantire tale servizio, essenziale per la gestione quotidiana del sito del JRC di Ispra. L'unità R.I.3 sarà responsabile della gestione amministrativa del contratto e del controllo del servizio. Le esigenze sono attualmente soddisfatte mediante il contratto di servizi n. 942530-2022 stipulato con Euro &Promos in vigore dal maggio 2022.

summary: Rechtsberatung bei Bauprojekten des JRC Karlsruhe
content: Rechtsberatung bei Bauprojekten des JRC Karlsruhe

caName: Rechtsberatung bei Bauprojekten des JRC Karlsruhe
description:
Zur Unterstützung der JRC Karlsruhe, nukleares Forschungsinstitut der EC am Standort des KIT Campus Nord, mit atomrechtlicher Genehmigung nach § 9 AtG zum Umgang mit radioaktiven Materialien, wird juristischer Rat in baurechtlichen Fragen benötigt. Dabei kann es sich um allgemeine Fragen bei den Instandsetzungsarbeiten an bestehenden Gebäuden im Hinblick auf die Anforderungen der deutschen Behörden oder um Fragen und Forderungen verschiedener Bieter und/oder Auftragnehmer in der Auftragsabwicklung zu vertraglichen und rechtlichen Aspekten handeln.

Im Zusammenhang mit Neubauprojekten, bei dem die technischen Anlagen ab Ende 2025 eingebaut und im Jahr 2028 in Betrieb genommen werden sollen, wird der Rechtsbeistand beigezogen, um mögliche Ansprüche der Auftragnehmer aus rechtlicher Sicht zu identifizieren, auf Anforderung zu bewerten und das JRC Karlsruhe bei verschiedenen Tätigkeiten zu unterstützen, wie z. B:

•	Beratung zu Strategien zur Schadensminderung
•	Identifizierung potenzieller Ansprüche (im Falle von Verzögerungen, Änderungen, unvorhergesehenen Bedingungen usw. bei der Vertragsausführung) und Analyse von Ursache-Wirkungs-Beziehungen
•	Bewertung von eingereichten Nachtragsforderungen auf vertragsrechtliche Ansprüche

content: NL-Petten: Study on cooling individual and centralized technologies to cover the current and future cooling demand in the residential sector of the EU

caName: NL-Petten: Study on cooling individual and centralized technologies to cover the current and future cooling demand in the residential sector of the EU
description: The study will provide energy modelers and policy makers in the EU with detailed data and projections related to the current and future techno-economic performance of cooling technologies, leading to more accurate models and better-informed policy-making in the field of cooling, thereby supporting the heating and cooling strategy. The study will focus on cooling technologies that are applicable for individual  and centralized cooling in the residential sector. The study aims to provide impartial quantitative information about the current and future operational and economic characteristics of different cooling technologies. This information will cover key parameters necessary for technical and financial assessments of cooling technologies, as well as for systemic modelling activities, including efficiency, capital, and operating costs. The information provided must be representative of the various conditions prevailing in the EU (e.g., climate, prices). This can be achieved by giving differentiated data according to geographical/climatic zones (e.g., Nordic, Mediterranean, Western, and Eastern) or by other means deemed appropriate, such as formulas, graphs, and/or tables.

summary: Consulting services for assessment of opportunities for adoption of Artificial Inteligence based solutions in administrative processes of the Joint Research Centre
content: Consulting services for assessment of opportunities for adoption of Artificial Inteligence based solutions in administrative processes of the Joint Research Centre

caName: Consulting services for assessment of opportunities for adoption of Artificial Inteligence based solutions in administrative processes of the Joint Research Centre
description:
The aim of the contract is to provide the Joint Research Centre of the European Commission with consulting services for the assessment of opportunities for adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) based solutions in administrative processes. 
Specifically, the contract foresees the following four main tasks: 
1) Development of a comprehensive AI assessment methodology.
2) Practical testing across at least one use-case per activity (the identified activities are: Site infrastructure, development, maintenance and operations; Logistics and document management; Health and safety at work; Security; Care for the environment; Social support and wellbeing; Site representation; Other Horizontal processes; Procurement, contracts and finance). 
3) High-level AI tool analysis and recommendations. 
4) Assessment of organizational processes based on the mapping of activities. 

The key features of the requested tasks are:
a) Market-Informed Approach: the expected deliverables must reflect current industry trends where AI adoption in public procurement is accelerating, with careful attention to transparency and responsible implementation as highlighted in recent policy developments. 
b) Comprehensive Deliverable Structure: the four-deliverable framework must ensure practical methodology development, real-world testing, tool analysis, and complete organizational assessment within the 3-month contract duration. 
c) Risk Management Focus: given the evolving nature of AI regulation and implementation challenges, the tasks must include robust risk assessment requirements and legal and ethical compliance frameworks. 
d) Scalable Methodology: the approach must ensure that the developed methodology can be adapted across different public administration contexts while maintaining standardized assessment criteria.
title: Consulting services for assessment of opportunities for adoption of Artificial Inteligence based solutions in administrative processes of the Joint Research Centre

summary: Stability monitoring of GMO CRMs
content: Stability monitoring of GMO CRMs

caName: Stability monitoring of GMO CRMs
description:
In the frame of the post certification monitoring of certified reference materials, measurements are required for the determination of the GMO content in GMO certified reference materials:
On each of the GMO CRMS the following determination shall be performed:
•	4 bottles of the GMO material (1 g) will be provided by JRC Geel.
•	For each bottle, three independent DNA extractions will be performed from three subsamples, for a total of 12 extracts.
•	On each of the extracts, the following experiments must be performed: 
	1 gel electrophoresis to assess the integrity of the DNA. (NB: all the extracts can be run on the same gel).
	1 rt-PCR measurement for the transgene and 1 rt-PCR for the endogene, except for Lot 7, where 3 rt-PCR measurements i.e; 2 for the transgene and 1 for the endogene are needed. All measurements will be performed under repeatability conditions i.e. in one analytical series.
	Gel electrophoresis (as much as necessary) with the rt-PCR results + adequate standards to verify/compare the size of the resulting band.
	Absorbance ratios of 260nm/280nm and 260nm/230nm.
	RNase has to be added during DNA extraction to digest possible RNA in the extract. This is to avoid a RNA band on the gel (low molecular weight).

The materials can be analysed with other materials without impeding the independence of the results for the individual materials.
title: Stability monitoring of GMO CRMs

summary: Electron Backscatter Diffraction detector on the existing scanning electron microscope (SEM) in the MCL laboratory
content: Electron Backscatter Diffraction detector on the existing scanning electron microscope (SEM) in the MCL laboratory

caName: Electron Backscatter Diffraction detector on the existing scanning electron microscope (SEM) in the MCL laboratory
description:
Requests within recent and ongoing projects highlighted the relevance of electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) and transmission Kikuchi diffraction (TKD) beyond anticipated needs: Open Access (JAMMED, CRAFT, 3DPIMEA, CANMECH, NIFEM, SAHARA and CHRONIC), Exploratory Research (ULTIMATE and DICTION), competitive projects (NUCOBAM, INNUMAT), in addition to institutional activities (SMARTI). 
The first reason is the trend towards increased variety in materials investigated prompted by open-access and competitive projects, compared to institutional activities for which the existing SEM and PFIB combination has been configured for, particularly in projects where the synergies with G.I.4 activities are on methodology developments rather than on the case study. The second reason is a growing interest in EBSD and TKD in general, triggered by recent major improvements in detector sensitivity and, specifically within the frame of the present procurement, indexation methods.
The result was/will be the saturation of the availability of the EBSD system on the Plasma focused ion beam - scanning electron microscopy PFIB-SEM. The EBSD detector on the PFIB-SEM is geared towards 3-D imaging and sample preparation for cases where standard polishing and etching methods produce artefacts, which is not needed for most screening analyses. Further, the PFIB-SEM is a heavily used and advanced instrument (often running overnight and during week-ends using automation and further periodic downtimes for maintenance), procured primarily for specific tasks, including micro-fabrication, 3-D imaging, lamella preparation and high-resolution imaging of ion-polished cross-sections. Therefore, screening and specific 2-D high-resolution EBSD measurements block the PFIB-SEM and affect its availability for fulfilling its primary purpose. 
The proposed solution is the procurement and installation of a high-throughput capable EBSD system on the SEM. Benefits are anticipated on several fronts. First, the pressure on the PFIB-SEM for tasks outside its main purpose will be reduced. Second, visiting scientists can operate the SEM after adequate training, which is not feasible with the PFIB-SEM because of its use case at G.I.4 (prototyping and 3-D measurements campaigns over several weeks) and higher complexity and maintenance needs.
title: Electron Backscatter Diffraction detector on the existing scanning electron microscope (SEM) in the MCL laboratory

summary: Mobile 24/7 Outdoor Passive Radio Frequency (RF) - based Counter Unmanned Aircraft System (Counter-UAS)
content: Mobile 24/7 Outdoor Passive Radio Frequency (RF) - based Counter Unmanned Aircraft System (Counter-UAS)

caName: Mobile 24/7 Outdoor Passive Radio Frequency (RF) - based Counter Unmanned Aircraft System (Counter-UAS)
description:
The JRC DRONE project investigates technologies to counter Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS) around critical infrastructure and public spaces. To support this, the project requires a mobile, outdoor-deployable RF-based C-UAS system capable of continuous 24/7 operation. 

This system will be installed for multi-month periods on a tripod (without permanent fixtures), used to collect RF signal data, detect UAS and operators, and assess system performance in live environments. After each deployment phase, it must be easily dismantled and redeployed elsewhere. 

The solution must include transport case, tripod, 25-meter power and Ethernet cables, a web-based user interface, and support for RF signal recording, direction finding, and machine learning-based classification. Free updates of the drone signature library must be included for the lifetime of the product.
title: Mobile 24/7 Outdoor Passive Radio Frequency (RF) - based Counter Unmanned Aircraft System (Counter-UAS)

content: Operational water-surface reflectance factors for above-water radiometry

caName: Operational water-surface reflectance factors for above-water radiometry
description:
The Joint Research Centre (JRC) contributes to validating Copernicus Sentinel-2 and -3 aquatic data products with several autonomous above-water systems, such as those included in the Ocean Colour component of the Aerosol Robotic Network (AERONET-OC; Zibordi et al., 2009, 2022).
The validation of Copernicus Sentinel-2 and -3 data products with AERONET-OC in-situ measurements is crucial for the assessment and eventual minimisation of uncertainties both in satellite data products and in the algorithms applied to their processing, thus ensuring a maximized return of investment for the Copernicus Programme.
The present service request concerns the computation through accurate radiative transfer simulations of operational water-surface reflectance factors for above-water radiometric data obtained with the measurement and data reduction protocols implemented in AERONET-OC.

The aim of this contract is to define and develop the interior design of the building, with a specific focus on offices, collaborative spaces, co-working areas, dining, social spaces, and meeting rooms. Importantly, the interior design project must be fully integrated into the detailed design of the building, under construction, to ensure cohesion between architecture and interior elements. summary: Markets for secondary raw materials: volumes, quality, prices, and likely global suppliers to the EU under given market conditions
content: Markets for secondary raw materials: volumes, quality, prices, and likely global suppliers to the EU under given market conditions

caName: Markets for secondary raw materials: volumes, quality, prices, and likely global suppliers to the EU under given market conditions
description:
The primary objective of this contract is to improve the current knowledge and understanding of secondary material markets, focusing on plastic recyclates, aluminum scrap, steel scrap, copper scrap, paper and cardboard waste, and textile fibres. The expected outcomes are: I) Improved understanding of secondary material markets and II) Quantitative data and information to feed in-house JRC models.
The tasks involve I) Defining the scope of the study, including relevant statistical codes for each material, II) Analyse the current international market situation, including trade volumes, prices, and barriers. III) Describe the current supply situation, including production capabilities and costs for major supplying countries. IV) Identify key drivers of future supply availability and costs and provide a market outlook for each material. 
Economic operators are also invited to participate in the request for information at the following link: https://ec.europa.eu/eusurvey/runner/bd5cba05-1af2-8865-7ff4-93053bf9b793

caName: Passenger transport for JRC-Geel
description: JRC Geel is located 7 km outside Geel centre and is not well connected to the public transport infrastructure. As a result transportation services for its staff and visitors are required. JRC Geel members of staff undertake numerous missions during the year in connection to the business needs of the institute. Additionally there is a large number of visitors visiting the JRC Geel on a regular and non-regular basis. The transport services are mainly provided within the boundaries of the provinces of Antwerpen, Limburg and Vlaams-Brabant (incl. Brussels). Occasionally the services are required outside the areas mentioned above and include transport abroad (for example Germany, the Netherlands) depending on the relevant activities of the JRC Geel. The main destinations are to / from the Brussels airport, to/from Brussels centre and to/from Geel / Mol. Therefore, the JRC Geel has an intention to call upon an external service provider for the transport of staff members and visitors of the JRC Geel by car and minibus. Furthermore, transport of luggage with normal weight and size is also required.

summary: Rechtsberatung bei Bauprojekten
content: Rechtsberatung bei Bauprojekten

caName: Rechtsberatung bei Bauprojekten
description:
Zur Unterstützung der JRC Karlsruhe, nukleares Forschungsinstitut der EC am Standort des KIT Campus Nord, mit atomrechtlicher Genehmigung nach § 9 AtG zum Umgang mit radioaktiven Materialien, wird juristischer Rat in baurechtlichen Fragen benötigt. Dabei kann es sich um allgemeine Fragen bei den Instandsetzungsarbeiten an bestehenden Gebäuden im Hinblick auf die Anforderungen der deutschen Behörden oder um Fragen und Forderungen verschiedener Bieter und/oder Auftragnehmer in der Auftragsabwicklung zu vertraglichen und rechtlichen Aspekten handeln.

Im Zusammenhang mit Neubauprojekten, bei dem die technischen Anlagen ab Ende 2025 eingebaut und im Jahr 2028 in Betrieb genommen werden sollen, wird der Rechtsbeistand beigezogen, um mögliche Ansprüche der Auftragnehmer aus rechtlicher Sicht zu identifizieren, auf Anforderung zu bewerten und das JRC Karlsruhe bei verschiedenen Tätigkeiten zu unterstützen, wie z. B:

•	Beratung zu Strategien zur Schadensminderung
•	Identifizierung potenzieller Ansprüche (im Falle von Verzögerungen, Änderungen, unvorhergesehenen Bedingungen usw. bei der Vertragsausführung) und Analyse von Ursache-Wirkungs-Beziehungen
•	Bewertung von eingereichten Nachtragsforderungen auf vertragsrechtliche Ansprüche
•	Abwehr und Verhandlung etwaiger außergerichtlichen Ansprüche 
•	Prüfung, Vorbereitung und Einreichung von Mängel- und Schadensersatzansprüchen.

Der Berater für Rechtsfragen soll zudem das JRC Karlsruhe unterstützen bei Aufgaben wie z. B:

•	Identifizierung und rechtliche Bewertung potenzieller Ansprüche der Bieter und Vertragspartner 
•	Beantwortung vertragsrechtlicher Fragenstellungen
•	Erstellung von Gutachten und Bewertung rechtlicher Risiken
•	Im Falle von Streitigkeiten: Entwicklung von Strategien zur Streitbeilegung
