content: Risk assessment of organic priority substances contained in sewage sludge and derived mineral-like materials applied on EU agricultural land

caName: Risk assessment of organic priority substances contained in sewage sludge and derived mineral-like materials applied on EU agricultural land
description:
The primary objective of this contract is to assess the environmental and human health risks from selected organic contaminants contained in sewage sludge and derived materials thereof applied on agricultural fields in the EU.
The scope of this work is limited to organic contaminants. A total of 10 organic contaminants shall be assessed, including 7 organic priority substances or substance groups (PAH, PCDD/F+dl-PCB, long-chain PFAS, SCCPs/MCCPs, alkylphenols, PCNs, and phthalate acid esters; as identified in the 2022 JRC study (https://publications.jrc.ec.europa.eu/repository/handle/JRC129690)) as well as three additional compounds of concern to stakeholders (e.g. pharmaceutical residues, surfactants). Other contaminants and compounds of concern contained in sewage sludge, such as metals, biological pathogens, microplastics, and antimicrobial resistance genes fall outside the scope of this study. 
 
Economic operators are also invited to participate in the request for information at the following link: https://ec.europa.eu/eusurvey/runner/09b449a2-346e-aba0-6afc-8e4ed7c7a0a1

summary: HbA1c and HbA0 purified
content: HbA1c and HbA0 purified

caName: HbA1c and HbA0 purified
description:
This procedure concerns the procurement of purified human HbA1C and HbA0 in stabilizing buffer (containing at least 50 mmol/L  MES, 10 mmol/L KCN, 1 or 2 mmol/L Na2EDTA,  pH 6.2, additional additives are allowed to be present as well ), subdivided in aliquots. The objective of the project is the production of candidate certified reference materials (CRM) for HbA0 and HbA1c that will replace the previous CRM ERM-AD500/IFCC. JRC will produce the candidate CRM by mixing solutions of highly purified human HbA1c and HbA0. 

The final material will consist of a set of 6 solutions with different amount-of-substance fractions of HbA1c and it will be evaluated by the IFCC network of HbA1c Reference Method Laboratories. The production of these reference materials is of crucial importance in clinical chemistry, driven by the EU Regulation on in vitro diagnostic medical devices (IVD-MD) (Regulation (EU) 2017/746), which requires traceability of calibrants and control materials.

The EU Ecolabel (EUEL) Regulation EC 66/2010  provides a framework for the setting of voluntary ecological criteria for defined product groups with the aim of reducing the negative environmental impacts on the environment, health, climate and natural resources, associated with the production and consumption of those same products.
The requested work seeks for the support in the revision of the EUEL for indoor cleaning services established by Commission Decision (EU) 2018/680 of 2 May 2018. summary: Betreuung der Überwachungszentrale und der technischen Anlagen des JRC Karlsruhe im 24- Stunden-Schichtbetrieb
content: Betreuung der Überwachungszentrale und der technischen Anlagen des JRC Karlsruhe im 24- Stunden-Schichtbetrieb

caName: Betreuung der Überwachungszentrale und der technischen Anlagen des JRC Karlsruhe im 24- Stunden-Schichtbetrieb
description:
Mittels Überwachungs- und Kontrollmaßnahmen sollen die Gebäude und betriebstechnischen Anlagen, Labore und wissenschaftlichen Einrichtungen in einem sicheren Zustand innerhalb und außerhalb der Regelarbeitszeit gehalten werden. Zur Durchführung dieser Aufgaben ist eine ständige Besetzung der Überwachungszentrale (ÜWZ) zu gewährleisten. Dies ist dem Arbeitsbereich der technischen Infrastruktur zugeordnet.

Die Tätigkeiten der vom AN einzusetzenden Mitarbeitern sind neben der permanenten Besetzung der ÜWZ, während der Regelarbeitszeit, die praktische Unterstützung der Arbeitsgruppen in der technischen Infrastruktur bei Reparatur- und Instandsetzungsarbeiten sowie wiederkehrenden Prüfungen, teilweise mit externen Sachverständigen. Außerhalb der Regelarbeitszeit, sind die Durchführung von Rundgängen sowie Interventionen bei Störungen und Alarmen Schwerpunkte der Tätigkeiten. 

Das Angebot umfasst die Durchführung eines Schichtdienstes mit je einer 8-stündigen Früh-, Mittel- und Spätschicht sowie zusätzlich einer ÜWZ-(Tag)Schicht an allen Arbeitstagen. Jeder Schichtdienst ist mit einer Fachkraft im Bereich Elektrotechnik (Energietechnik/Fernmeldetechnik/Mess- und Regeltechnik/Mechatronik) sowie einer Fachkraft im Bereich Mechanik (Gas-, Wasser-, Heizungs- und Klimatechnik) zu besetzen. 

Die Koordination seitens des Auftragnehmers wird durch zwei Fachkräfte, ebenfalls in den Bereichen Elektrotechnik sowie Mechanik, an allen Werktagen durchgeführt und dient als Ansprechpartner für den Koordinator des JRC Karlsruhe. 

Für die vorgesehenen Mitarbeiter müssen bereits für die Bewerbung Nachweise der Qualifikation eingereicht werden.
title: Betreuung der Überwachungszentrale und der technischen Anlagen des JRC Karlsruhe im 24- Stunden-Schichtbetrieb

summary: Unleashing the Science, Technology and Innovation (STI) transformative potential of Regional Centres of Excellence (RCoE)
content: Unleashing the Science, Technology and Innovation (STI) transformative potential of Regional Centres of Excellence (RCoE)

caName: Unleashing the Science, Technology and Innovation (STI) transformative potential of Regional Centres of Excellence (RCoE)
description:
The objective of this contract is to build and improve the capacities of Regional Centres of Excellence (RCoE) to understand the systemic impacts of Science, Technology and Innovation (STI) investments related to agri-food, water, biodiversity and forests and beyond. To do so, this work will develop and implement a methodology for a systemic place-based approach to mobilising STI for green transition. The methodology will:  
•	Support the identification, assessment and prioritisation of STI investments, taking into account cross-sectoral impacts, synergies, and trade-offs;
•	Generate and disseminate guidance for interdisciplinary and cross-sectoral coordination of RCoEs for research and innovation on green transition. 
The approach will complement and reinforce existing integrated approaches to sustainable resource management in the identified RCoEs within selected African countries. The focus will also be on integrating scientific evidence and participatory approaches in designing and assessing policy strategies and projects.

summary: Data collection, validation & harmonisation for the EU Industrial R&D Investment Scoreboards 2025-2028
content: Data collection, validation & harmonisation for the EU Industrial R&D Investment Scoreboards 2025-2028

caName: Data collection, validation & harmonisation for the EU Industrial R&D Investment Scoreboards 2025-2028
description: Since 2004, the Commission has produced the EU Industrial R&D Investment Scoreboards to analyse corporate R&D investment data and the positioning of EU-based companies compared to their global peers. The publication of the Scoreboard in December each year intends to raise awareness of the importance of R&D for businesses and to encourage firms to disclose information about their R&D investments and other intangible assets, provide economic analyses and inspire policy recommendations for Europe. The data for the Scoreboard come from companies’ publicly available audited accounts. The main objective of this framework contract is data collection and validation for the EU Industrial R&D Investment Scoreboards 2025-28. The work shall be organised in annual cycles with regard to publication of the report each December. The approach is that, based on data provided by the Commission, the financial reports of up to 4000 firms shall be retrieved and several indicators should be gathered and validated for eligibility and accuracy. Moreover, this work involves cross-checking the data to establish a coherent and comprehensive final dataset, including occasional additional verifications after publication of the data in the Scoreboard report.
title: Data collection, validation & harmonisation for the EU Industrial R&D Investment Scoreboards 2025-2028

summary: EU Ecolabel criteria revision for Tourist Accommodation Services
content: EU Ecolabel criteria revision for Tourist Accommodation Services

caName: EU Ecolabel criteria revision for Tourist Accommodation Services
description:
The aim of the contract is to provide the Commission with services that support the revision of EU Ecolabel criteria for Tourist Accommodation Services.  
The EU Ecolabel (EUEL) Regulation EC 66/2010  provides a framework for the setting of voluntary ecological criteria for defined product groups with the aim of reducing the negative environmental impacts on the environment, health, climate and natural resources, associated with the production and consumption of those same products.
The requested work seeks for the support in the revision of the EUEL for tourist accommodation established by Commission Decision (EU) 2017/175 of 25 January 2017. 
The Contractor must provide background analysis and an explanation of the methodology employed, and provide robust answers to the following key research questions: 
The Contractor will generate environmental, technical and economic data and scientific evidence as needed for the EU ecolabel revision process. 

The Contractor shall give particular relevance in its analysis to the following issues: 
a) EEA market data for the Tourism sector, including volumes and turnover; 
b) Estimates of the current distribution of product models on the market; whenever possible, information on future trends should also be collected including estimation of the potential uptake of EU Ecolabel Tourist Accommodation services. 
c) The identification of the most relevant environmental impacts will be carried out by looking at existing scientific evidence, namely the Product Environmental Footprint Category Rules (PEFCRs) that is currently being developed. 
d) EU Ecolabel criteria shall also take into account and harmonise as much as possible with existing criteria developed by officially recognised ecolabelling schemes in Member States (art. 11.2 of the EU Ecolabel Regulation). 
e) Development of social and ethical criteria (when relevant and possible). 
f) Estimation of the costs of the tests required to carry out for the verification of the EU Ecolabel requirements.
title: EU Ecolabel criteria revision for Tourist Accommodation Services

description:
Oggetto del bando di gara è "Esecuzione delle attività di controllo previste nel Piano di Manutenzione dell’opera parti edili dell’edificio 100 e 101". La prima fase dell’appalto consta nell’ingegnerizzazione del processo: trasformare il piano di manutenzione in procedure operative di controllo. La seconda fase consta nell’esecuzione di tutti i controlli previsti dal piano di manutenzione seguendo le procedure operative precedentemente approvate dalla committenza. 
Nella prima fase si richiede di analizzare il piano di manutenzione dell’opera parti edili e di realizzare una strategia esecutiva che ottimizzi l’attività di controllo e la successiva registrazione dei dati. Nella seconda fase, seguendo la strategia di cui sopra, si dovranno eseguire e registrare i controlli come previsto dal piano di manutenzione. Il personale del JRC supporterà il tecnico del contraente al fine di fornire il necessario supporto operativo (non sono richieste attività manuali). E’ richiesta esperienza nella creazione di procedure e strategie per la manutenzione programmata.
Le attività ed i controlli previsti dovranno effettuarsi effettuati una sola volta. 
Al fine di comprendere meglio gli aspetti operativi, una sessione on line, aperta esclusivamente ai potenziali offerenti che si sono registrati sul sito di F&T (indicato in questa pagina) , e un sopralluogo sul sito sono previste dopo la pubblicazione dei documenti di gara.

summary: Data collection, validation & harmonisation for the EU Industrial R&D Investment Scoreboards
content: Data collection, validation & harmonisation for the EU Industrial R&D Investment Scoreboards

caName: Data collection, validation & harmonisation for the EU Industrial R&D Investment Scoreboards
description: Since 2004, the Commission has produced the EU Industrial R&D Investment Scoreboards to analyse corporate R&D investment data and the positioning of EU-based companies compared to their global peers. The publication of the Scoreboard in December each year intends to raise awareness of the importance of R&D for businesses and to encourage firms to disclose information about their R&D investments and other intangible assets, provide economic analyses and inspire policy recommendations for Europe. The data for the Scoreboard come from companies’ publicly available audited accounts. The main objective of this framework contract is data collection and validation for the EU Industrial R&D Investment Scoreboards 2025-28. The work shall be organised in annual cycles with regard to publication of the report each December. The approach is that, based on data provided by the Commission, the financial reports of up to 4000 firms shall be retrieved and several indicators should be gathered and validated for eligibility and accuracy. Moreover, this work involves cross-checking the data to establish a coherent and comprehensive final dataset, including occasional additional verifications after publication of the data in the Scoreboard report.
title: Data collection, validation & harmonisation for the EU Industrial R&D Investment Scoreboards

summary: Betreuung der Überwachungszentrale und der technischen Anlagen des JRC Karlsruhe im 24- Stunden-Schichtbetrieb
content: Betreuung der Überwachungszentrale und der technischen Anlagen des JRC Karlsruhe im 24- Stunden-Schichtbetrieb

caName: Betreuung der Überwachungszentrale und der technischen Anlagen des JRC Karlsruhe im 24- Stunden-Schichtbetrieb
description:
Mittels Überwachungs- und Kontrollmaßnahmen sollen die Gebäude und betriebstechnischen Anlagen, Labore und wissenschaftlichen Einrichtungen in einem sicheren Zustand innerhalb und außerhalb der Regelarbeitszeit gehalten werden. Zur Durchführung dieser Aufgaben ist eine ständige Besetzung der Überwachungszentrale (ÜWZ) zu gewährleisten. Dies ist dem Arbeitsbereich der technischen Infrastruktur zugeordnet.

Die Tätigkeiten der vom AN einzusetzenden Mitarbeitern sind neben der permanenten Besetzung der ÜWZ, während der Regelarbeitszeit, die praktische Unterstützung der Arbeitsgruppen in der technischen Infrastruktur bei Reparatur- und Instandsetzungsarbeiten sowie wiederkehrenden Prüfungen, teilweise mit externen Sachverständigen. Außerhalb der Regelarbeitszeit, sind die Durchführung von Rundgängen sowie Interventionen bei Störungen und Alarmen Schwerpunkte der Tätigkeiten. 

Das Angebot umfasst die Durchführung eines Schichtdienstes mit je einer 8-stündigen Früh-, Mittel- und Spätschicht sowie zusätzlich einer ÜWZ-(Tag)Schicht an allen Arbeitstagen. Jeder Schichtdienst ist mit einer Fachkraft im Bereich Elektrotechnik (Energietechnik/Fernmeldetechnik/Mess- und Regeltechnik/Mechatronik) sowie einer Fachkraft im Bereich Mechanik (Gas-, Wasser-, Heizungs- und Klimatechnik) zu besetzen. 

Die Koordination seitens des Auftragnehmers wird durch zwei Fachkräfte, ebenfalls in den Bereichen Elektrotechnik sowie Mechanik, an allen Werktagen durchgeführt und dient als Ansprechpartner für den Koordinator des JRC Karlsruhe. 

Für die vorgesehenen Mitarbeiter müssen bereits für die Bewerbung Nachweise der Qualifikation eingereicht werden.

content: Crime Scene to Court Room: Strengthening outcomes of nuclear forensics in prosecution

caName: Crime Scene to Court Room: Strengthening outcomes of nuclear forensics in prosecution
description:
The JRC is planning to issue a tender aimed at strengthening the outcomes of nuclear forensics in prosecution. The scope of the work involves assisting the JRC in determining how nuclear forensic findings can be utilized in court proceedings and how expert witnesses presenting the evidence are accepted across EU Member States. Additionally, the task includes developing guidance for prosecutors on the specific aspects of nuclear forensics. The tender also seeks to exploit the use of traditional forensic evidence collected from radioactively contaminated items and to create training exercises for law enforcement that merge traditional and nuclear forensic examinations.

The successful tenderer shall work in collaboration with the JRC and a working group, to be established, consisting of lawyers and scientists from EU Member States. The tenderer should possess expertise in radiological crime scene management, nuclear forensic science, and have experience working with law enforcement.

caName: NL-Petten: Supply test machines for small size test pieces (small punch) in the nuclear fields and related services of maintenance.
description: Framework Supply Contract for the procurement of creep test machines and related services to support testing materials in inert environment (preferentially Argon) using small size test pieces under combination of various combinations of load types in the nuclear field. The main target application is Small Punch creep testing (according to EN 10371:2021 standard), but it is not limited to this. The target temperature range is estimated up to 800 or 900 degrees Centigrade. This procurement includes provisions for preventative and corrective maintenance, calibration services and spare parts and similar as a part of supply channel mode catalogue. The new creep test machines shall assure good control, quality of results, operational safety and efficiency.

summary: Durchführung von Objektsicherungsaufgaben im JRC Karlsruhe
content: Durchführung von Objektsicherungsaufgaben im JRC Karlsruhe

caName: Durchführung von Objektsicherungsaufgaben im JRC Karlsruhe
description:
Das JRC Karlsruhe ist einer der sechs wissenschaftlichen Standorte der Gemeinsamen Forschungsstelle der Europäischen Kommission (Joint Research Centre, JRC) und ist der Hauptsitz der wissenschaftlichen Direktion für nukleare Überwachung und Sicherheit. Es befindet sich auf dem Campus Nord des Karlsruher Instituts für Technologie (KIT) in Karlsruhe, Deutschland.
Im Rahmen des nuklearen Arbeitsprogramms des JRCs widmet sich der JRC-Standort Karlsruhe der nuklearen Überwachung und Sicherheit, um die wissenschaftlichen Grundlagen für den Schutz des europäischen Bürgers vor den Risiken zu schaffen, die mit dem Umgang und der Lagerung hochradioaktiver Stoffe einhergehen.
Ziel dieser Ausschreibung ist die Erbringung von Objektsicherungsaufgaben an dem JRC Standort in Karlsruhe.
Die Aufgaben richten sich nach den geltenden Vorschriften und Vorgaben sowohl auf europäischer (BESCHLUSS (EU, Euratom) 2015/443 DER KOMMISSION vom 13. März 2015 über Sicherheit in der Kommission) wie auf nationaler Ebene (Anforderungen an den Objektsicherungsdienst und an Objektsicherungsbeauftragte in kerntechnischen Anlagen und Einrichtungen der Sicherungskategorie I).
title: Durchführung von Objektsicherungsaufgaben im JRC Karlsruhe

summary: Sale of 7.7 g of Radium-226 for medical applications
content: Sale of 7.7 g of Radium-226 for medical applications

caName: Sale of 7.7 g of Radium-226  for medical applications
description: The European Commission, Joint Research Centre (JRC) in Karlsruhe (Germany) plans to sell approximately 7.7 grams of Radium-226 (Ra-226), a valuable resource from its our strategic inventory utilised for cutting-edge research and development in nuclear medical applications. This includes applications in the production of Actinium-225 (Ac-225) for the use of targeted alpha therapy. Following a surge of demand for Ac-225, Ra-226 material serves as a crucial source material for producing it as well as other valuable medical radioisotopes, such as Lead-212 (Pb-212). With a growing demand and limited supply for Ra-226, the JRC Karlsruhe wants to contribute to the medical isotope supply chain. The expertise along with the state-of-the-art assets at JRC Karlsruhe, equips it to contribute effectively to this critical field. This sale is meant to bolster the availability of Ra-226 for medical applications and further the advancement of nuclear medicine.
title: Sale of 7.7 g of Radium-226  for medical applications

content: NEB Innovative Funding Advisory Hub

caName: NEB Innovative Funding Advisory Hub
description: The European Commission, in line with the New European Bauhaus (NEB) initiative, aims to create an interactive IT platform called the ‘NEB Funding Hub’. This platform will facilitate the matchmaking of small-scale projects that align with the core NEB values (sustainability, inclusion, and quality of experience) with appropriate funding sources, including public and private financiers, as well as crowdfunding entities.  The platform will support the identification, ranking, and financing of NEB-related projects with a funding requirement of up to an estimative value of EUR 100,000. The overarching goal of the assignment is to develop, launch, and maintain the NEB Funding Hub - an interactive online platform that brings together small NEB projects and funding providers (both philanthropic and other public/private financial entities). The platform aims to match small but high-potential NEB projects with funding opportunities through a tailored methodology for project matchmaking.

summary: Production Al-Co foils and wires
content: Production Al-Co foils and wires

caName: Production Al-Co foils and wires
description:
The JRC wants to purchase foils and wires of two Al-Co alloys with different composition. One alloy should be Al - 0.1 % Co, the other Al - 1 % Co (both m/m). They will be made from high-purity Al and high-purity Co, both provided by the JRC.

The materials will be used as a basis for certified reference materials (CRMs) that serve as flux monitors in nuclear reactors. Typical users use 1-5 mg per use. To fulfil their role, it is important that
•	the material is homogeneous ideally on a 1 mg level, meaning that the standard deviation of mass fractions of Co in various 1-mg portions is ideally below 1 %;
•	the material is not contaminated by other metals during processing. Especially contamination by Cu, Fe, Ni and Mn should be avoided and ideally, the final mass fractions of Ni, Cu and Fe should be below 2 mg/kg

This call is also open to candidates located in a country which is part of the" Government Procurement Agreement" (GPA) .
title: Production Al-Co foils and wires

summary: Automated DNA and RNA extraction platform using the magnetic bead technology
content: Automated DNA and RNA extraction platform using the magnetic bead technology

caName: Automated DNA and RNA extraction platform using the magnetic bead technology
description: An automated DNA/RNA extraction system, based on the use of the magnetic bead technology, would allow to increase the speed and throughput capacity of the lab, but also, and more importantly, to improve the consistency of the extraction of the nucleic acids, increasing precision and reducing variability and pipetting errors. Another important aspect is the minimal risk of cross-contamination. The laboratory will also have the magnetic bead technology as an additional procedure to be able to compare with the currently implemented manual and kit-based DNA extraction methods based on DNA purification using columns. Performing DNA extraction of all the samples to be analysed during homogeneity studies of proficiency test materials will also be advantageous for ensuring the repeatability conditions of such experiments.
title: Automated DNA and RNA extraction platform using the magnetic bead technology

description: The survey aims to gain insights into the functioning of the EU vehicle repair and maintenance services, including the spare parts distribution market, as well as the role of vehicle data and the uptake of connected vehicles in the repair market outlook. The survey will provide evidence and information relevant to a study carried out by JRC in order to support the evaluation of the functioning of the Motor Vehicle Block Exemption Regulation (EU) No 461/2010 ("MVBER"). This evaluation must be carried out by the Commission as part of the review process of the MVBER. This exercise is led by DG COMP, and the study is part of an AA signed between DG COMP and JRC in order to provided technical and economic analysis of the trends underpinning recent developments in the vehicle repair and maintenance services market.

caName: Esecuzione delle attività di controllo prescritte nel piano di manutenzione (opere di genio civile). Edificio 100-101.
description:
Oggetto del bando di gara è "Esecuzione delle attività di controllo previste nel Piano di Manutenzione dell’opera parti edili dell’edificio 100 e 101".
La prima fase dell’appalto consta nell’ingegnerizzazione del processo: trasformare il piano di manutenzione in procedure operative di controllo.
La seconda fase consta nell’esecuzione di tutti i controlli previsti dal piano di manutenzione seguendo le procedure operative precedentemente approvate dalla committenza.
Nella prima fase si richiede di analizzare il piano di manutenzione dell’opera parti edili (allegato nr1) con i relativi commenti ed integrazioni apportati dalla stazione appaltante, e di realizzare una strategia esecutiva che ottimizzi l’attività di controllo e la successiva registrazione dei dati.
La strategia esecutiva dovrà portare alla realizzazione di diversi format quali come minimo:
1) check list dei controlli aggregate per ogni tipologia di locale;
2) cronoprogrammi con relative planimetrie delle aree interessate;
3) format di comunicazione con gli utenti;
4) format documentazione riassuntiva finale.
Nella seconda fase, seguendo la strategia di cui sopra, si dovranno eseguire e registrare i controlli come previsto dal piano di manutenzione. Si richiede di effettuare tutte le attività ed i controlli previsti una volta senza considerare la frequenza riportata nel piano di manutenzione.
Si segnala che sono state apportate modifiche al piano di manutenzione originale, che hanno ridotto quasi a zero gli interventi di ripristino veri e propri, focalizzando l’attenzione sui controlli.
title: Esecuzione delle attività di controllo prescritte nel piano di manutenzione (opere di genio civile). Edificio 100-101.

summary: Accelerator tube section for MONNET
content: Accelerator tube section for MONNET

caName: Accelerator tube section for MONNET
description:
The accelerator tube section is the part of the accelerator that contains a vacuum and houses the particles as they are accelerated. In a tandem accelerator like the Pelletron, this tube spans the entire acceleration region, and its function is to keep the path clear for the ions or particles to travel through.

It consists of a series of electrodes that are spaced along the length of the tube. A strong electric field is applied between the electrodes, which is responsible for accelerating the particles.

The tube is segmented in 15 sections to facilitate the creation of a smooth electric potential gradient for accelerating the charged particles. The accelerator tube operates under a high vacuum to minimize collisions with air molecules that would interfere with the movement of the particles.

This procurement procedure is meant to replace one of the fifteen sections which has been damaged and temporary repaired. A replacement part should be purchased without any delay to avoid a facility shutdown.

Technical description: JRC-Geel accelerator tube section:
1X 2FA059470: GEEL 4UD-4 spark gap arrangement ACCELERATOR TUBE, 21 gap sections, 10/11 layout, N7.25 assembly, with spark gaps.

Government Procurement Agreement (GPA) is applicable to this call.
title: Accelerator tube section for MONNET

summary: Management and storage of custom chemical library
content: Management and storage of custom chemical library

caName: Management and storage of custom chemical library
description:
In order to stimulate the generation of validation data from promising non-animal methods in the area of developmental neurotoxicity (DNT), EURL ECVAM intends to provide a specific set of 96 DNT reference chemicals to method developers who have a keen interest in assessing the performance of their method and further optimising it as necessary, with a view towards its eventual application in regulatory toxicology and chemical safety assessment. 
The required service should be able to source, manage, store, reformat and ship chemicals requested by the in vitro methods laboratory.

The contracting authority will set up a direct contract for management and storage of the DNT custom chemical library. The chemical library will be used for in vitro studies to investigate the toxicity effects in cells, organoids and alive organisms (vertebrate embryos, i.e. zebrafish) and to elucidate the mechanisms of action of the chemical compounds related to developmental neurotoxicity (DNT).

summary: Training on European Sustainable Product Policy
content: Training on European Sustainable Product Policy

caName: Training on European Sustainable Product Policy
description:
The objective of this contract is for the contractor to prepare and execute a training in co-operation with the JRC to increase the participant’s ability to contribute to the JRC scientific research to prepare product specific legislation.
The learning objectives can be separated in 3 blocks:
1.	Policy context: 	
To understand the landscape of European Union environmental product policies (Ecodesign, EU Ecolabel, Green Public Procurement, Green Claims Directive etc), what are the objectives of each instrument, how do they interact with broader policy objectives such as climate policy, circular economy action plan, Zero-pollution, energy policy and others.	
2.	Policy implementation: 	
To understand the process by which the European Commission implements secondary – i.e. product specific – legislation (evidence gathering, market research, better regulation and impact assessment; stakeholder interaction, standardisation, market surveillance etc	
3.	Specific Tools: 	
Get an overview and an understanding of the main tools and models applied in the process (Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) and Life Cycle Costing (LCC), Product Environmental Footprint (PEF) etc)
title: Training on European Sustainable Product Policy

summary: Homogeneity and stability study of two EPS candidate reference materials
content: Homogeneity and stability study of two EPS candidate reference materials

caName: Homogeneity and stability study of two EPS candidate reference materials
description:
Homopgeneity and stability study of the candidate reference material ERM-FC440k.

The concerns the homogeneity and stability studies of EPS plates of a candidate reference material. The plates have a thickness of 35 mm and a thermal conductivity of approximately 32 mW/(m.K). 

Test samples
•	15 plates of dimensions 300 mm x 300 mm x 35 mm
•	15 plates of dimensions of 600 mm x 600 mm x 35 mm
•	15 plates of dimensions of 500 mm x 500 mm x 35 mm cut from the 600 mm x 600 mm x 35 mm

Measurements to be performed on each plate
•	2 determinations of the thermal conductivity at 20 °C including two independent determinations of the thickness

The measurements should be performed in the following order:
•	One measurement of the thermal conductivity on each of the 300 mm x 300 mm x 35 mm; after each plate has been measured once, the second measurement should be performed.
•	One measurement of the thermal conductivity on each of the 600 mm x 600 mm x 35 mm; after each plate has been measured once, the second measurement should be performed.
•	Then the 600 mm x 600 mm should be cut into 500 mm x 500 mm. Then One measurement of the thermal conductivity on each plate should be performed; after each plate has been measured once, the second measurement should be performed.
title: Homogeneity and stability study of two EPS candidate reference materials

summary: Radio Frequency (RF) Windows
content: Radio Frequency (RF) Windows

caName: Radio Frequency (RF) Windows
description:
The European Commission’s Joint Research Centre (JRC) located in Geel (Belgium) has the intention to purchase 4 GE-2024-10 RF-windows.
The RF-windows are a critical component in the Geel Electron Linear Accelerator (GELINA) RF-system and for this, extra spare part are needed.
The Geel Electron Linear Accelerator (GELINA) uses high power 2998MHz (S-band) radio frequency (RF) waves to accelerate electrons. The accelerator consists of 3 accelerating sections, and RF waves are generated by 3 klystrons, each with a dedicated modulator to modulate the power. Each klystron provides an RF output via 2 arms, which are connected to a corresponding accelerating section via a system of wave guides that transport the RF waves. The arms at the output of the klystrons can only safely operate under a constant SF6 gas pressure of 3 bars. As the accelerator itself operates under vacuum, windows are needed at some point in the wave guide system to separate the SF6-filled part from the vacuum part. These windows should be able to endure the given RF power, with a limited of RF power in the windows (insertion loss). At the same time, leak rates should be limited, on one hand to guarantee the vacuum inside the accelerator, and on the other hand to limit losses of SF6 to the environment, as this is an extremely strong greenhouse gas (GWP 23500). The RF-windows will serve as spare parts for existing RF-windows, and should therefore comply with the given material specifications, dimensions, flange specifications and cooling interfaces.
title: Radio Frequency (RF) Windows

The objective of this contract is to analyse innovation capabilities and industrial dynamics in European rural areas using econometric, machine learning, and economic complexity methods. The analyses shall address two issues of EU policy-relevance:

summary: Exploratory study to quantify the effect of Start Up relocation abroad
content: Exploratory study to quantify the effect of Start Up relocation abroad

caName: Exploratory study to quantify the effect of Start Up relocation abroad
description: A topic in current discussions of EU competitiveness and innovation capacities is whether the relocation of European and EU-funded innovative startups, particularly those in their scaleup phase, constitutes a net loss to the EU economy and if so, what the policy response to this should be. However, to date, no sufficiently thorough analysis of the relocation phenomenon has been carried out to permit a well-informed policy discussion, in particular relating to quantifications of the positive and negative consequences for the EU economy of startups relocating or partly relocating abroad. The primary objective of the work to be contracted is to provide a comprehensive understanding and empirical assessment of European startup and scaleup migration, regarding the magnitude of relocation, the main factors motivating relocation, and in particular the economic consequences of relocation for both sending and receiving countries. After a review of the most relevant theoretical and empirical literature related to the broader issue, the contractor should compile an exhaustive and detailed firm-level dataset of start-ups and scale-ups that allows identification of firm relocation and that includes relevant economic indicators such as employment, revenue, innovation, or type of relocation. The dataset should cover the most relevant EU-27 and major non-EU economic countries, in particular the United States, and should track firms over time. The contractor should propose an approach to utilize the compiled dataset to conduct in-depth economic, statistical and econometric analyses, examining the magnitude, the motivations and the impacts of European firms' relocating, in particular to the United States. The data analyses should focus on providing a detailed picture of those issues by e.g. comparing migrating/non-migrating firms or assessing the relative importance of various motivations to leave (push and pull factors). The contractor should employ appropriate econometric models to address econometric issues such as sample selection and ensure the robustness of the findings. The contractor should also propose and develop adequate methods/tools that allow to evaluate the overall net impact of startup and scale-up relocation on key variables of interest, such as GDP, employment, innovative capacity or productivity, in Europe.
title: Exploratory study to quantify the effect of Start Up relocation abroad

summary: Capacity building and Experimentation for Innovation for Place-based Transformation
content: Capacity building and Experimentation for Innovation for Place-based Transformation

caName: Capacity building and Experimentation for Innovation for Place-based Transformation
description:
The aim of this contract is to develop and implement an integrated set of activities for equipping European practitioners and policy makers from EU and third countries associated to the programme Horizon Europe with the resources needed to design and implement innovation policies for place-based transformation in the frame of the “Innovation for place based transformation” initiative supported by the European Parliament, with the aim to:

1.	Reinforce territorial capacities for transformative innovation policies by developing and delivering a Capacity Building programme;
2.	Support a place-based transformative innovation policy experimentation arena, where territories can jointly engage into different thematic policy Experimentations Journeys, based around common challenges.

To achieve these objectives the following activities are foreseen in the contract:  
•	To design, develop and deliver a modular training and coaching package (capacity building) targeted to national, local and regional administrations, and their territorial stakeholders (business sector, academia and citizens representatives) from the EU and third countries associated to Horizon Europe. 
•	To design and facilitate transformative innovation expertise and logistic for the support of a minimum 6 Experimentation Journeys (experimentation activities) to be proposed by the Joint Research Centre of the European Commission (EC-JRC) based on the analysis of the received expression of interest by participating territories; 
•	The modular trainings and coaching package and the Experimentation Journeys must be designed to provide a self-standing experience for those taking part in one of the two, and a coordinated experience to those attending both. 
•	In addition, the contractor will undertake the following activities: management  and organisation of events, including logistics, (online, in presence and hybrid), continuous engagement and communication with participants; and coordinating all activities related to Capacity Building and Experimentation Journeys in close collaboration with EC-JRC.
title: Capacity building and Experimentation for Innovation for Place-based Transformation

The NGS is key in the Decommissioning and Waste Management (D&WM) Program.

summary: Data Collection about Behavioural Factors Influencing EU Firms’ Decisions in Undertaking Actions Recommended in Energy Audits Reports, Investing in Energy Efficiency and Saving Energy at the Workplace.
content: Data Collection about Behavioural Factors Influencing EU Firms’ Decisions in Undertaking Actions Recommended in Energy Audits Reports, Investing in Energy Efficiency and Saving Energy at the Workplace.

caName: Data Collection about Behavioural Factors Influencing EU Firms’ Decisions in Undertaking Actions Recommended in Energy Audits Reports, Investing in Energy Efficiency and Saving Energy at the Workplace.
description:
The project aims to evaluate the behavioral factors and misperceptions influencing senior executives' decisions on energy efficiency investments and the adoption of positive energy-consumption practices. By examining these factors, the study seeks to identify barriers that hinder firms' efforts to improve energy efficiency.
 
The goal is to inform policies that encourage more investments in energy efficiency by understanding managers' preferences and decision-making processes. Despite significant national incentives and substantial firm investments in energy efficiency, there remains untapped potential. The study will provide recommendations for designing effective financial programs and information campaigns.
 
To achieve these objectives, the project will conduct a computer-assisted telephone survey of at least 1,000 C-level executives from diverse firms across different EU Member States. This survey will explore how specific behavioral aspects influence managers' decisions regarding energy audit recommendations and investments in energy-efficient technologies or practices.
title: Data Collection about Behavioural Factors Influencing EU Firms’ Decisions in Undertaking Actions Recommended in Energy Audits Reports, Investing in Energy Efficiency and Saving Energy at the Workplace.

summary: Moderation on an online training on participatory processes for local, regional and national public administrations in the EU
content: Moderation on an online training on participatory processes for local, regional and national public administrations in the EU

caName: Moderation on an online training on participatory processes for local, regional and national public administrations in the EU
description:
The JRC and the European Commission's Competence Centre on Participatory and Deliberative Democracy (CC-DEMOS) have built a specific training offer on citizen engagement processes based on co-creation and deliberation for public administrations at local, regional and national level across the EU. The training offer targets three levels of competence (basic, advanced and train-of-trainers) and is available in EN, DA, PL. It includes a full package of resources: for each competence level, it provides a course-book, annotated PowerPoint presentations, roll-out of the course, agenda of the course, self-assessment questionnaire, in-class exercises, and case collection.
In the perspective of upscaling the use of this training package and reaching out to a large number of administrations, JRC is collaborating with the EU Academy to make the offer available on-line and in the three languages. The development of the training offer through pilots in Denmark and Poland has revealed that it is paramount to have moderators with a high level of experience with and expertise on citizen engagement in order to deliver successful training and accommodate specific participants' requests for knowledge and competence. Moreover, experienced practitioners and moderators would ensure that more case studies and examples are brought in that meet the interest of participants and improve the overall quality of the training. Thus, JRC and CC-DEMOS are seeking to procure online moderation of the training on citizen engagement which will consist in combining asynchronous and synchronous sessions and ensure the creation of a community of learners from public administrations and future trainers.
title: Moderation on an online training on participatory processes for local, regional and national public administrations in the EU

summary: Maintenance and support to the project management software tool adopted by Directorate J to manage the Nuclear Decommissioning & Waste Management (NDWM) Programme
content: Maintenance and support to the project management software tool adopted by Directorate J to manage the Nuclear Decommissioning & Waste Management (NDWM) Programme

caName: Maintenance and support to the project management software tool adopted by Directorate J to manage the Nuclear Decommissioning & Waste Management (NDWM) Programme
description:
The "ND Project" is the software platform used by the Nuclear Decommissioning & Waste Management Directorate (NDWMD) to plan, track and report (monitoring of programme progress) the Decommissioning & Waste Management (D&WM) Programme initiated by JRC-Ispra for its obsolete nuclear installations.
This software platform is Microsoft Project Professional 2016 currently installed on Microsoft Azure Cloud SaaS and it uses the Project Management Institute (PMI) approach with relevant indicators selected as the most appropriate tools to monitor the D&WM Programme progress.
The platform is mainly used by the Management Support Sector (MSS) of the NDWMD, Project Leaders of the NDWMD, the Director and the HoU of NDWMD and by external supplier representative partially authorised to consult the platform in a read and write mode for displaying and edit views, including Gantt charts and reports.
This software requires skilled figures with the expertise to supporting, maintaining, continuously enhancing the system so to be kept up to date and to satisfy incoming programme needs. 
In details, the following services are foreseen to be provided:
• Microsoft Office Project consulting: support to project managers, errors checking,
system updates and program customizations, PM consulting;
• Exceptional maintenance activities as backup and recovery activities, software upgrade, etc.;
• Development, upon JRC Ispra request, of “ad hoc” reports, Gantt diagrams, OLAP cubes, custom views, special macros and attributes for projects and resources etc. helpdesk service;
• Periodic newcomers training, refresher's courses and when necessary coaching on new functionalities, including the provision of synthetic operating manuals. Specific courses for for Platform administrators.
The expert assistance for the tool maintenance, upgrade and customisation is provided neither by the JRC Helpdesk nor was found into the existing IT framework contracts.
On top of that the NDWM Directorate is envisioning to migrate from the current tool MS project to Oracle Primavera (in particular to better handle risk management): expertise in both these project management tools and experience in migrating from the first to the latter is high desirable.
title: Maintenance and support to the project management software tool adopted by Directorate J to manage the Nuclear Decommissioning & Waste Management (NDWM) Programme

content: Durchführung von Objektsicherungsaufgaben im JRC Karlsruhe

caName: Durchführung von Objektsicherungsaufgaben im JRC Karlsruhe
description:
Das JRC Karlsruhe ist einer der sechs wissenschaftlichen Standorte der Gemeinsamen Forschungsstelle der Europäischen Kommission (Joint Research Centre, JRC) und ist der Hauptsitz der wissenschaftlichen Direktion für nukleare Überwachung und Sicherheit. Es befindet sich auf dem Campus Nord des Karlsruher Instituts für Technologie (KIT) in Karlsruhe, Deutschland.
Im Rahmen des nuklearen Arbeitsprogramms des JRCs widmet sich der JRC-Standort Karlsruhe der nuklearen Überwachung und Sicherheit, um die wissenschaftlichen Grundlagen für den Schutz des europäischen Bürgers vor den Risiken zu schaffen, die mit dem Umgang und der Lagerung hochradioaktiver Stoffe einhergehen.
Ziel dieser Ausschreibung ist die Erbringung von Objektsicherungsaufgaben an dem JRC Standort in Karlsruhe.
Die Aufgaben richten sich nach den geltenden Vorschriften und Vorgaben sowohl auf europäischer (BESCHLUSS (EU, Euratom) 2015/443 DER KOMMISSION vom 13. März 2015 über Sicherheit in der Kommission) wie auf nationaler Ebene (Anforderungen an den Objektsicherungsdienst und an Objektsicherungsbeauftragte in kerntechnischen Anlagen und Einrichtungen der Sicherungskategorie I).
Der Vertrag umfasst den Zugang zu als „RESTREINT UE/EU RESTRICTED“ eingestuften Verschlusssachen und deren Bearbeitung und/oder Aufbewahrung bzw. Speicherung, worauf der Beschluss (EU, Euratom) 2015/444 und dessen Durchführungsbestimmungen Anwendung finden.
Besondere Sicherheitsanforderungen sind Bestandteil des Vertrags (Geheimschutzklausel im Anhang des Vertrags). Die Vergabe von Unteraufträgen unterliegt der schriftlichen vorherigen Genehmigung durch den öffentlichen Auftraggeber und der Einhaltung aller Sicherheitsvorschriften durch den Unterauftragnehmer und dessen Mitarbeiter.

summary: Study on the adoption of automation technologies and labour market outcomes: the role of key innovators
content: Study on the adoption of automation technologies and labour market outcomes: the role of key innovators

caName: Study on the adoption of automation technologies and labour market outcomes: the role of key innovators
description: The significant progress of AI, impacting an increasing number of companies and employees, has prompted the need to analyse the technological capabilities of top R&D investors in automation technologies. These technologies encompass artificial intelligence, industrial robots, and other Industry 4.0 innovations. The primary objective is to understand the labour market outcomes of these investments. Starting with data provided by the JRC, including Scoreboard company panel data and the JRC-OECD COR&DIP databases, and supplemented with other data sources such as ORBIS, ORBIS IP, PATSTAT, and EU-SILC, the contractor shall: 1) develop indicators for automation technology and the labour market at the firm, geographical, and industry levels; 2)  propose an approach to utilise the harmonised dataset to conduct in-depth statistical and econometric analyses, examining how the adoption of automation technologies influences various labour market outcomes. The analysis should consider factors such as job displacement, wage changes, skill shifts, and the creation of new employment opportunities. The contractor must employ appropriate econometric models to control for confounding variables and ensure the robustness of the findings.

summary: Economic analysis of labour use in agroforestry farming systems in Côte d'Ivoire
content: Economic analysis of labour use in agroforestry farming systems in Côte d'Ivoire

caName: Economic analysis of labour use in agroforestry farming systems in Côte d'Ivoire
description:
The primary aim of this contract is to conduct a high-frequency survey to gather empirical evidence regarding the use of labour, inputs, and the assessment of outputs across different cocoa farming systems in Côte d’Ivoire. The focus of this research project is to meticulously compare agroforestry systems with other farming practices, particularly those that are based on full-sun cultivation,  to evaluate the economic and environmental sustainability of cocoa production. This research initiative is designed to fill the existing knowledge gap about the labour and input use of different cocoa farming systems, and its impact on yield and revenues, thereby enabling a comprehensive understanding of the viability and scalability of these systems in the face of land and climate constraints and other challenges for the cocoa sector in Côte d’Ivoire.
The objectives of this contract include the following: to systematically collect and analyze data on labour utilization, input application, and production, for a sample of cocoa producers representing the diversity of cocoa farming systems in Côte d’Ivoire; to quantify and compare the economic efficiency of agroforestry versus traditional farming systems, with a particular focus on labour productivity; to evaluate the potential of agroforestry systems in maintaining land productivity while adhering to sustainable and environmentally friendly practices; and to provide actionable insights that can inform policy decisions and best practices for cocoa cultivation in Côte d’Ivoire.
The ultimate goal is to empower stakeholders, including farmers, policymakers, and industry leaders, with evidence-based recommendations that can help promote agroforestry as a reliable and profitable farming system that also aligns with the EU’s regulatory framework on imported deforestation, thus contributing to the long-term resilience and prosperity of the cocoa sector.
title: Economic analysis of labour use in agroforestry farming systems in Côte d'Ivoire

summary: TECHNICAL SUPPORT FOR THE DEVELOPMENT AND UPDATE OF EUROMOD – 7 LOTS
content: TECHNICAL SUPPORT FOR THE DEVELOPMENT AND UPDATE OF EUROMOD – 7 LOTS

caName: TECHNICAL SUPPORT FOR THE DEVELOPMENT AND UPDATE OF EUROMOD – 7 LOTS
description:
EUROMOD is a tax-benefit microsimulation model, which covers in a consistent manner the Member States of the European Union. The model allows to study the effects of taxes and social benefits on household incomes and work incentives for the population of each country and for the EU as a whole. EUROMOD is unique in its area as it features a great flexibility in the scope of its simulation and ensures cross-country consistency of the modelling approach and comparability of the results. 
The model has increasingly been used by the Commission services over the past few years, particularly so in the European Semester context. Additionally, the model represents a valuable research infrastructure for the academic community in the area of fiscal policy analysis, with highly cited research conducted using EUROMOD being published in top journals.
The contracts are intended to provide the Commission with services that support the development and update of the microsimulation model EUROMOD for 7 country-specific modules as follows:
Lot 1: Support to EUROMOD for Austria
Lot 2: Support to EUROMOD for Croatia
Lot 3: Support to EUROMOD for Germany
Lot 4: Support to EUROMOD for Greece
Lot 5: Support to EUROMOD for Luxembourg
Lot 6: Support to EUROMOD for Romania
Lot 7: Support to EUROMOD for Slovenia
title: TECHNICAL SUPPORT FOR THE DEVELOPMENT AND UPDATE OF EUROMOD – 7 LOTS

summary: Technical assistance in defining requirements for the inclusion of data and information in Digital Product Passport (DPP)
content: Technical assistance in defining requirements for the inclusion of data and information in Digital Product Passport (DPP)

caName: Technical assistance in defining requirements for the inclusion of data and information in Digital Product Passport (DPP)
description:
The general objective of this call for tenders is to procure targeted and technical support in defining the nature of the information requirements under the Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation (ESPR), for possible inclusion in the Digital Product Passport (DPP), supporting the ongoing work in this area, in the context of the development of product-specific (and in certain cases horizontal) delegated acts.
The specific objectives involve performing an analysis that will contribute to further specifying the requirements in three main areas:
-	Type of information to be included in the product passport: This includes providing an overview of possible information that could be included in the DPP and defining the minimum set of common information required in DPP. Recommendations on the format or units of data may be included as appropriate .
-	General rules and principles specifying the circumstances in which the product passport should correspond to the model, batch, or item level: This refers to determining whether the information in the product passport should be applied at the model, batch, or individual item level.
-	Recommendations on the responsibilities regarding the introduction and update of information in the product passport: This covers identifying the roles and responsibilities of various actors, such as manufacturers, repairers, maintenance professionals, remanufacturers, recyclers, competent national authorities, and the Commission or any organization acting on their behalf, in terms of the type and frequency of data introduction and updates in the product passport.
title: Technical assistance in defining requirements for the inclusion of data and information in Digital Product Passport (DPP)

summary: Capacity building and Experimentation for Innovation for Place-based Transformation
content: Capacity building and Experimentation for Innovation for Place-based Transformation

caName: Capacity building and Experimentation for Innovation for Place-based Transformation
description:
The aim of this contract is to develop and implement an integrated set of activities for equipping European practitioners and policy makers from EU and third countries associated to the programme Horizon Europe with the resources needed to design and implement innovation policies for place-based transformation in the frame of the “Innovation for place based transformation” initiative supported by the European Parliament, with the aim to:

1.	Reinforce territorial capacities for transformative innovation policies by developing and delivering a Capacity Building programme;
2.	Support a place-based transformative innovation policy experimentation arena, where territories can jointly engage into different thematic policy Experimentations Journeys, based around common challenges.

To achieve these objectives the following activities are foreseen in the contract:  
•	To design, develop and deliver a modular training and coaching package (capacity building) targeted to national, local and regional administrations, and their territorial stakeholders (business sector, academia and citizens representatives) from the EU and third countries associated to Horizon Europe. 
•	To design and facilitate transformative innovation expertise and logistic for the support of a minimum 6 Experimentation Journeys (experimentation activities) to be proposed by the Joint Research Centre of the European Commission (EC-JRC) based on the analysis of the received expression of interest by participating territories; 
•	The modular trainings and coaching package and the Experimentation Journeys must be designed to provide a self-standing experience for those taking part in one of the two, and a coordinated experience to those attending both. 
•	In addition, the contractor will undertake the following activities: management  and organisation of events, including logistics, (online, in presence and hybrid), continuous engagement and communication with participants; and coordinating all activities related to Capacity Building and Experimentation Journeys in close collaboration with EC-JRC.
title: Capacity building and Experimentation for Innovation for Place-based Transformation

description:
Het GCO in Petten beschikt over een opslagfaciliteit voor gevaarlijk afval voordat het wordt ingezameld door een gespecialiseerd bedrijf. Deze faciliteit, gebouw 324, bestaat uit een losstaand betongebouw met 1 verdieping, afmetingen ± 5,300 mmx 2,270 mm.
De huidige faciliteit voldoet niet aan de behoeften van het GCO Petten. Er is momenteel geen faciliteit om chemisch afval tijdelijk op te slaan voordat het door bevoegd personeel wordt beheerd en naar behoren wordt opgeslagen. Daarom is er bij de huidige faciliteit extra ruimte (uitbreiding) nodig om tijdelijk veilig met chemicaliën om te gaan (ongeveer dezelfde afmeting als origineel).
Daarnaast zijn er nog andere ruimtes waarvan de deuren grondig gereinigd moeten worden. 
Ten slotte voldoet het bestaande station voor niet-gevaarlijk afval ook niet aan de behoeften van het GCO Petten. Daarom moet de huidige stalen overkapping worden gesloopt en moet er een nieuw houten hekwerk worden geplaatst. Ook zal een deel van de huidige containers worden vervangen door ondergrondse containers.

summary: Survey on growers and citizens’ preferences on pest management for Xylella Fastidiosa
content: Survey on growers and citizens’ preferences on pest management for Xylella Fastidiosa

caName: Survey on growers and citizens’ preferences on pest management for Xylella Fastidiosa
description: This contract aims to collect primary data through surveys to contribute the socioeconomic analysis of Xylella Fastidiosa (Xf) impacts and adoption of Integrated Pest Management (IPM). The survey will investigate the optimal combination of IPM measures from a supply (adoption by growers) and demand (societal valuation) point of view. Further, the survey will cover aspects related to attitudes and behaviours of the growers (e.g. innovativeness of the grower as well growers’ preparedness to take environmental measures on the farm, including risk aversion, networking and knowledge sharing among growers.), aspects related to Xf (e.g. knowledge of the pest), and structural aspects of the farm. The target population of the survey will be EU growers and citizens. The survey must be done through CATI-WEB-CATI interviews for growers in the provinces of Córdoba, Jaén, and Alicante (Spain), and in the Apulia region in Italy. The survey for citizens will be implemented online, with citizens mainly from Andalusia, Comunidad Valenciana (Spain), and the Apulia region in Italy, but also from elsewhere in the two countries.
title: Survey on growers and citizens’ preferences on pest management for Xylella Fastidiosa

summary: Quantification and composition analysis of plastics in the residual (mixed) fraction of municipal solid waste
content: Quantification and composition analysis of plastics in the residual (mixed) fraction of municipal solid waste

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure.

The study will provide an assessment of the composition of plastics in the residual, mixed fraction of municipal solid waste in various Member States, based on a methodology to be developed by the Contractor and an actual sampling and analysis of mixed municipal waste. Current waste statistics show a discrepancy between the amounts of plastic put on the market and those ending up in waste. Despite a certain fraction of plastics remaining in the society, it is assumed that a substantial fraction of plastics ends up in the mixed fraction of municipal waste. This hampers the subsequent recycling of plastics. A better understanding on the amounts and types of plastics that end up in the mixed muncipal waste will thus enable the development of policies to redirect those plastics back into the circular economy.

summary: Stability monitoring EURM-111, EURM-112
content: Stability monitoring EURM-111, EURM-112

description:
The European Commission’s Joint Research Centre (JRC) located in Geel (Belgium) intends to launch a call for tenders for measurements for the annual assessment of stability of Certified Reference Materials (CRMs) EURM-111 and EURM-112 by means of mouse phrenic nerve (MPN) assay and UV spectrophotometry.
The appointed laboratory shall determine the potency (paralytic halftime) of EURM-111 and EURM-112, applying mouse phrenic nerve assay. 4 units of each CRM shall be analysed, with 4 independent technical replicates per unit. In total, 16 measurements per CRM shall be performed. The same units shall be used to determine the A280 absorbance using UV spectrophotometry. 3 independent replicates per unit shall be analysed, using repeatability conditions. In total, 12 measurements per CRM shall be performed.

content: TECHNICAL SUPPORT FOR THE DEVELOPMENT AND UPDATE OF EUROMOD – 7 LOTS

caName: TECHNICAL SUPPORT FOR THE DEVELOPMENT AND UPDATE OF EUROMOD – 7 LOTS
description:
EUROMOD is a tax-benefit microsimulation model, which covers in a consistent manner the Member States of the European Union. The model allows to study the effects of taxes and social benefits on household incomes and work incentives for the population of each country and for the EU as a whole. EUROMOD is unique in its area as it features a great flexibility in the scope of its simulation and ensures cross-country consistency of the modelling approach and comparability of the results. 
The model has increasingly been used by the Commission services over the past few years, particularly so in the European Semester context. Additionally, the model represents a valuable research infrastructure for the academic community in the area of fiscal policy analysis, with highly cited research conducted using EUROMOD being published in top journals.
The contracts are intended to provide the Commission with services that support the development and update of the microsimulation model EUROMOD for 7 country-specific modules as follows:
Lot 1: Support to EUROMOD for Austria
Lot 2: Support to EUROMOD for Croatia
Lot 3: Support to EUROMOD for Germany
Lot 4: Support to EUROMOD for Greece
Lot 5: Support to EUROMOD for Luxembourg
Lot 6: Support to EUROMOD for Romania
Lot 7: Support to EUROMOD for Slovenia
title: TECHNICAL SUPPORT FOR THE DEVELOPMENT AND UPDATE OF EUROMOD – 7 LOTS

summary: Battery cycler for performance and durability tests at single cell level for large cells in JRC laboratories of Petten.
content: Battery cycler for performance and durability tests at single cell level for large cells in JRC laboratories of Petten.

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure.

The cycler will be used to expand the laboratory's testing capabilities and adapt it to new market trends and progress in the field of battery storage. In particular, this system will cover performance and durability tests at single cell level for large cells. Large cells are being continuously more and more adopted by the market while the size (in terms of storage capacity) may reach even 500 - 1 000 Ah in case of cells for stationary systems, and is expected still to grow in the future. Testing such cells require using high currents (several hundreds of Amps) at low voltage. Fulfilling those parameters at the same time is out of the range for systems currently employed in BESTEST lab, and thus the new investment is needed.

description:
Am Standort des JRC Karlsruhe wurde der Neubau eines zusätzlichen separaten Labor- und Lagergebäudes Flügel M geplant und mit den Bauarbeiten begonnen. Die Neubaumaßnahme hat eine Bruttogrundfläche von ca. 8 500 m2 und dient dazu, die notwendige Infrastruktur für die wissenschaftlichen Arbeiten auch für die Zukunft sicherzustellen. Nach Unterbrechung der Arbeiten ist jetzt die Projektfortführung für die restlichen Maßnahmen zur kompletten Errichtung und Inbetriebnahme des Flügel M notwendig. Die Hauptpakete sind Technische Gebäudeausrüstung (TGA 1 und 2) und Anlagensicherung (AS). Für das Gewerk TGA 2 wird ein geeigneter Auftragnehmer (AN) gesucht. Zum Angebotsumfang des hier 
ausgeschriebenen Pakets TGA 2 gehören folgende Systeme und Komponenten:
Gewerk Elektrotechnik:
— Mittelspannungsschaltanlage inkl. Ausrüstung der Trafostationen,
— Netzersatzanlagen,
— USV -Anlagen,
— Haupt - und Unterverteilungen,
— Elektroinstallationen,
— Beleuchtungssysteme,
— Kabelführungssysteme,
— Erdung und Blitzschutz,
Gewerk Leit- und Kommunikationstechnik:
— Fernsprechnebenstellenanlage und Datennetzwerke,
— Durchsageanlage,
— Gegensprechanlage,
— Uhrenanlage,
— Brandmeldeanlage,
— Gaswarnanlage,
— Seismische Instrumentierung,
— Erweiterung des vorhandenen Gefahren- und Video Management System (GVMS),
— Bedien- und Beobachtungssystem (BuB),
— Meldeanlage Unterdruck,
Gewerk Strahlenschutzmesstechnik:
— Überwachung der Luftaktivität,
— Personenüberwachung,
— Ortsdosisleistungsüberwachung,
— Kritikalitätswarnanlage,
— Mobile Messeinrichtungen,
— Low Level Messplatz,
— Zentrale Messstation,
— Prüfstrahler.
title: Neubau Flügel M am Standort des JRC Karlsruhe Lieferung der Technischen Gebäudeausrüstung TGA Teil 2 – Gewerke Elektrotechnik, Leit- und Kommunikationstechnik, Strahlenschutzmesstechnik

summary: GLOBAL PROJECTIONS OF STORM SURGES AND WAVES UNDER CLIMATE CHANGE SCENARIOS
content: GLOBAL PROJECTIONS OF STORM SURGES AND WAVES UNDER CLIMATE CHANGE SCENARIOS

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure.

The aim of this work is to provide the JRC with quantitative estimates of how meteorological sea level components will evolve during the present century along coastlines worldwide. A range of greenhouse gases emissions scenarios will be considered, ranging from stringent mitigation to high emissions. Specific objectives involve the modelling of waves (i) and of storm surges (ii) along coastlines worldwide. The following emissions scenarios are to be considered: SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5, SSP3-7.0, SSP5-8.5. A critical aspect in the execution of this work is the definition of the ensemble of forcing Global Climate Models (GCMs). There is some freedom in the selection of the latter, but it is required that the 5 models classified as primary in the Inter-Sectoral Impact Model Intercomparison Project (ISIMIP ) will be used. The ISIMIP ensemble consists of 10 models that reproduce the variability of larger ensembles. Of these, 5 models are classified as primary, and considered as mandatory in ISIMIP-compliant studies. The other 5 models are classified as secondary and considered optional.
title: GLOBAL PROJECTIONS OF STORM SURGES AND WAVES UNDER CLIMATE CHANGE SCENARIOS

summary: Survey on growers and citizens’ preferences on pest management for Xylella Fastidiosa
content: Survey on growers and citizens’ preferences on pest management for Xylella Fastidiosa

caName: Survey on growers and citizens’ preferences on pest management for Xylella Fastidiosa
description: This contract aims to collect primary data through surveys to contribute the socioeconomic analysis of Xylella Fastidiosa (Xf) impacts and adoption of Integrated Pest Management (IPM). The survey will investigate the optimal combination of IPM measures from a supply (adoption by growers) and demand (societal valuation) point of view. Further, the survey will cover aspects related to attitudes and behaviours of the growers (e.g. innovativeness of the grower as well growers’ preparedness to take environmental measures on the farm, including risk aversion, networking and knowledge sharing among growers.), aspects related to Xf (e.g. knowledge of the pest), and structural aspects of the farm. The target population of the survey will be EU growers and citizens. The survey must be done through CATI-WEB-CATI interviews for growers in the provinces of Córdoba, Jaén, and Alicante (Spain), and in the Apulia region in Italy. The survey for citizens will be implemented online, with citizens mainly from Andalusia, Comunidad Valenciana (Spain), and the Apulia region in Italy, but also from elsewhere in the two countries.
title: Survey on growers and citizens’ preferences on pest management for Xylella Fastidiosa

summary: Stability monitoring EURM-111, EURM-112
content: Stability monitoring EURM-111, EURM-112

caName: Stability monitoring EURM-111, EURM-112
description:
The European Commission’s Joint Research Centre (JRC) located in Geel (Belgium) intends to launch a call for tenders for measurements for the annual assessment of stability of Certified Reference Materials (CRMs) EURM-111 and EURM-112 by means of mouse phrenic nerve (MPN) assay and UV spectrophotometry.
The appointed laboratory shall determine the potency (paralytic halftime) of EURM-111 and EURM-112, applying mouse phrenic nerve assay. 4 units of each CRM shall be analysed, with 4 independent technical replicates per unit. In total, 16 measurements per CRM shall be performed. The same units shall be used to determine the A280 absorbance using UV spectrophotometry. 3 independent replicates per unit shall be analysed, using repeatability conditions. In total, 12 measurements per CRM shall be performed.
title: Stability monitoring EURM-111, EURM-112

summary: Impact of retail alliances on farmers and upstream SMEs
content: Impact of retail alliances on farmers and upstream SMEs

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure.

In recent years, the emergence of retail alliances (RAs) has become increasingly prominent, with large retail groups or chains forming alliances within individual Member States, across various European countries, and even with non-European partners. This trend has raised concerns among suppliers and policymakers regarding the growing concentration of buying power in the retail sector and its potential implications for the agricultural and food supply chain, notably farmers and upstream SMEs. The objective of this project is to provide socio-economic analyses of the impacts of RAs on farmers and upstream SMEs through selected case studies. The project should cover the following issues: (i) impacts of RAs on contract negotiation practices and contracting practices, (ii) impacts of RAs on the prevalence of unfair trading practices, (iii) impacts of RAs on prices, costs, risks and benefits sharing across the chain, (iv) vertical pass-through of costs, risks and benefits of RAs along the chain and (v) horizontal spillover effects on costs, risks and benefits of RAs across different operators. The analyses should be based on information collected through structured interviews and/or focus groups with relevant operators/stakeholders.
title: Impact of retail alliances on farmers and upstream SMEs

summary: Extended Figaro tables 2010-2022: FIGARO-E3
content: Extended Figaro tables 2010-2022: FIGARO-E3

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure.

The FIGARO-E3 database is an inter-country supply, use, and input-output tables (IC-SUIOT) database that includes extensions related to energy and fuel combustion emissions, other GHG emissions, and labor categorized by gender and skill levels. It was originally intended for use in EU environmental policies. However, there are several limitations to this product. Firstly, the update and benchmarking of FIGARO official data was only conducted for the year 2015, thereby restricting the database's utility. Secondly, the current classification systems of industries and products, and environmental pressures and impacts, may not serve all purposes required to design, implement, and monitor EU environmental policies, and may require expansion. Finally, there is no automated process to produce preliminary FIGARO-E3 IC-SUIOT when new FIGARO data is released, i.e., from 2023 onward. The purpose of this contract is to extend the FIGARO-E3 database from 2010 to 2022, incorporating all available FIGARO data. This extension will greatly enhance the versatility and applicability of this data, particularly in the context of EU climate and circular economy policies. In addition, potential expansions of the current products and industries, and environmental pressures and impacts, will be assessed, taking into consideration a wide range of available micro and macro data. This is because expanding the database to incorporate more comprehensive environmental and economic classifications will significantly amplify the potential applications and impact of the data. This could open the door to new applications, for instance, in the frames of open strategy autonomy. Finally, the development of an automated system to update FIGARO-E3 would allow the most recent data to be easily available.
title: Extended Figaro tables 2010-2022: FIGARO-E3

summary: Pilot exercise for data validation & harmonisation for the 2024 EU Industrial R&D Investment Scoreboard
content: Pilot exercise for data validation & harmonisation for the 2024 EU Industrial R&D Investment Scoreboard

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure.

Since 2004, the Joint Research Centre (JRC), Directorate B, has produced the EU Industrial R&D Investment Scoreboards. These reports describe and analyse corporate R&D investment data Scoreboard data and provide additional information on the positioning of leading R&D investing companies in relation to other key indicators of relevance for industrial innovation policy and industrial R&D efforts. The publication of the Scoreboard each December since 2004 intends to raise awareness of the importance of R&D for businesses and to encourage firms to disclose information about their R&D investments and other intangible assets. The data for the Scoreboard come from companies’ publicly available audited accounts. The main objective of this contract is to conduct a pilot exercise for data validation and cross-check for the 2024 EU Industrial R&D Investment Scoreboard, to be published in December 2024. Based on data provided by the JRC, several indicators should be validated for accuracy and eligibility, verified and complemented. Moreover, this work involves cross-checking the data to establish a coherent and comprehensive final dataset, including small additional verifications after publication of the data in the December 2024 Scoreboard report.
title: Pilot exercise for data validation & harmonisation for the  2024 EU Industrial R&D Investment Scoreboard

summary: Stability monitoring EURM-111, EURM-112
content: Stability monitoring EURM-111, EURM-112

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure.

The European Commission’s Joint Research Centre (JRC) located in Geel intends to launch a call for tenders for measurements for the annual assessment of stability of Certified Reference Materials (CRMs) EURM-111 and EURM-112 by means of mouse phrenic nerve (MPN) assay and UV spectrophotometry. The laboratory shall determine the potency (paralytic halftime) of EURM-111 and EURM-112, applying mouse phrenic nerve assay. Four units of each CRM shall be analysed, with four independent technical replicates per unit. - So in total, 16 measurements per CRM shall be performed. The same units shall be used to determine the A280 absorbance using UV spectrophotometry. Three independent replicates per unit shall be analysed, using repeatability conditions. – So in total, 12 measurements per CRM shall be performed.

content: Realization of the electromechanical system of the New Grouting Station and of some minor civil works for its adaptation to Buildings 41-41C-41K at Area 40

caName: Realization of the electromechanical system of the New Grouting Station and of some minor civil works for its adaptation to Buildings 41-41C-41K at Area 40
description:
In the frame of the Decommissioning and Waste Management (D&WM) Program established by JRC Ispra, a New Grouting Station (NGS) must be realized in order to produce conditioned packages of Solid Radioactive Waste (SRW) to be stored at the Interim Storage Facility of the Site.
The NGS requires all the necessary electromechanical systems needed to operate. These systems need to be installed inside three existing buildings inside the Controlled Area of Area 40. Among these systems are: The Handling System, whose scope is the handling of waste drums, overpacks, containers and final waste packages within the NGS facility; the Grouting System, whose function is to prepare wet mortar (grout) for immobilization of nuclear solid waste; all the service and auxiliary systems needed to safely operate the NGS facility. The NGS is key in the Decommissioning and Waste Management (D&WM) Program.

description:
