De gevel van gebouw 050 moet worden gerenoveerd om de isolatiewaarde te verbeteren ter optimalisatie van het energieverbruik. Om de thermische isolatie van gebouw 050 te verbeteren, wordt de gevel aan de buitenkant geïsoleerd. Dit om tegemoet te komen aan de behoefte aan energiebesparingen en de mogelijkheid om een lagere temperatuur te gebruiken voor de verwarming van het gebouw. Het gebouw werd ongeveer 50 jaar geleden opgericht. De gevelrenovatie zal bijkomend de esthetiek en de samenhang van het gebouw verbeteren.

description: The aim of this contract is to assess the prevalence and implications of algorithmic management at work in the EU by collecting representative data on the use of digital devices and on algorithmic management at work, with a particular focus on the use of AI-driven tools. For this purpose, a statistically representative sample of the working age population in all EU Member States will be interviewed by phone, using a standardised questionnaire. The end result will be a dataset that will be used to study the prevalence and implications of digital monitoring and algorithmic management at work in the EU. Another key objective of this contract will be to develop a suitable sampling strategy and survey methodology. The methodological starting point will be the approach taken in the initial implementation of the AMPWork survey.

summary: TECHNICAL SUPPORT FOR THE DEVELOPMENT AND UPDATE OF EUROMOD FOR BULGARIA (LOT 1) & FINLAND (LOT 2)
content: TECHNICAL SUPPORT FOR THE DEVELOPMENT AND UPDATE OF EUROMOD FOR BULGARIA (LOT 1) & FINLAND (LOT 2)

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure.

EUROMOD is a tax-benefit microsimulation model, which covers in a consistent manner the Member States of the European Union. The model allows to study the effects of taxes and social benefits on household incomes and work incentives for the population of each country and for the EU as a whole. EUROMOD is unique in its area as it features a great flexibility in the scope of its simulation and ensures cross-country consistency of the modelling approach and comparability of the results. The model has increasingly been used by the Commission services over the past few years, particularly so in the European Semester context. Additionally, the model represents a valuable research infrastructure for the academic community in the area of fiscal policy analysis, with highly cited research conducted using EUROMOD being published in top journals. The contract is intended to provide the Commission with services that support the development and update of the microsimulation model EUROMOD for Bulgarian and Finnish country-specific modules.

summary: System for the analysis of genomic DNA, cell-free DNA
content: System for the analysis of genomic DNA, cell-free DNA

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure.

The contracting authority intends to buy a system for the analysis of genomic DNA, cell-free DNA and other nucleic acids by proprietary small-scale gel electrophoresis with automated sample processing for quick and reliable sample quality control for RNA and DNA sample analysis. The system for RNA and DNA sample analysis must include: an instrument with automated electrophoresis for RNA and DNA analysis, measuring the DIN (DNA Integrity Number) and RIN (RNA Integrity Number) values. In addition the contractor has to provide a software that provides fast and intuitive data analysis of nucleic acid sample data from the automated electrophoresis instrument. It must offer streamlined data acquisition, analysis, and reporting for nucleic acid sample quality control (QC) and support high-throughput workflows by providing automatic calculation for sample concentration, sizing, and integrity. The software must offer two modes for analysis, which are peak or region focused. The software must enable customizable visualization of the results in various formats like electropherograms, gel images, and tables. summary: Supply of the Electron Backscatter Diffraction detector on the existing scanning electron microscope (SEM) in the MCL laboratory
content: Supply of the Electron Backscatter Diffraction detector on the existing scanning electron microscope (SEM) in the MCL laboratory

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure.

Recent open access projects (CANMECH, SAHARA, CHRONIC and NIFEM) resulted in requests for high-throughput electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) screening analyses beyond the anticipated needs. These requests come in addition to the activities planned based upon institutional (INVISION) and competitive projects (NUCOBAM and INNUMAT), which saturates the availability of the EBSD system on the Plasma focused ion beam - scanning electron microscopy (PFIB-SEM, installed in 312-031). Requests for screening EBSD measurements beyond the anticipated needs stems from the increased variety in materials investigated promoted by open-access projects, compared to institutional and competitive activities for which the existing SEM (312-028) and PFIB (312-031) combination has been configured for. This is particularly true for Open-Access projects with methodological rather than case study synergies with G.I.4 activities. The EBSD detector on the PFIB-SEM is geared towards high spatial and angular resolution and 3-D imaging, which is not needed for screening analyses. Further, the PFIB-SEM is a heavily-used and advanced instrument (often runnign 24/7 using automation and further periodic downtimes for maintenance), procured primarily for other demanding tasks, including micro-fabrication, 3-D imaging, lamella preparation and high-resolution imaging of ion-polished cross-sections. Therefore, screening EBSD measurements block the PFIB-SEM and affect its availability for fulfilling its main purpose. The development of the situation is anticipated to lead soon to the rejection of measurements requests beyond the reasonable for Open Access and/or competitive activities. The proposed solution is the installation of a dedicated entry-level EBSD system on the SEM installed in 312-028. Benefits are anticipated on several fronts. First, the pressure on the PFIB-SEM for tasks outside its main purpose will be alleviated. Second, the SEM can be manipulated by Open-Access users after adequate training, which is not tractable with the PFIB-SEM because of its use case at G.I.4 (prototyping and 3-D measurements campaigns over several weeks) and higher complexity and maintenance needs.
title: Supply of the Electron Backscatter Diffraction detector on the existing scanning electron microscope (SEM) in the MCL laboratory

summary: Support study for developing a method for assessing data from the disclosure obligation on the destruction of unsold consumer products and for the definition of product-specific or sectoral bans
content: Support study for developing a method for assessing data from the disclosure obligation on the destruction of unsold consumer products and for the definition of product-specific or sectoral bans

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure.

The aim of this contract is to provide an analytical framework/methodology for the assessment of information on destruction of unsold products and the lifecycle environmental impacts of this practice, to be used for future impact assessments which can lead to a ban of this practice for a specific product groups. The analytical framework for the assessment of information on destruction of unsold products should take into account the information that is required to be disclosed under paragraph 1 of Article 20 of the ESPR proposal: the number of unsold consumer products discarded per year, differentiated per type or category of products; the reasons for the discarding of products; the delivery of discarded products to preparing for re-use, remanufacturing, recycling, energy recovery and disposal operations in accordance with the waste hierarchy as defined by Article 4 of Directive 2008/98/EC. Therefore, the specific objectives of this project are: i) Analysis of industry-wide practices (understanding the prevailing trends and practices related to the destruction of unsold products in various sectors (e.g. textile, ICT, etc.) and collection of data on the destruction of unsold consumer products by consulting stakeholders/economic operators). The research should provide information on the reasons and economic drivers for destruction. ii) Develop an analytical framework for the environmental impact assessment and life cycle management (evaluating the environmental impacts of product destruction and understanding their life cycle management). iii) Drafting the format for the disclosure of the information about destruction of unsold products. iv) Develop a methodology to assess the benefit of putting a ban in place v) Testing the analytical framework. vi) Producing a report that include all the findings and methodologies developed.
title: Support study for developing a method for assessing data from the disclosure obligation on the destruction of unsold consumer products and for the definition of product-specific or sectoral bans

description:

JRC-Petten performs research on structural materials, assessment of structures, systems and components with regards to integrity and ageing effects and material degradation mechanisms, relevant to the safety of current and future nuclear power plants. In this context, JRC-Petten is currently using various methods for characterization of metallic materials and components, including tensile testing, creep testing, small punch testing, Charpy impact testing, mechanical testing in corrosive environments, application of microscopic test methods, and neutron diffraction. To complement its materials characterization portfolio, JRC-Petten intends to re-introduce the capability to perform Vickers hardness testing on a variety of the sample types relevant to, among others, the above testing techniques. This will concern testing of samples of diverse sizes and shapes, including small thickness (small punch testing) or large surface area (neutron diffraction) samples. To this end, JRC-Petten would like to procure a new table-top hardness testing machine for a wide range of test loads.

content: Alkaline phosphatase (ALP) raw material

description:

A new CRM for ALP will be produced and the processing will be done by an external company specialized in the production of control material for human enzyme measurements. This human alkaline phosphatase (ALP) material will be used to develop a reference material certified for its catalytic activity concentration. The catalytic activity of ALP in serum is frequently measured in medical laboratories for the detection and diagnosis of liver diseases (such as cirrhosis, hepatitis and cancer) and bone disorders. In order to contribute to a clinical decision, the obtained results should be accurate and equivalent, independent of reagents kits, instruments or the location and time of testing. Standardisation of enzyme measurements can be achieved by using reference systems, in which certified reference materials together with the reference measurement procedures developed by the International Federation of Clinical chemistry (IFCC) are the key components.

summary: Modelling the environmental and socio-economic impacts of Circular Economy policies
content: Modelling the environmental and socio-economic impacts of Circular Economy policies

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure.

The overarching objective of this Contract is to produce a methodology and associated modelling toolbox to assess the environmental and socio-economic impacts (costs, employment, and distributional effects) of EU CE policies. To answer the research question “How effective they are and how they can be recalibrated to bring us on the required trajectory to deliver on the (Green Deal and CE) objectives”? Methodology and associated modelling tools should build upon the state-of-the-art in the field. Particular attention shall be placed on making the modelling framework scientifically robust, user-friendly and adjustable for future applications. The specific objectives of the study are: • To elaborate future scenarios of CE policies for selected carbon-intensive industrial materials (e.g. cement/construction materials, steel, aluminium, plastic), based upon interviews with relevant stakeholders and literature. • To produce a methodology and, accordingly, flexible modelling tools to assess the environmental and socio-economic impacts of CE policies. The modelling framework shall ensure flexibility to incorporate future changes, quantification of the relevant impacts, parametrisation, uncertainty analyses. • To apply the methods to a selected number of scenarios representing CE policies or policies that can affect circularity in EU, focusing primarily on carbon-intensive materials. Among the others, the potential effects of Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanisms on the CE in Europe shall also be studied.
title: Modelling the environmental and socio-economic impacts of Circular Economy policies

summary: Assessment of carbon intensities of refined products resulting from co-processing with bio-based feedstock in oil refineries
content: Assessment of carbon intensities of refined products resulting from co-processing with bio-based feedstock in oil refineries

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure.

JRC intends to purchase consultancy services to model petroleum refineries running with co-processed bio feedstock and able to assess their carbon intensities. The work will include several bio feedstock as inputs, various amount of bio-feedstock as inputs and several insertion points for the bio-feedstock inputs in the refinery. The analysis will include the use of bio-feedstock inputs with various compositions, including lipids (vegetable oils, (used cooking oils, animal fats and other waste-products), tall oils, biomass-derived oils (fast pyrolysis oil and other biocrudes) from municipal solid waste and other lignocellulosic biomass. The work should also include sensitivity analysis regarding the environmental assessment of the carbon intensities of the refined co-processed outputs, either based on LCA framework or others.

summary: Supply of an Atomic Force Microscope
content: Supply of an Atomic Force Microscope

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure.

Unit F.2 is active in the characterization of nanomaterials since many years and in particular in their physico-chemical characterization and interaction with biological systems. Both aspects need special microscopy techniques, since conventional optical microscopy techniques are limited in resolution. Today, one of the golden standards for nanomaterials characterization is Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM). AFM is able to measure nanomaterials and characterize their mechanical, electrical and optical properties and it can work in different environments. Moreover it can work directly on living cells in-vitro, including their nanomechanical characterization and nanomanipulation and controlled dispensing of nanomaterials. These studies will have an enormous impact on institutional projects like PITCH, SAMSON and TEMPO all involving the characterization of nanomaterials as well as the outreach activities, where AFM is one of the most requested techniques. Thus, the unit F2 (Technologies for Health) of the directorate Health consumer and reference materials intends to purchase an Atomic Force Microscope (AFM).
title: Supply of an Atomic Force Microscope

summary: Survey-based study on the state of play of Digitalisation in EU agriculture
content: Survey-based study on the state of play of Digitalisation in EU agriculture

description: This contract aims to collect primary data through surveys to contribute to the assessment of the state of play of digitalization in the EU agriculture. For this, the Commission will draw a first version of the questionnaire on digitalisation in the agricultural sector. The survey will cover technologies such as precision farming, real time applications, terrestrial and aerial drones, tools on prices, sensors, artificial intelligence, blockchain, satellite imagery, big data and analytics, agricultural decision support systems, etc. Further, the survey must investigate (i) the use of digital technologies and services on the farm, the scope of their use and its implications for sustainability and resilience, (ii) bottlenecks and drivers for the adoption of digitalization, by investigating financial support (i.e. investments, credits) and support services (such as advisors), infrastructure, skills and digital and data governance aspects, as well as (iii) the propensity of EU farmers to pursue investments in digitalization in the future. The target population of the survey will be EU farmers. The survey must be done through face-to-face interviews and other methods (telephone, virtual meeting, videoconference) in at least six Member States.

summary: Provision of support to the JRC-Geel Safety Culture Self-Assessment – Analysis of the SCSA questionnaire
content: Provision of support to the JRC-Geel Safety Culture Self-Assessment – Analysis of the SCSA questionnaire

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure.

The Article 5.7 of the Royal Decree of 30 November 2011 on the safety requirements for nuclear installations requires that, at all levels, the organization must continuously demonstrate, support and promote attitudes and behaviours that reflect a strong and sustainable safety culture. The management system must provide the means to systematically develop, support and promote these attitudes and behaviours. The relevance and effectiveness of these resources must be assessed in the context of self-evaluations (self-assessment) and the reviews of the management system. The Royal Decree of 20 July 2001 on the general regulations on the protection of the population, of workers and the environment against the dangers of ionizing radiation lays down the priorities of the Health Physics Service (HPS), such as working on the continuous improvement of safety, radiation protection and promoting and supporting the knowledge development, training and safety culture of staff. In 2021, the JRC-Geel launched the action plan on the safety culture self-assessment. It was decided to use the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) safety culture practical guidance as a basis against which to assess the strengths and weaknesses of the JRC-Geel site’s safety culture. The IAEA approach was considered fit for purpose, since it offers an opportunity of developing an in-house understanding (on the long-term) and reflection regarding the organization’s culture. The JRC-Geel launched as part of its on-going safety culture self-assessment, a safety culture questionnaire in February 2023, which was closed on 31st March 2023. JRC-Geel would like support in the analysis of the results of the aforementioned questionnaire. Here is the general outline of the contract specifications: • to foresee at least two meetings with the JRC-Geel SCSA team to discuss results and organise communication; • the full analysis of the SCSA questionnaire ; • presentation of the results as graphs; • definition of the questions to be developed in focus groups and interviews; • technical report with results of the analysis; To be done in 15 working days to be carried out within 1 month upon delivery of the Excel data files by JRC-Geel.
title: Provision of support to the JRC-Geel Safety Culture Self-Assessment – Analysis of the SCSA questionnaire

summary: Pilot study of the SELFIEforTEACHERS version for Early Childhood Education and Care (ECEC)
content: Pilot study of the SELFIEforTEACHERS version for Early Childhood Education and Care (ECEC)

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure.

This call follows both DigCompEdu framework (https://publications.jrc.ec.europa.eu/repository/handle/JRC107466) and the Digital Education Action Plan (2021-2027; https://education.ec.europa.eu/focus-topics/digital-education/action-plan) in developing SELFIEforTEACHERS, a self-reflection instrument for educators. Almost 140,000 school education teachers have already registered in the tool, allowing them to reflect on their digital practices, test their practical knowledge and guide them in further developing their skills. The objective of this study is to provide an adapted version of SELFIEforTEACHERS for Early Childhood Education and Care (ECEC) professionals, which (i) will inform policy making and research and (ii) will provide a practical instrument to education stakeholders empowering them to promote digital competence. The study is expected to involve researchers, ECEC leaders as well as ECEC professionals. The expected outcomes are (i) a reliable and valid adapted SELFIEforTEACHERS version for ECEC professionals and (ii) an increase awareness in the digital competence for ECEC professionals.

content: Development of a new website for Copernicus Emergency Management Service - On Demand Mapping

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle value procedure.

summary: Stabilised AC and DC Power Supplies for cathode heating of klystrons, thyratron's and injection.
content: Stabilised AC and DC Power Supplies for cathode heating of klystrons, thyratron's and injection.

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure.

Stabilised power supplies for cathode heating of klystrons, thyratron's and injection. Spare parts and replacement of unreliable power supplies. Among the pulsed white spectrum neutron sources available in the world, the linear electron accelerator facility in Geel (GELINA), is the one with the best time resolution. GELINA combines four specially designed and distinct units: a high-power pulsed linear electron accelerator, a post-accelerating beam compression magnet system, a mercury-cooled uranium target, and flight paths with measurement equipment. GELINA is one of the first JRC research infrastructure providing open access to Member State researchers allowing a variety of nuclear measurements. The accelaration of the electrons is achieved by injection of high power radio frequency pulses into the accelerator cavities. These pulses are produced by klystron modulators. The modulators are fed from a pulse forming network which is switched by a hydrogen thyratron. High stability, accuracy and precision are required from the electronic circuits involved in order to achieve stable electron beam acceleration and energy distribution. The ordered power supplies will be part of the klystron and thyratron cathode circuits.
title: Stabilised AC and DC Power Supplies for cathode heating of klystrons, thyratron's and injection.

Well being in digital education is an emerging policy field and it is expected to have high policy impact at European level and beyond. The objective of the study is to provide research evidence on the needs of well-being in Digital Education in Member States which: a) will inform policy making and research b) will provide practical instruments to the education stakeholders empowering them to promote well-being in Digital Education. The study is expected to involve Policy makers in all member states and Ed-tech designers with support from DG-EAC and JRC, parents, , School leaders teachers and students across educational levels (primary, secondary and VET). The expected study outputs are: 1.An evidence based study on the state of play of well-being needs in digital education environments in the MS (literature Review and field study) in order to identify what works, for whom, why and what does not work. 2. summary: Verhardingswerkzaamheden tussen gebouwen 120 & 060
content: Verhardingswerkzaamheden tussen gebouwen 120 & 060

description:
Gelieve op te merken dat dit geen aanbesteding betreft, maar een publicatie om aan te kondigen dat de aanbestedende dienst de intentie heeft in de toekomst een onderhandelingsprocedure van geringe of middelmatige waarde te publiceren (zie hier).

Betreft de heraanleg van de bovenbouw op de site JRC te Geel gelegen tussen de gebouwen 060 en 120. De bestaande verharding is niet meer in goede staat. Waterstagnatie, breuk in betonverhardingen en verouderde asfaltdelen. De zone tussen de gebouw 060 en 120 is van gevel tot gevel verhard. Deze oppervlakte wordt niet maximaal benut door voertuigen/vrachtwagens. Het ontwerp omhelst de aanpak van de oppervlakte waarbij rekening wordt gehouden dat ongebruikte verharding wordt vervangen door groenzones en of waterdoorlatende verharding. De grens van werken is vanaf de huidige rijweg tot op einde zijgevellijn van gebouw 060. De aanpak van het toegangspad naar de inkom gebouw 060. De gabaritbreedte tussen de twee gevels bedraagt 18,25m. De nieuwe aanleg omhelst een centraal weggedeelte van 10m breed in betonverharding en dit in kader van doorgang vrachtwagens en andere dienstwagens. De overige verhardingen en funderingen zijn gekozen in functie om deze aan te leggen in doorlatende verhardingen en funderingen. De overige invulling wordt voorzien in groenvakken/grasdallen/poreuze betonstraatstenen en dit voor toegankelijkheid van bestaande garages, inkomdeuren en poorten. Tussen de bestaande rijweg en zone naar de containeropstelling bestaat deze zone nu uit een asfaltverharding. Voorstel is om deze zone deels in te vullen als groenzone met nog een 3-tal parkeerplaatsen in grasdallen. De zone insteek naar het containerpark wordt mee aangelegd in beton. Langs de zijgevel wordt nog een groenzone voorzien. Op einde van de insteek containerzone is voorstel om de verharding over de volledige breedte mee op te nemen zodat er minstens drie containers naast elkaar kunnen geplaatst worden. Het pad naar de inkom is op heden 2m breed. Dit pad wordt verbreed tot 2,5m in kader van beter toegankelijkheid en gebruik (voetgangers/fietser richting fietsstalling,…). Naar niveaus toe behouden we het laagste punt (de huidige greppel) en wordt een prefab vlakke kantstrook voorzien (beter overrijdbaar). Vanaf gebouw 060 naar de kantstrook wordt een betonverharding in één helling aangelegd. De verharding gebouw 120 wordt ook éénzijdige helling voorzien naar de kantstrook. Naar niveaus toe betekent dit dat de wegenis naar gebouw 120 hoger komt te vallen dan de huidige verhardingsaanzet tegen het gebouw. Door het niveau op te trekken tot 2cm onder het vloerpas vervalt ook één optrede aan de zij-inkom.
title: Verhardingswerkzaamheden tussen gebouwen 120 & 060

summary: Quantification and composition analysis of textiles intended for re-use, recycling, and disposal
content: Quantification and composition analysis of textiles intended for re-use, recycling, and disposal

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure.

The general objective of this contract is to sample, quantify and characterise textiles ending up in mixed solid municipal waste (TMW) and textiles intended for re-use/recycling (TIR) in selected EU Member States, and to assess their management. The specific objectives of the study are: - To develop a sampling strategy and methodology that generates new measurement data on TMW/TIR (mass flows and composition data, as outlined below) in EU regions that differ in their management system for used textiles, taking into consideration potential constraints in terms of sample size and logistics associated to the budget. Therefore, the strategy should take into account main drivers for textile waste generation and the management of used textiles; - To measure in a standardised manner absolute quantities of TMW/TIR for each of the samples using the developed sampling strategy; - To measure in a standardised manner the potential for value conservation and circularity by indexing parameters linked to material quality (e.g. minimum standards for reparability, reusability and recyclability) and composition (e.g. information on type of the spectrum of natural and synthetic fibers and the relative proportion/purity levels of these fibers in garments). The scope of the work is limited to (i) textiles that end up in mixed municipal waste as defined in the Waste Framework Directive (2008/98/EC) (TMW), and (ii) textiles fractions intended for re-use/recycling following the separate collection of textiles (TIR). Textile articles that fall under the scope of this study include post-consumer household textiles, such as clothes, shoes, and other (small) home textiles (sheets, kitchen linens, bath towels, etc.). The exact definition of textile articles and products is to be agreed with the Contractor. Separate collection systems involve that a material stream is sorted/divided by type and nature to facilitate a specific treatment. Separate collection systems for textiles varies across Member States, and may collect waste and/or non-waste materials, for instance at textile waste sorting facilities, bring/donation/recycling banks, charity organisations, etc. The geographical coverage of the present contract must include minimum 2 Member States of the European Union.
title: Quantification and composition analysis of textiles intended for re-use, recycling, and disposal

summary: Syringes and repeating adaptors ETD kit
content: Syringes and repeating adaptors ETD kit

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure.

Detection technology at the airport is often the last line of defence against a terrorist attack. In Europe, the specialist knowledge and capability to test explosives detection equipment are not evenly distributed across Member States. The European Commission – Directorate general Joint research Centre (JRC) is actively supporting Member States to implement EU policies by enhancing testing capabilities, promoting best practices and facilitating the testing and verification of screening equipment deployed at European Airports. In this context, the JRC has developed an explosive trace detection (ETD) test kits (code: JRC-S4S-200) to verify that ETD equipment in airports continuous to meet performance requirements.). To date, the ETD test kit (& training courses) have been provided to the Commission’s inspectors (DG MOVE), the national inspectors of the 27 EU Member States, the EFTA surveillance authorities, and non-EU Members of ECAC. In order to enhance and harmonise the testing capabilities in Europe, the JRC is now making these kits available to European Civil Aviation Airports.

description:

The European Commission’s Joint Research Centre (JRC) located in Geel has the intention to order measurements for the assessment of stability of candidate Certified Reference Material (CRM), ERM-CZ130 PAHs and elements in fine dust (PM10-like) by means of indirect an direct methods. The goal of this study is the assessment of stability and minimum sample intake of candidate CRM ERM-CZ130 for PAHs on fine dust (PM10-like), applying method EN 12341 for sample weighing. The basis of the stability assessment approach is to assess the degree of instability of the candidate CRM. This is best achieved by performing measurements under repeatability conditions. The basis of minimum sample intake assessment is a series of measurements with deceasing amount of sample taken from two randomly selected vials. summary: Counter-UAS living lab
content: Counter-UAS living lab

description: The application of drone (Unmanned Aircraft Systems UASs) is becoming very popular in many areas with the implementation of the new drone regulations. However, there is potential for misuse of drones: they can be used to breach privacy, for espionage by using cameras or other sensors, to hijack telecommunication signals and in combination with biological or chemicals agents, explosives or other weapons they could harm persons, disrupt services and damage infrastructure. The JRC DRONE project is doing research on how to counter UAS around critical infrastructure. As part of this project JRC will setup a living lab for Critical Infrastructure stakeholders. It will demonstrate policy impact to identify needed policies around c-UAS, for research on c-UAS solutions, to develop processes, procedures and to link it to solutions. summary: Counter-UAS Living Lab
content: Counter-UAS Living Lab

description: The application of drone (Unmanned Aircraft Systems UASs) is becoming very popular in many areas with the implementation of the new drone regulations. However, there is potential for misuse of drones: they can be used to breach privacy, for espionage by using cameras or other sensors, to hijack telecommunication signals and in combination with biological or chemicals agents, explosives or other weapons they could harm persons, disrupt services and damage infrastructure.The JRC Drone project is doing research on how to counter UAS around critical infrastructure. As part of this project JRC will setup a living lab for Critical Infrastructure stakeholders. It will demonstrate policy impact to identify needed policies around c-UAS, for research on c-UAS solutions, to develop processes, procedures and to link it to solutions.This FWC will be used to buy services, equipment and to supplement JRC competences with experts needed to setup the living lab and a full counter UAS solutions.

summary: Technical Support for the Development and Update of EUROMOD – Seven Lots
content: Technical Support for the Development and Update of EUROMOD – Seven Lots

description: EUROMOD is a tax-benefit microsimulation model, which covers in a consistent manner the Member States of the European Union. The model allows to study the effects of taxes and social benefits on household incomes and work incentives for the population of each country and for the EU as a whole. EUROMOD is unique in its area as it features a great flexibility in the scope of its simulation and ensures cross-country consistency of the modelling approach and comparability of the results. summary: Data provision on affordability of sustainable food consumption and sustainability preferences during food inflation
content: Data provision on affordability of sustainable food consumption and sustainability preferences during food inflation

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle value procedure (read more here).

Food consumption and transition to sustainable food system are inherently linked, as food consumption has environmental (e.g. emissions of greenhouse gases) and public health effects. This is in particular highlighted in the EU Farm to Fork Strategy stating that “current food consumption patterns are unsustainable from both health and environmental points of view” and that the transition to sustainable food system cannot “happen without a shift in people’s diets”. The need for changing diets is also recognized by some European consumers: more than three quarters of Europeans believe that climate change is a serious problem in their country at the moment. This is also reflected in the consumers’ food purchasing decision, with a sizable proportion of EU consumers stating that they have changed their consumption to more sustainable food in recent period. Concurrently, during the first part of 2022, the affordability of food gained policy attention as the average food inflation significantly increased in the EU potentially affecting sustainable consumption choices of consumers. The objective of this project is to provide food consumption data that allow to examine the food purchasing choices (value and volume) among consumers aggregated over different sustainable food product categories (e.g. organic, plant-based substitutes/alternatives for animal products), consumer type (e.g., income, age, gender), consumer attitude towards sustainability (self-declared level of sustainable awareness) and year when consumers are subject to price pressure caused by inflation. This data should be provided for at least one Member State.
title: Data provision on affordability of sustainable food consumption and sustainability preferences during food inflation

content: NL-Petten: Algemene aanneming voor onderhouds-, af- en ruwbouwwerken in en rondom de gebouwen die worden beheerd en/of gebruikt door het GCO Petten.

description:
Gelieve op te merken dat dit geen aanbesteding betreft, maar een publicatie om aan te kondigen dat de aanbestedende dienst de intentie heeft in de toekomst een onderhandelingsprocedure van geringe of middelmatige waarde te publiceren (zie hier).

Het GCO Petten is voornemens een kader werkendiensten contract af te sluiten ter afdekking van de volgende werkzaamheden: preventieve en herstellende onderhoudswerken, alsook inrichtings-, aanpassings- en afwerkingswerken aan zowel de binnen- als de buitenzijde van de gebouwen die worden gebruikt of beheerd door de Europese Commissie in Petten (met name metselwerk, alle soorten vloer- en wandbekleding, alle schilderwerken, alle soorten scheidingswanden, verlaagde plafonds, verhoogde vloeren, houten schrijnwerk, ijzerwaren, alle technieken voor de af- en ruwbouw, afdichting en het onderhoud van daken en gevels, enz.). Voorts dekt het contract de uitvoering van ad-hoc projecten voor inrichtings- en ruwbouwwerken die gedurende contract uitvoering naar voren komen.

description: Isotopic reference materials for uranium and plutonium are on high demand within the nuclear safeguards community, e.g. JRC-G.II.8, DG Energy, the IAEA (International Atomic Energy Agency). In particular, a new 233U spike is needed to replace the exhausted IRMM-040a spike, and a mixed spike with 233U and 242Pu is needed to replace the exhausted IRMM-046c spike for the characterisation of large dried spike (LSD) reference materials. For long-time storage of these new reference materials quartz ampoules are needed. Since flame-sealing is not permitted in the JRC-G.2 nuclear laboratories any more, screw-cap quartz ampoules are the best option. Screw-cap ampoules have been ordered by JRC-G.2 in the past and used successfully in recent years. To satisfy the current and future needs, 475 quartz ampoules need to be purchased.
title: Quartz Ampoules for the Certification of Uranium and Plutonium Reference Materials

summary: Supply of an inert gas glovebox workstation for handling, chemical processing and storage of air-sensitive samples
content: Supply of an inert gas glovebox workstation for handling, chemical processing and storage of air-sensitive samples

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle value procedure (read more here).

JRC Karlsruhe intends to procure a standalone, high-integrity glovebox workstation of stainless steel construction providing a universal laboratory bench area, designed for a single operator and having generous storage capabilities (large freezer, underbench cupboard for solvent bottles, shelves). The glovebox must operate under continuously recirculated, filtered, purified, and monitored high-purity argon atmosphere and fitted with suitable technical provisions to allow efficient inward and outward transfer of the material and samples from the adjacent laboratory area. The operations undertaken involve manual handling, production, isolation, storage and dispensing of highly oxygen and moisture sensitive solid and liquid chemical samples, generation and use of reactive intermediates (i.e. ligand transfer reagents) via reactions in anhydrous solvents, precision weighing of air-sensitive materials. This glovebox is not intended for radiological or extremely toxic volatile material service.
title: Supply of an inert gas glovebox workstation for handling, chemical processing and storage of air-sensitive samples

summary: BIODIVERSITY, AGRICULTURAL PRACTICES AND ECONOMIC SUSTAINABILITY AND BIODIVERSITY IN FARMING SYSTEMS IN SUB-SAHARAN AFRICA
content: BIODIVERSITY, AGRICULTURAL PRACTICES AND ECONOMIC SUSTAINABILITY AND BIODIVERSITY IN FARMING SYSTEMS IN SUB-SAHARAN AFRICA

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle value procedure (read more here).

The objective of this study is to undertake a comprehensive analysis of the functioning of farming systems in different countries of Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), with a specific focus on the impacts on biodiversity. Various case studies will be selected in rural areas, representing the diversity of farming systems and agro-ecological conditions in developing countries, and notably SSA. In each of the case study, a sound methodology will be applied for the characterization of the functioning of farming systems and for the collection of data related to the various dimension of their sustainability, completed by the collection of detailed and specific data for the construction of biodiversity indicators related to botanic, entomologic (e.g. pollinator) and soil biodiversity.

summary: Feasibility Study of the European Digital Skills Certificate, as Action 9 of the Digital Education Action Plan (2021-2027)
content: Feasibility Study of the European Digital Skills Certificate, as Action 9 of the Digital Education Action Plan (2021-2027)

description: The Digital Education Action Plan (2021-2027) proposes as Action 9 to ‘Develop a European Digital Skills Certificate (EDSC) that may be recognised and accepted by governments, employers and other stakeholders across Europe. This would allow Europeans to indicate their level of digital competences, corresponding to the Digital Competence Framework proficiency levels’. The objectives of the study are:— mapping and analysis of the Digital competence development and skills certification landscape in the EU;— identification of stakeholders for consultation;— gap analysis (what is the demand for an EDSC and what is lacking) to understand the role and value of an EU Digital Skills Certificate and how it could support recognition of digital skills in Europe;— validation of the operational concept;— technical feasibility;— costs and benefits analysis for different stakeholders;— limitations, risks and challenges;— propose the definition of the purpose, scope and steps of a pilot of the EDSC.
title: Feasibility Study of the European Digital Skills Certificate, as Action 9 of the Digital Education Action Plan (2021-2027)

summary: Versuchsaufbau für Brandversuche Lüftung / Experimental Setup for Fire tests on ventilation ducts / Wing M
content: Versuchsaufbau für Brandversuche Lüftung / Experimental Setup for Fire tests on ventilation ducts / Wing M

description:
Bitte beachten Sie, dass es sich hierbei nicht um eine Ausschreibung handelt, sondern um eine Veröffentlichung, in der die Absicht des öffentlichen Auftraggebers angekündigt wird, ein künftiges Verhandlungsverfahren mit niedrigem oder mittlerem Wert zu veröffentlichen.

Das Projekt "Wing M" ist ein Großprojekt der Infrastruktur der GFS Karlsruhe: der Bau eines neuen Laborgebäudes für den Umgang mit radioaktiven Stoffen gemäß dem deutschen Atomgesetz. Seine Fertigstellung ist für 2025 geplant. Bei dem Lüftungssystem für Fl. M wird ein Produkt angewendet, dass nicht für alle Anwendungsfälle eine behördliche Zulassung besitzt. Nur ein Teil der Anwendungen des Produkts, die wir für den Flügel M benötigen, ist zugelassen. Für die Anwendungen, für die es keine Zulassung gibt, müssen wir eine "Zustimmung im Einzelfall" beantragen. Wir haben die Materialprüfanstalt Braunschweig beauftragtt, um ein Gutachten für die ausgewählte Brandschutzdämmung mit unseren eigenen spezifischen Anwendungen zu erstellen. Im Rahmen dieses Gutachtens wurde nun deutlich, dass ein positives Gutachtenergebnis für zwei Anwendungsfälle nur durch Brandversuche beurteilt werden kann und nicht durch reine Berechnungen möglich ist. Die Durchführung des Versuchs selbst sowie die Auswertung der Ergebnisse und der technische Bericht wurden bereits bei der Materialprüfanstalt Braunschweig (MPA Baunschweig) beauftragt. Sie stellt auch die Versuchseinrichtungen (Ofen mit entsprechender Messtechnik für den Versuch) zur Verfügung. Sie hat auch die Größen und Formen der zu prüfenden Lüftungskanäle einschließlich der Dämmung vorgeschrieben. Allerdings ist die MPA Braunschweig weder Hersteller von Lüftungskanälen noch hat sie Monteure, die die zu prüfenden Kanäle und die Isolierung an ihrem Ofen anbringen können. Daher müssen wir die folgenden Dienstleistungen einkaufen: - Lieferung der Lüftungskanäle und der Isolierung nach den Vorgaben der MPA Braunschweig - Montage und Einbau der Komponenten in den Räumen der MPA Braunschweig (Ofen) - Demontage und Entsorgung der geprüften Kanäle und Isolierungen nach dem Brandversuch - Der Einbau der Komponenten muss zu Beginn der Woche 14/2022 erfolgen, da der Versuchsofen für die Wochen 14 bis 16 / 2022 reserviert ist. - Die Demontage der Bauteile muss am Ende der Woche 16/2022 erfolgen, da der Versuchsofen für die Wochen 14 bis 16 / 2022 reserviert ist.

summary: Quantification of amino acids in hydrolysed protein solutions by means of high-performance amino acid analysis (AAA)
content: Quantification of amino acids in hydrolysed protein solutions by means of high-performance amino acid analysis (AAA)

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure.

EC-JRC requests to order high-performance amino acid analysis (AAA) measurements on four different candidate reference materials. The materials are pure native and recombinant protein toxins in solution. The samples will be quantitatively hydrolysed at EC-JRC and shall be analysed by the tenderer. Per analyte, 12 measurements shall be performed, whereby on each of the 3 measurement days, 4 measurements shall be performed. Calibration samples and QC samples are to be analysed in addition in each measurement series. A validated method has to be applied. The results shall be reported per amino acid (those amino acids the lab routinely uses for quantification). Timelines for results are February 2022 for the first two analytes and April 2022 for the other two analytes. The measurement results are needed in order to have to have qualitatively and quantitatively enough data for assigning protein mass fraction (and/or protein mass concentration) values to the materials.

summary: Supply of a two-colour microarray scanner to read biomolecules arrays
content: Supply of a two-colour microarray scanner to read biomolecules arrays

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure.

Pandemics preparedness needs fast, accurate and sensitive methods for the detection of pathogens and for following the presence of antibodies against pathogens after infection. Bio-photonics, coupled with specific bio-recognition elements and microfluidics, offers the ability to improve the overall testing capabilities against existing and emerging pathogens. In particular, protein microarrays are an established approach to the development of highly sensitive, and reproducible tests, while detection in the near infrared region increases sensitivity. The unit F.2 has several activities in this area and is developing and harmonizing methods and measurement strategies for the accurate characterization of bio-recognition elements against pathogens (both antigens and antibodies). To be able to read and analyse protein microarray chips, the unit F.2 aims to purchase a protein microarray scanner able to detect signals in the near-infrared region.

summary: Het aanleggen van noodstroomvoorziening in gebouw 309 van het GCO te Petten.
content: Het aanleggen van noodstroomvoorziening in gebouw 309 van het GCO te Petten.

description:
Gelieve op te merken dat dit geen aanbesteding betreft, maar een publicatie om aan te kondigen dat de aanbestedende dienst de intentie heeft in de toekomst een onderhandelingsprocedure van geringe of middelmatige waarde te publiceren.

De European Commission heeft besloten dat in het bestaande gebouw 309 een noodstroomvoorziening dient te komen. Deze noodstroomvoorziening zorgt ervoor dat bij een netuitval de bedrijfsvoering niet verstoord wordt. Op verdiepingen krijgen alle kantoren en vergaderruimten minimaal één WCD die op de noodstroomvoorziening is aangesloten. De nieuwe no-break WCD’s krijgen een afwijkende kleur, zodat voor de gebruiker duidelijk is dat dit de noodstroomvoorziening betreft. De scope van het project betreft met name een nieuwe voedingskabel aansluiten op verdeelinrichting HK6N-3, vermogensautomaat groep F2 instellen, doorvoeringen, voedingskabel aanleggen van 310 tot nieuwe UPS verdeelinrichting in gebouw 309. Voor gebouw 309 betreft met name demontagewerkzaamheden, nieuwe verdeelinrichtingen, één UPS, voedingskabels, kanalisatie, doorvoeringen, no-break WCD’s, toevoerrooster techniekruimte 033 en luchtafzuiging. In gebouw 309 wordt een UPS geplaatst, waarop de noodstroomvoorzieningen zijn aangesloten. Voor het geval dat er voor lange tijd noodstroom benodigd is, wordt het nieuwe UPS aangesloten op het NSA in het naastgelegen gebouw 310.

summary: Floating Litter Monitoring App and web data management interface
content: Floating Litter Monitoring App and web data management interface

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure.

The Marine Strategy Framework Directive (MSFD) and the Zero Pollution Action Plan require harmonised approaches and methodologies for the acquisition of comparable environmental pollution data over time and space. The quantification of floating macro litter at sea (and its input through rivers, as well as litter on the shallow seafloor) is in that context, a specific challenge, as it is currently depending on visual observations, which require specific tools and approaches in order to ensure comparable data output. A mobile computer application, based on the MSFD protocol for the monitoring of floating macro litter has been developed by JRC (supplied by ATOS) and used for environmental monitoring. It has been employed within the RIMMEL project for riverine litter input and within the EMBLAS project in the Black Sea, in the Mediterranean Sea, and as well in the Arctic for monitoring of floating macro litter at sea. This approach, so far used as a scientific tool, should now be made available to EU Member States and beyond, in order to facilitate the large scale data acquisition through scientists, and when applicable, citizens. The application will support the implementation of a harmonized monitoring scheme for floating marine macro litter at sea and in rivers, allowing the monitoring of surface floating litter. The web interface will in addition allow the upload of data on floating litter and shallow seafloor litter in a harmonised format through a data template. The new version will allow the availability of the app through official platforms for a wide public and provide additional functionalities.
title: Floating Litter Monitoring App and web data management interface

summary: Data-collection activity on gender differences in the labour market
content: Data-collection activity on gender differences in the labour market

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle value procedure.

The purpose of this tender procedure is the implementation of an independent study by the JRC aimed at identifying the behavioural factors related to the gender pay gap . In particular, the contractor will support the European Commission by implementing an online experiment. The study will focus on understanding and confirming existing evidence on behavioural traits attributed to women. For example, to investigate if social comparison in the labour market is gendered, if women are less prone to proactive salary negotiations and self-promotion, if they are more likely to signal their willingness to work for a lower wage, if under certain circumstances they are more risk averse, have lower levels of competitiveness and underperform in negotiations when information is scarce. Finally, women seem to be harsher than men in their self-evaluation, tending to see themselves as less competent than their co-workers, which can lead them to accept unfair treatment.

summary: Analysis of knowledge sharing approaches for models and methods in science
content: Analysis of knowledge sharing approaches for models and methods in science

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure.

The objective of this study is to identify and analyse different (online) approaches to sharing knowledge on models and methods within and across scientific communities. The analysis should describe the salient features of each approach, the underpinning rationale, and important strengths and weaknesses that impact efficiency and effectiveness. It is intended that the study goes beyond life sciences since the sharing of models and methods is also an important pursuit in other domains, bringing together scientists based in academia, industry, government, and civil organisations. Consideration should also be given to economic and organisational factors to set up and operate different knowledge sharing approaches with a view to understanding the type and level of costs involved, challenges in ensuring sustainability, and ultimately impact versus investment. The findings of the study should provide a sound evidence-base that will inform future approaches to sharing knowledge on non-animal models and methods used in science.

Terephthalate (PET). The specific method which is under investigation

functional group such as thiols which may be used to covalently bind
ligands which have specific functionalities such as fluorescence. The
peptides should exhibit strong preferential binding to hydrophobic
surface such as polymers and low binding to hydrophilic inorganic
materials such as metal oxides and minerals.

summary: Uptake of Nanoplastics into Organoids (UNO)
content: Uptake of Nanoplastics into Organoids (UNO)

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure.

The EU scientific advisory bodies such as Science Advice for Policy by European Academies (SAPEA 2019) and the Group of Chief Scientific Advisors (SAM, 2019) have recommended a number of policy actions in order to respond to the growing public concern on micro/nanoplastic pollution. One of their recommendations was related to the identification and prioritization of plastic items that can pose high risks to humans and the ecosystem. In particular, the lack of understanding on the degradation process of plastic products into micro and nanoplastics and the impact of plastic debris on human health requires attention by the legislative /regulatory system. Whereas biological barriers protect humans from the uptake of microplastics, risks for the internalization of plastic particle into the human circular system can increase with a decrease in size of the particles. The limited information on the impact of nanoplastics on human health requires the development of strategies, tools and methods in order to identify those nanoplastics occurring in environmental mixtures that can be harmful to humans. The study object of the call for tender aims to explore organoids for their potential to serve as in vitro model for toxicological studies. Furthermore, the study should help us to understand whether nanoplastics can be harmful to vulnerable populations such as patients with pre-damaged intestinal tissue or manifested diseases.

summary: Supply of a FTIR Spectrometer with Heated ATR
content: Supply of a FTIR Spectrometer with Heated ATR

description: The European Commission [Directorate-General Joint Research Centre (DG JRC) in Geel] intends to purchase a fourier transform infrared spectroscopy coupled with attenuated total reflectance (FTIR-ATR).Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy coupled with attenuated total reflectance (FTIR-ATR) is a non-destructive and rapid technique very well suited for routine control of purity. summary: Case studies on algorithmic management in the logistics and healthcare sectors
content: Case studies on algorithmic management in the logistics and healthcare sectors

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure.

The digital transition is acknowledged as one of the driving forces of “Commission Work Programme – A union that strives for more” (COM(2020) 37 final), which states states that Europe “must move first on the future technologies with the most potential, while ensuring the European approach is human, ethical and value-based”. Algorithmic management, i.e. the use of computer-programmed procedures for the coordination of work, is a key aspect of the digital transition, which is expanding from digital labour platforms to traditional work settings. The outcomes are likely to have several impacts on the so-called “future of work”. The main aim of this contract is to carry out eight case studies at establishment level for investigating the impact of the algorithmic management on work organisation, job quality and industrial relations in the logistics and healthcare sectors, in two European countries (Italy and France). For each sector (logistics and healthcare) and country (Italy and France), the contractor is expected to visit at least two different establishments and carry out qualitative interviews, collect documentary evidence and undertake desk research to complement as necessary. As final deliverable, the contractor will then summarise the main findings from the case studies in four reports, one for each country-sector combination.
title: Case studies on algorithmic management in the logistics and healthcare sectors

summary: Economic Complexity Analysis of Export Prices
content: Economic Complexity Analysis of Export Prices

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure.

The objective of the contract is to investigate how Economic Complexity analysis can provide new insights by exploiting the rich bilateral data on unit export prices provided in UN Comtrade or similar databases. Comtrade, in particular, contains information on the total value in US dollars as well as the quantity (in various units) of each trade flow. From this it is possible to retrieve an average unit value, or export price, for the traded goods. In this, the work should be carried out from a perspective of European industrial competitiveness. Another objective is the use – and potential advancement – of state-of-the art data-cleaning and noise-controlling techniques, as they are currently employed and discussed in Economic Complexity (e.g. Tacchella et al. 2018). This is considered an essential part of the contract, and shall be used to prepare a consolidated dataset of export prices of the highest possible quality.

summary: Data Collection for Behavioural Experiment with Farmers
content: Data Collection for Behavioural Experiment with Farmers

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure.

The new green architecture of the proposal for a Common Agricultural Policy post 2020 (CAP 2020+) introduces a new voluntary policy measure to promote environmentally friendly practices, the Eco-Schemes (ECS). Farmers so willing will be able to choose from a portfolio of environmentally friendly management practices offered by countries against a payment.In 2020 the European Commission – Joint Research Centre (JRC) undertook a behavioural experiment on farmers and the new green architecture of the CAP focusing basically on the trade-offs between mandatory (conditionality) and voluntary (eco-schemes) contributions of farmers to the environment (Dessart el al. 2021) . The experiment did not fully take into account the interaction with agri-environmental and climate measures (AECM). Therefore there is a need to improve the understanding of the inter-actions between eco-schemes and AECM with a view to the assessment of CAP strategic plans and the implementation of the new CAP. The present contract aims to collect data from a sample of farmers in at least four countries from the European Union using a computer assisted platform. The selected contractor is expected to: - program the questionnaire and experiment developed by the JRC (including all of its variants to capture the relevant treatments) into an electronic platform; - translate it to the relevant languages; - pilot the questionnaire in some of the countries where the fieldwork will be undertaken, - implement the changes needed as a follow-up of the finding of the pilot, - implement the revised questionnaire and experiment to a sample of farmers in the selected countries, and - prepare a database with the data gathered.
title: Data Collection for Behavioural Experiment with Farmers

summary: Counter Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS) proof of concept. Equipment installation, configuration and tests
content: Counter Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS) proof of concept. Equipment installation, configuration and tests

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure.

The application of drone (Unmanned Aircraft Systems UASs) is becoming very popular in many areas and U-Space services are maturing in parallel with implementation of the new drone regulations. In Europe drone use is increasing rapidly with services in agriculture, transport, survey, surveillance etc. However, there is potential for misuse of drones: they can be used to breach privacy, for espionage by using cameras or other sensors, to hijack telecommunication signals and in combination with biological or chemicals agents, explosives or other weapons they could harm persons, disrupt services and damage infrastructure. The JRC DRONE project is doing research on how to counter UAS around critical infrastructure. As part of this research JRC will do a proof of concept (PoC) counter UAS installation on the JRC Geel site. The lessons learned from this PoC will be included in the handbook to critical infrastructure owners. The proof of concept will include material and services to: • Install Software, infrastructure, ICT system, services and all material needed for this • Install and configure a UTM (C2C) system to merge data from the all the sensors specified in list • Spectrum analysis equipment and all material, service needed to connect this to UTM system • Remoter eID detectors (2) and all linked material and service to add this to the UTM system • Short range radar according to specification and all material and service needed to connect this to UTM • UAS detection camera with all services and material needed to connect this to UTM system • Test drones flown by a certified drone pilot • Operators and management staff to complete the PoC.
title: Counter Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS) proof of concept. Equipment installation, configuration and tests

summary: Study on mapping the deployment of regional bioeconomies in Europe
content: Study on mapping the deployment of regional bioeconomies in Europe

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure.

Analytical study to support R&I policy-making - Study on mapping the deployment of regional bioeconomies in Europe. Since 2017, the European Commission has been mapping, through surveys and desk research, the progress of Member States and other countries in developing strategies and other policy initiatives dedicated to the Bioeconomy at the national level. At the regional level, however, the large number of relevant topics, initiatives, stakeholders and IT platforms covering different territorial realities, languages, etc., so far, did not allow a comprehensive overview of the strategies adopted. The present study aims to support the Commission to understand and analyse the deployment of regional bioeconomy strategies across Europe. The study will also support the objectives of the European Bioeconomy Policy Forum (EBPF) to facilitate interaction and mutual learning of best practices, while enhancing interregional cooperation to deliver joint actions in support of bioeconomy developments (Action 3.2.3 of the EU Bioeconomy Action Plan). The commissioning of this study to tenderers with relevant knowledge, expertise and capabilities to collect and analyse information on social and environmental policies across European regions will facilitate the achievement of these goals.
title: Study on mapping the deployment of regional bioeconomies in Europe

Gelieve op te merken dat dit geen aanbesteding betreft, maar een publicatie om aan te kondigen dat de aanbestedende dienst de intentie heeft in de toekomst een onderhandelingsprocedure van geringe of middelmatige waarde te publiceren.

Ten behoeve van gebouw gerelateerde werktuigbouwkundige installaties is het GCO Petten voornemens een onderhoudsovereenkomst af te sluiten voor een initiële periode van 12 maanden, verlengbaar tot een maximum duur van 48 maanden conform contract. Het betreft een kader contract en diensten worden middels bestelbonnen afgeroepen. De onderhoudsdiensten, bestaande uit zowel preventief als correctief, zijn van toepassing op de volgende groepen van installaties: A. Luchtbehandelingskasten en B. Luchtverdeelslangen. Preventief onderhoud: Het periodiek controleren, reinigen, schoonmaken en verrichten van de door de Aanbestedende Dienst of diens gemachtigde noodzakelijk geachte werkzaamheden, zoals aangegeven in het preventief onderhoudsprogramma en conform de onderhoudsrichtlijnen van fabrikanten van de desbetreffende installaties en onderdelen. Het preventieve onderhoud is inclusief klein materiaal, gebruiksartikelen en afvoer van materiaal. Correctief onderhoud: Het reageren op en het uitvoeren van werkzaamheden nadat een zodanig defect (storing of verstoring) is geconstateerd dat de installatie of delen daarvan buiten werking is/zijn gesteld of moeten worden gesteld. Onder het correctief onderhoud worden tevens de acties gezien die genomen moeten worden naar aanleiding van constateringen gedurende preventief onderhoud en welke niet onder laatstgenoemde service zijn afgedekt (geen klein materiaal). Deze worden gezien als curatieve acties, waaronder wordt verstaan het uitvoeren van reparaties en/of vervangingen naar aanleiding van constateringen gedaan tijdens preventief onderhoud.
title: NL-Petten: Preventief en correctief onderhoud van luchtbehandelingskasten en luchtverdeelslangen van het GCO Petten

summary: FTIR Spectrometer with heated ATR
content: FTIR Spectrometer with heated ATR

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure.

Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy coupled with attenuated total reflectance (FTIR-ATR) is a non-destructive and rapid technique very well suited for routine control of purity. Optimal results are obtained by analysing products in its melted form. Therefore, a compact system able to be placed easily in different locations to facilitate the sample handling/preparation and provided with a temperature controlled ATR unit is required. Here are some of the minimum technical requirements which can still change before the launch date of teh effective call: At least the following instrumental and operational features must be guaranteed: - The device must be based on Infrared spectroscopy (spectral range at least 400 cm-1 to 4000 cm-1). - The spectrometer must include a heated Attenuated Total Internal Reflectance module (ATR) with a robust (fixation of the crystal by glue does not assure the required stability and will therefore not be accepted) diamond crystal allowing the measurement over the full spectral range according to the optical configuration of the spectrometer. - The ATR diamond crystal plate must be heatable up to 100 C for the analysis of fluids. The temperature controller must be completely included in the spectrometer and temperature must be regulated from the software. - The device must be a compact system consisting of a FT infrared spectrometer with the heatable ATR and the computer for operating the software. The device must be portable and easy to transport in order to facilitate the operation within a laboratory or in different laboratories. - ...

summary: Modelling study on the role of Energy Communities in the energy transition
content: Modelling study on the role of Energy Communities in the energy transition

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure.

The European Commission has developed the European Green Deal strategy aiming at transforming the EU into the first climate-neutral continent by 2050. At the same time, the Clean Energy Package offers new opportunities for citizens and SMEs on how to satisfy their energy needs. This comes at a time when innovations, such as deep cost reductions of distributed generation and storage technologies, digitalisation and transactive energy schemes, make possible the emergence of a new decentralised paradigm in the energy system. Estimates suggest that by 2030, energy communities could own some 17% of installed wind capacity and 21% of solar. By 2050, almost half of EU households are expected to be producing renewable energy. The key objective of this work is assessing, through modelling, the impact of policy and regulatory instruments, such as network tariffs and energy taxes, on the possible evolution of the energy system, with a particular focus on the expected operational and investment decisions by community-based energy initiatives. The JRC intends to contract consultancy services to prepare a modelling study on the role of Energy Communities in the energy transition. The contractor is expected to analyze qualitatively and quantitatively the impact of network tariffs and energy taxes & levies on the operational and investment decisions of Energy Communities. The contractor is expected to develop use cases of typical Energy Communities and assess their impact on the energy system, using UCED and expansion energy models. The estimated value of the contract is 60.000 Euro for a period of 9 months. The economic operators interested to receive the invitation to tender have to register on this website.
title: Modelling study on the role of Energy Communities in the energy transition

summary: development of XFuelBuilder for Automatic evaluation of Neutron Coincidence Collar (NCC) Measurements by Euratom Inspectors
content: development of XFuelBuilder for Automatic evaluation of Neutron Coincidence Collar (NCC) Measurements by Euratom Inspectors

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure.

The service required is the development of XFuelBuilder for Automatic evaluation of Neutron Coincidence Collar (NCC) Measurements. Objectives: XFuelBuilder is a Montecarlo-based modelling software application originally developed to support the nuclear inspectorates in the analysis of NCC (Neutron Coincidence Collar) measurements of fresh BWR and PWR fuel assemblies. It runs MCNP (Monte Carlo N-Particle transport) and PTA (Pulse Train Analysis) simulations on user-definable fuel assemblies for a range of NCC detector geometries, and reports the simulation results for comparison with measurement data. However, in its current version, XFuelBuilder can only be used as a stand-alone software and the configuration of the simulation parameters is only performed through a graphical user interface. In order to enable the embedded use of XFuelBuilder in connection with the Integrated Review and Analysis Platform (IRAP) and automatically analyse data of (unattended) measurements, the software needs to be re-engineered. A new version of the XFuelBuilder application will be developed. summary: Feasibility Study of the European Digital Skills Certificate, as Action 9 of the Digital Education Action Plan (2021-2027)
content: Feasibility Study of the European Digital Skills Certificate, as Action 9 of the Digital Education Action Plan (2021-2027)

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure.

The recent Digital Education Action Plan (2021-2027) published last Sep 30th 2020, proposes as Action 9: to “Develop a European Digital Skills Certificate (EDSC) that may be recognised and accepted by governments, employers and other stakeholders across Europe. This would allow Europeans to indicate their level of digital competences, corresponding to the Digital Competence Framework proficiency levels”. The first task that the EC is undertaking is the development of a Feasibility Study. The Joint Research Centre of the European Commission, and in particular, the Unit B4 Human Capital and Employment, is in charge of its execution. The detailed specifications of this study will be developed taking into account the input gathered through the 1st stakeholders' consultation (24/2-12/3). The study foresees a time of 12 mm and the outsourcing of the study for an amount of 100.000€. The aims of the study are the following: (1) analysis of existing certification schemes and models in Europe; (2) identification of stakeholders for consultation; (3) gap analysis (what is the demand for an EDSC and what is lacking) to understand the role and value of an EU Digital Skills Certificate and how it could support recognition of digital skills in Europe; (4) validation of the operational concept; (5) technical feasibility; (6) costs and benefits analysis for different stakeholders; (7) limitations, risks and challenges; (8) propose the definition of the purpose, scope and steps of a pilot of the EDSC.
title: Feasibility Study of the European Digital Skills Certificate, as Action 9 of the Digital Education Action Plan (2021-2027)

summary: Development of a multimodal schedule-based route planner application
content: Development of a multimodal schedule-based route planner application

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure.

The aim of this contract is to provide the Joint Research Centre (JRC) with an open-source route planner application that will support the unit Economics of Climate Change, Energy and Transport (JRC.C.6) of the Directorate C Energy, Transport and Climate modelling activities in the domain of multi-modal scheduled-based public transport. The European Green Deal is a set of policy initiatives by the European Commission with the overarching aim of making Europe climate neutral in 2050. Currently transport accounts for a quarter of the Union’s greenhouse gas emissions and it is still growing. The sustainable mobility policy of the European Green Deal seeks a 90% reduction of those emissions by 2050. Among other initiatives, it will address vehicle emissions, urban congestion, promote the use of railway for freight and improve public transport. Public transportation data is largely based on schedule information provided by public organizations in different formats, more traditionally in General Transit Feed Specification (GTFS ) and more recently in Network Timetable Exchange (NeTEx) format. The JRC.C.6 unit is seeking to expand its modelling capabilities by having a new multimodal scheduled-based transport tool optimised for the analysis of GTFS and NeTEx railway data with EU-wide coverage. The application sought shall be based in one of the open-source route planners currently available in the market but further customised to accommodate the specific requirements needed for modelling purposes at EU-27 level. Aspects as data cleaning and formatting will also have to be tackled. Further data results analysis and visualisation options are also being considered under the scope of this contract.
title: Development of a multimodal schedule-based route planner application
