summary: Support to the assessment of the 2020 climate change pledges from large Asian emitters
content: Support to the assessment of the 2020 climate change pledges from large Asian emitters

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure.

The Economics of Climate Change, Energy and Transport (JRC.C.6) Unit of Directorate C 'Energy, Transport and Climate' unit counts with different modelling tools for the assessment of the impacts of climate-related policies at EU and global level. These tools aim at mimicking the market behaviour in those sectors whose economic activity entails greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions (mainly energy-intensive sectors and land-use ones), as well as the macroeconomic impacts in terms of costs, efficiency gains, terms of trade, jobs, etc. across the different sectors of the economies. The JRC.C.6 Unit is seeking to enhance its modelling and analysis capabilities related to country-level and global projections of GHG emissions pathways, with special focus on addressing the implications of the pledges announce by Japan, China and South Korea. This involves the mobilization and improvement of the energy-economy models at the disposal of the Unit; the update of the underlying databases; and the execution of quantitative analyses under different assumptions of regional and global policy architectures. The aim of this contract is to assist JRC.C.6 in the execution of model-driven analyses of regional and global projections of GHG emissions, with a particular focus on the climate-protection pledges announced in 2020 by the main Asian emitters. The contract will assist with updated data, scenario analyses and improved model-based capabilities. It includes the study of the feasibility, costs and implications of the series of implementation pathways.
title: Support to the assessment of the 2020 climate change pledges from large Asian emitters

summary: Technical support services for the setup, maintenance and update of the EREK knowledge base
content: Technical support services for the setup, maintenance and update of the EREK knowledge base

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure.

The European Resource Efficiency Knowledge Centre (EREK for short) provides tools, information and business opportunities demonstrating new and better ways for European companies, especially SMEs, to be resource efficient, improve their environmental performance, and benefit from circular economy business models. Launched a few years ago as an independent project, EREK is now being integrated in the European Cluster Collaboration Platform (ECCP) in order to leverage powerful synergies by reaching out to industrial cluster organisations and their members. A key aspect of the resources provided by EREK is the Knowledge Base, a repository of validated, up-to-date information, based on state-of-the-art experience gathered from top performers and validated by experts, presenting in particular best practice on resource efficiency and the circular economy in various industrial and economic sectors. The EREK knowledge base aims to deliver practical, accurate information on technical and economic aspects in an easy-to-use format to achieve maximum impact in the targeted organisations and help them become more resource efficient. The objective of this contract is to provide technical support services for the setup, maintenance and update of the EREK knowledge base. To this end, it will be necessary to refine both the form and content of material, which would be the most impactful to deliver resource efficiency solutions within the target groups of EREK. For instance, the technical content submitted by users of the platform (suggestions for showcases or case studies) will be reviewed and validated prior to publication; in parallel, best environmental management practices (or “BEMPs”) will be updated or created to add to the continuously updated body of knowledge available through EREK/ECCP. An Industrial Symbiosis toolkit will also be developed and updated. This will provide companies, clusters and other key stakeholders with information on resource efficiency solutions adapted to their needs. More broadly, this contract will contribute to the validation of the technical content of the knowledge base to enrich the portfolio of resource efficiency solutions presented to the EREK community.
title: Technical support services for the setup, maintenance and update of the EREK knowledge base

content: Plasma cleaning system for activation of glass substrates and thin films

description:

A bench-top plasma instrument is required for substrate preparation and surface activation of deposited thin films. Specifically, we are interested in surface cleaning, activation for better adhesion and soft-etching capabilities. The instrument should be equipped with a vacuum chamber that is able to accommodate glass substrates of minimum 100 x 100 mm and preferably up to 200 x 200 mm. Further, it should be able to deliver variable RF powers. Other process parameters such as pressure, plasma duration, and the choice or composition of gas should be controlled by the user via a built in PC interface. The system needs both a manual and automated, recipe-programed mode. The instrument will be used with non-toxic gases only. Finally, the instrument should have an oil-free vacuum pump.

summary: TECHNICAL SUPPORT FOR THE DEVELOPMENT AND UPDATE OF EUROMOD FOR SWEDEN
content: TECHNICAL SUPPORT FOR THE DEVELOPMENT AND UPDATE OF EUROMOD FOR SWEDEN

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure.

EUROMOD is a tax-benefit microsimulation model, which covers in a consistent manner the Member States of the European Union. The model allows to study the effects of taxes and social benefits on household incomes and work incentives for the population of each country and for the EU as a whole. EUROMOD is unique in its area as it features a great flexibility in the scope of its simulation and ensures cross-country consistency of the modelling approach and comparability of the results. The model has increasingly been used by the Commission services over the past few years, particularly so in the European Semester context. Additionally, the model represents a valuable research infrastructure for the academic community in the area of fiscal policy analysis, with highly cited research conducted using EUROMOD being published in top journals. The contract is intended to provide the Commission with services that support the development and update of the microsimulation model EUROMOD for Sweden .
title: TECHNICAL SUPPORT FOR THE DEVELOPMENT AND UPDATE OF EUROMOD FOR SWEDEN

summary: Stability monitoring of two candidate certified reference materials ERM-FD104 (dioxide powder) and ERM-FD105 (barium sulfate) by transmission electron microscopy
content: Stability monitoring of two candidate certified reference materials ERM-FD104 (dioxide powder) and ERM-FD105 (barium sulfate) by transmission electron microscopy

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure.

Stability monitoring of two candidate certified reference materials ERM-FD104 (titanium dioxide powder) and ERM-FD105 (barium sulfate) by transmission electron microscopy (TEM). The purchase is a critical requirement in the production process of the aforementioned certified reference materials (link to JRC.F.6 active Work Programme). The European Commission’s Joint Research Centre (JRC-Geel, Belgium) has the intention to award a framework contract (FWC) for services to cover the investigation of the stability of two powder candidate certified reference materials (CRMs), ERM-FD104 and ERM-FD105. The services are referred to as “short-term” and “long-term” stability studies. These terms must be interpreted as the time periods during which the final CRMs will be stable after their release. Results obtained from the short-term stability studies will be used by the Contracting Authority to establish appropriate conditions for dispatch of the CRMs to customers. Results obtained from the long-term stability studies will be used by the Contracting Authority to establish appropriate long-term storage conditions and define the shelf-life of the CRMs. The Contractor will analyse the size of the constituent particles of an alumina-coated titanium dioxide (candidate ERM-FD104) and a barium sulfate (candidate ERM-FD105) fine powder using transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and according to the technical specifications as described below. The certified reference materials will support the implementation of the European Commission’s Recommendation on the definition of a nanomaterial (2011/696/EU). The FWC will include 4 possible projects: - Project 1: Short-term stability of candidate ERM-FD104 - Project 2: Short-term stability of candidate ERM-FD105 - Project 3: Long-term stability of candidate ERM-FD104 - Project 4: Long-term stability of candidate ERM-FD105 The Contracting Authority will exceptionally accept participation of economic operators from other countries without creating a precedent or obligation for the future.
title: Stability monitoring of two candidate certified reference materials ERM-FD104 (dioxide powder) and ERM-FD105 (barium sulfate) by transmission electron microscopy

summary: Computational thinking and computer science in school education in Europe (Computhink)
content: Computational thinking and computer science in school education in Europe (Computhink)

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure.

The aim of this contract is to provide an update and further analysis of the 2016 JRC report “An analysis of educational approaches to developing Computational Thinking”. The report provided a comprehensive overview of research findings and grass root and policy initiatives for developing Computational Thinking in compulsory education in Europe. Since the publication of this report, however, many changes have been happening on curricula in Europe. This is linked to the growing understanding that digital competence goes beyond basic digital skills. The study will reflect on these changes and in particular on how curricula are addressing the need for developing competences in computational thinking and computer science. The work will include: • A review of academic and grey literature and policy documents; • Semi-structured interviews with experts, policy makers and stakeholders; • A final report summarising Computational thinking and Computer Science approaches and paradigms in primary and secondary schools in Europe.

summary: Qualitative analysis of SELFIE Impact
content: Qualitative analysis of SELFIE Impact

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure.

SELFIE is the European self-reflection tool to help schools develop their digital capacity. It was launched by the European Commission in October 2018 and now counts more than 7500 schools and 670,000 users from 57 countries. The study concerns a qualitative research to analyse the impact and use of SELFIE in schools with the aim to explore ways to improve the tool and the support materials and get insights into how the tool can be used in the most effective way to support the digital transformation of schools. To this end the study will need to 1. Identify indicators and describe the impact of SELFIE 2. Situate the impact of SELFIE within the context of the digital transformation of schools, taking into account interrelated concepts like: digital readiness of schools, school management models, the changing landscape of technologies, theory of change in organizations, integration of innovation in education as well as the datafication 3. Run at least 15 case studies, in three different countries (five schools per country). The study will gather qualitative data on the impact of SELFIE in schools but also design and test interventions (design-based research) which will aim at supporting schools to use SELFIE in ways that support their digital transformation. 4. Provide a set of recommendations including but not limited to: the improvement of the tool; support material; school actions; taking into account also the difference between school types.
title: Qualitative analysis of SELFIE Impact

summary: Development of a multimodal schedule-based route planner application
content: Development of a multimodal schedule-based route planner application

description:

The aim of this contract is to obtain a multimodal schedule-based route planner application built upon the current version of one of the open-source tools currently available. The new version of the tool must fulfil the following requirements: • Ability to perform trip planning and routing analysis based on transport schedule data. For calculations over large areas (multi-country level), the use of OpenStreetMap may not be adequate due to the OSM file size. • Ability to carry out simulations at, at least, EU-27 level with reasonable resources in terms of ICT infrastructure and computation time.

summary: Realizzazione della pavimentazione in calcestruzzo armato post-teso per la piattaforma esterna nord dell’edificio 48
content: Realizzazione della pavimentazione in calcestruzzo armato post-teso per la piattaforma esterna nord dell’edificio 48

description:
Si informa che la presente non è un bando di gara, ma una pubblicazione che annuncia l'intenzione dell'amministrazione aggiudicatrice di pubblicare una futura procedura negoziata di basso o medio valore.

Costruzione di una piattaforme esterna all'edificio 48 del CCR impiegata per la costruzione e la demolizione di campioni sperimentali di grandi dimensioni testati nel laboratorio ELSA del CCR. Gli edifici sperimentali che vengono costruiti e demoliti sulla piattaforma, vengono trasportati da e verso il laboratorio per mezzo di speciali rulli (procedura unica per questo tipo di laboratorio), pertanto le piattaforme devono avere un'ottima planarità e l'assenza di giunti. Per questa ragione la piattaforma deve essere realizzata con calcestruzzo post-teso che consente la realizzazione di superfici piane senza giunti di dilatazione e limita quindi i problemi riscontrati con le piattaforme precedenti. Al contempo, il Centro Comune di Ricerca (JRC) intende proporre l'utilizzo di materiali sostenibili per la realizzazione di questa piattaforma. La capacità di utilizzare materiali secondari (aggregati riciclati) costituisce un ulteriore aspetto importante al fine di realizzare un'economia circolare dei materiali da costruzione nel rispetto delle priorità del Green Deal.

summary: Homogeneity monitoring of titanium dioxide (ERM-FD104) and barium sulfate (ERM-FD105) particle candidate certified reference materials by transmission electron microscopy
content: Homogeneity monitoring of titanium dioxide (ERM-FD104) and barium sulfate (ERM-FD105) particle candidate certified reference materials by transmission electron microscopy

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure.

Homogeneity monitoring of two candidate certified reference materials ERM-FD104 (titanium dioxide powder) and ERM-FD105 (barium sulfate) by transmission electron microscopy (TEM). The purchase is a critical requirement in the production process of the aforementioned certified reference materials (link to JRC.F.6 active work programme). EUROPEAN COMMISSION JOINT RESEARCH CENTRE Directorate F – Health, Consumers and Reference Materials (Geel) Reference MaterialsCommission européenne/Europese Commissie, Retieseweg 111, 2440 Geel, BELGIQUE/BELGIË Geel, 15 July 2020 Technical specifications for the homogeneity monitoring of alumina-coated titanium dioxide and barium sulfate particle candidate certified reference materials by transmission electron microscopy Scope and background The European Commission’s Joint Research Centre (JRC, Geel, Belgium) has published an invitation to tender for a study to cover the investigation of the batch homogeneity of two candidate certified reference materials, ERM-FD104 and ERM-FD105. summary: Experiential Learning in Vocational Education and Training (VET) – Lessons for ICT Mediated Learning
content: Experiential Learning in Vocational Education and Training (VET) – Lessons for ICT Mediated Learning

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure.

The purpose of this contract is to generate knowledge and spread understanding about, as well as explore new approaches for experiential learning in initial and/ or continued Vocational Education and Training (VET) and other learning sectors that can inform secondary education in a post-Covid-19 outburst environment in the EU. The aim of this contract is to produce a minimum of 6 in-depth case studies, looking into application of experiential learning beyond the classroom, analyse them, and extrapolate lessons that can be shared within the wider education and training community. The focus will be primarily on VET (initial and/or continued VET) but can span over other learning contexts and will concentrate on the promotion of a key competence for lifelong learning. The study will look in particular at work-based VET, including apprenticeships, with the purpose to understand how effective experiential learning beyond the classroom is and what can be transferred to other contexts. The contractor will examine how experiential learning methods by “breaking the walls” of the classroom and focusing on creating value for others, can be leveraged to ease transition to online/blended learning formats across format education and training systems in scenarios where social distancing remains a constraint to resuming school-based education. The contractor will collect qualitative information in the field both form educators and learners, by way of in-depth semi-structured interviews, focus groups and/or direct observations. The analysis of the data collected will help understand: how – in VET – experiential learning interventions that are open to the external ecosystem facilitate the acquisition of entrepreneurship competence, other key competences (e.g. digital, personal social and learning to learn) and of curricular subjects, what the necessary conditions to be embedded for effective student learning are and what aspects of teaching and learning (including assessment) can be transferred to online/ blended learning settings.
title: Experiential Learning in Vocational Education and Training (VET) –  Lessons for ICT Mediated Learning

The aim of this contract is to carry out three case studies investigating the socio-economic impact of automation in the service industries, in the EU. The contractor will examine the impact of three different technologies by conducting qualitative, in depth, semi-structured interviews; the establishments/companies to be interviewed must have their main operations in an EU Member State. The contractor will carry out one case study on Professional cleaning robots; one case study on Autonomous Guided Vehicles (AGVs) in logistics; and one case study on Remote monitoring devices in healthcare. The aim of these case studies it to understand: how automation technologies change the business model, production and economic process in the service industries; the implications of these changes for work organization, occupational health and safety, and job quality; the implications of these changes in terms of tasks, occupations and skill requirements; and the drivers and barriers for the automation of services in the EU and potential future developments.

content: Supply of a Headspace Sampler to be used with a Gas-Chromatograph

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure.

The Directorate JRC.F - Health, Consumers and Reference Materials of the Joint Research Centre (the JRC) has the mission to provide scientific support to EU policy relating to different aspects of the food chain, consumer products, medical devices, health technologies, chemicals, cancer and rare diseases, nutrition, and public health care systems and to operate EU Reference Laboratories and Centres producing reference materials for a variety of areas. Particular emphasis is put on the management of collective scientific knowledge in relevant areas and its translation into evidence for policy making. The Directorate serves the Consumers, Food Safety and Health policy areas, and supports EU policy makers to tackle related upcoming policy initiatives in the field of food and feed safety control, such as food allergens, natural and process contaminants, as well as residues. The Directorate also operates all current three JRC-hosted European Union Reference Laboratories related to food safety, including the one on Food Contact Materials (FCMs). In this context the the Food & Feed Compliance Unit, specifically the FCM group, intends to purchase an Headspace The HS system should be able to transfer volatile substances from samples sealed inside HS vials after equilibrium between the gas and liquid phases, using temperature, agitation, and time to the GC allowing for the analysis of VOCs emitted. This analysis is achieved by pressurization of the vials and transfer of a portion of the headspace into a GC system. The minimum technical requirements for the HS system shall include: a) The possibility of being installed in several GCs, from different models and brands; b) Having a dynamic thermostating temperature range that allows temperatures up to at least 210 ºC, with a constant mode operation with equal thermostatting time for all samples; c) the possibility of holding up at least 40 vials to be analysed in the system tray, with both 9/10 and 20/22 ml vials; d) Have a heated transfer tube from the sampler to the GC compatible with point b) e) a vial shaker/agitator (or similar) that ensures homogeneous analysis of every sample; f) A pneumatic pressure-balanced syringeless/valveless injection, controlled electronically; g) a “trap” feature (or similar) that allows the use of internal standards during the analysis and the increase of sensitivity; h) A touch-screen graphical user independent interface for the control of the sampler; i) An automated leak checking mechanism (both static and dynamic); The supply of the system is not only intended as the physical provision of the instrument but includes its fabrication, packing, transport and delivery to the JRC Geel site, the assembly and installation of the instrument, conformity testing as well as the training of JRC personnel and maintenance for a 24-month period.

summary: Assessment of the Uncertainties Affecting the Sea Surface Reflectance (i.e., the rho-factor) in the AERONET-OC Data Processing
content: Assessment of the Uncertainties Affecting the Sea Surface Reflectance (i.e., the rho-factor) in the AERONET-OC Data Processing

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure.

The JRC contributes to the validation of Copernicus Sentinel-3 data with a number of autonomous measurements systems included in the Ocean Colour component of the Aerosol Robotic Network (AERONET-OC). A key element of the AERONET-OC data processing affecting the uncertainties of data products such as the normalized water leaving radiance (i.e., Lwn), is the accurate determination of the sky-glint component in the total radiance measured by above-water radiometer systems. This largely depends on the applied sea-surface reflectance (i.e., the rho-factor) whose value can vary with wavelength, measurement geometry, sea state, sky radiance distribution. Within such a context, the Joint Research Centre seeks for the development and implementation of an AERONET-OC testing tool for a quantitative assessment of the impact of the uncertainties affecting rho-factors and consequently Lwn. The service entails the design and implementation of a testing tool applicable to the generation of spectral Lwn from AERONET-OC field data (https://aeronet.gsfc.nasa.gov/new_web/ocean_color.html) as detailed in the article published in., Journal of Atmospheric and Oceanic Technology, 26, 2009 - https://doi.org/10.1175/2009JTECHO654.1. The testing tool should rely on a Guided User Interface (GUI) allowing to handle AERONET-OC data for selectable sites and periods in addition to a variety of input parameters relevant for the determination of Lwn. The GUI should specifically allow for the handling of: i. input AERONET-OC radiometric data in the the 400-710 nm spectral interval; ii. spectral rho-factors embracing those currently applied in AERONET-OC (i.e., those from Mobley, Applied Optics, 38, 1999), and alternative ones whose accuracy must be comprehensively supported by scientific evidence (e.g., publications), cross-comparisons of values resulting from modelling exercises, or any alternative solution able to warrant consistency of the spectral rho-factors applied.
title: Assessment of the Uncertainties Affecting the Sea Surface Reflectance (i.e., the rho-factor) in the AERONET-OC Data Processing

summary: Modelling of corporate tax systems in a microsimulation model for the assessment of the impact of corporate tax reforms
content: Modelling of corporate tax systems in a microsimulation model for the assessment of the impact of corporate tax reforms

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure.

The aim of the project is to provide computations of the corporate tax liability of a set of representative firms (small, large and multinational) by sector of activity (see below), in each of the following four EU Member States: France, Germany, Italy and Spain. The Contractor must perform the following main tasks during the implementation of the contract: 1) Identify and document firm-specific characteristics (balance sheet items and profit and loss statement) representative of homogenous groups of corporate taxpayers subject to a common set of corporate tax law provisions. 2) Identify and document the set of corporate tax parameters (tax base and tax rate) affecting the corporate tax liability of firms representing homogenous groups of corporate taxpayers 3) Compute the effective (average) corporate tax burden for the defined firm-specific combination of balance sheet items and profit and loss statement. 4) Identify and document any major change in the applicability of each tax law during the three fiscal years preceding fiscal year 2019. As a result, the Fiscal Policy Analysis Unit of the Directorate Growth and Innovation of the Joint Research Centre will be able to: (i) independently identify tax law provisions that have a significant impact on the corporate tax liability in each of the four EU Member States; and (ii) replicate the computation of the corporate tax liability under the same, or divergent, set of firm characteristics and underlying assumptions about the relevant tax parameters without additional effort.
title: Modelling of corporate tax systems in a microsimulation model for the assessment of the impact of corporate tax reforms

summary: REVISITING TEMPERATURE- MORTALITY ASSOCIATIONS USING CLIMATE REANALYSIS DATA
content: REVISITING TEMPERATURE- MORTALITY ASSOCIATIONS USING CLIMATE REANALYSIS DATA

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure.

Temperature-related mortality is one of the main impacts associated with climate change. Better understanding the degree to which environmental factors affect human health is crucial if the impact of climate change is to be fully appreciated. Also, as extreme weather events become more frequent, correct reporting and attribution is needed for effective evidence-based responses and to guide local, national, and global adaptation. The overall objective of the contract is to revisit the epidemiological characterisation of the temperature-mortality association (both heat- and cold-related) using spatially resolved climate reanalysis data at a global level (to the extent possible), comparing these to the current associations based on observational data. As a secondary objective, these revisited functions will be used to obtain temperature-related mortality projections associated to climate change under different socioeconomic scenarios.
title: REVISITING TEMPERATURE- MORTALITY ASSOCIATIONS USING CLIMATE REANALYSIS DATA

The European Commission’s Joint Research Centre (JRC) located in Geel (Belgium) will publish a call for tender for measuring genetically modified (GM) cotton GHB811 in ERM BF442. The JRC shall dispatch 1 bottle containing the calibrant (100 % GM GHB811 cotton powder) and 84 bottles with test materials to the contractor together with a test protocol. summary: Background data collection and life cycle assessment of construction and demolition waste (CDW) management
content: Background data collection and life cycle assessment of construction and demolition waste (CDW) management

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle value procedure.

The objective of this contract is to provide detailed techno-economic data and an environmental assessment of construction and demolition waste (CDW) management, focusing on individual material fractions. This will inform the Commission’s work in considering measures for preparing for re-use and recycling of CDW, in accordance with Article 11(6) of the Waste Framework Directive (Directive 2008/98/EC as amended in 2018). To assess whether the approach of setting material-specific targets is sound, it is necessary to investigate the relevance of different types of materials contained in CDW. The relevance will be assessed in terms of relative quantities, potential for increasing preparing for re-use and recycling of the specific material fraction(s) and potential contribution to environmental savings and in terms of climate change mitigation. In addition, relevant economic and policy considerations will be also taken into account. The call for tenders will be structured in 2 lots as follows: The objective of Lot 1 is to collect data, build projections and assess the effects of current and future CDW composition and its environmental impacts. The variability between Member States will be reviewed, to provide a balanced picture of the situations across the EU. Thorough literature review, direct evidence collection with key stakeholders, and projections of future evolutions will be the key elements for this assessment. The objective of Lot 2 is to collect detailed data informing a life cycle assessment. This assessment will be based on the compilation of a life cycle inventory for specific material fractions, which will be determined over the course of the project.
title: Background data collection and life cycle assessment of construction and demolition waste (CDW) management

summary: Uptake of Nanoplastics into Organoids (UNO)
content: Uptake of Nanoplastics into Organoids (UNO)

description:
The EU scientific advisory bodies such as Science Advice for Policy by European Academies (SAPEA 2019) and the Group of Chief Scientific Advisors (SAM, 2019) have recommended a number of policy actions in order to respond to the growing public concern on micro/nanoplastic pollution. One of their recommendations was related to the identification and prioritization of plastic items that can pose high risks to humans and the ecosystem. In particular, the lack of understanding on the degradation process of plastic products into micro and nanoplastics and the impact of plastic debris on human health requires attention by the legislative /regulatory system. Whereas biological barriers protect humans from the uptake of microplastics, risks for the internalization of plastic particle into the human circular system can increase with a decrease in size of the particles. The limited information on the impact of nanoplastics on human health requires the development of strategies, tools and methods in order to identify those nanoplastics occurring in environmental mixtures that can be harmful to humans. 
The study object of the call for tender aims to explore organoids for their potential to serve as in vitro model for toxicological studies. Furthermore, the study should help us to understand whether nanoplastics can be harmful to vulnerable populations such as patients with pre-damaged intestinal tissue or manifested diseases.
title: Uptake of Nanoplastics into Organoids (UNO)

summary: Innovation practices for sustainable agri-food supply chain
content: Innovation practices for sustainable agri-food supply chain

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure.

The “Farm to Fork” (F2F) strategy, a key component of the European Commission’s Green Deal, aims to transform EU food systems by supporting the three aspects of sustainability - economic, environmental and climate, and social and health. It includes the promotion of sustainable agricultural practices (e.g. precision farming, organic farming, stricter animal welfare standards or innovative ways to protect harvests from pests and diseases). Challenges and entrepreneurial opportunities for product and process innovation emerge for all operators in the agri-food supply chain. To better understand the drivers of innovation practices for sustainability and current and planned practices by operators of the agri-food supply chain, the Economics of Agriculture Unit of the Directorate Sustainable Resources of the Joint Research Centre is launching this project. The contract aims to collect information through literature review, semi-structured interviews and a questionnaire to operators (companies and business, including farmers and SMEs), active at the primary production, processing, packaging, wholesale, distribution and retail stages of the agri-food supply chain as well as from related organisations that represent or serve these companies and businesses. The objective of the contract is to bring evidence of the main drivers of innovation for sustainability (e.g. customer demand, production costs, reputation, regulation) and practices that operators are putting or planning to put in place in this area. The analysis also aims to identify how drivers and actions vary across different sectors (e.g. cereals, dairy, meat, fruits and vegetables) and different stages (e.g. farmers, processors, distributors, retailers) of the chains.
title: Innovation practices for sustainable agri-food supply chain

summary: Estimation of tariff equivalents for the air service sector
content: Estimation of tariff equivalents for the air service sector

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure.

The aim of this contract is to obtain accurate measures of tariff equivalents of protection on aviation services. The objective is to build a gravity model specific to the aviation sector and use its results to derive ad-valorem tariff equivalents of this sector. These tariffs will then be used in-house by the “Economics of Climate Change, Energy and Transport” Unit of the Energy, Transport and Climate Directorate of the Joint Research Centre as a baseline against a set of liberalisation scenarios for the aviation industry. The work requires building tariff equivalents for aviation for all countries on the Global Trade Analysis Project (GTAP) data. The tariff equivalents should be computed using a fixed effects methodology. The contractor must build a gravity type model using panel data to explain how the current level of liberalisation on air transport services impacts the value of bilateral passenger traffic. There is already evidence of a positive and significant relationship between the value of traffic and the degree of liberalisation of the aviation market. The gravity model should include information on aviation agreements between countries, distance between arrival and departure, and commercial flight information(e.g., airline, number and price of tickets, connections etc). Data collection for the model is also expected.

content: Analyse du fonctionnement des périmètres irrigués au Niger

description:
Veuillez noter qu'il ne s'agit pas d'un appel d'offres mais d'une publication annonçant l'intention du pouvoir adjudicateur de publier une future procédure négociée pour les marchés de faible ou moyenne valeur.

L'objectif du contrat est de conduire une enquête auprès des acteurs des Aménagements Hydro-Agricoles (AHA) au Niger, afin d'obtenir des données quantitatives permettant d'analyser le fonctionnement de ces périmètres irrigués, les coûts de production, l’efficacité de l’utilisation des ressources en eau, le fonctionnement des coopératives agricoles et des Associations d’Usagers de l’Eau. Ces données permettront de comparer l’efficacité de divers modes de gestion des AHA au Niger, pour assurer l’optimalité de la production agricole et des revenus des exploitants irrigants. Dans le cadre de ce projet de recherche, le rôle du contractant sera donc de collecter des données selon la méthodologie définie par le Centre Commun de Recherche de la Commission européenne et de les fournir dans le format désiré. La méthodologie mise en œuvre pour cette enquête s'appuiera sur une combinaison d'enquêtes avec questionnaires et d'entretiens semi-structurés avec les acteurs des AHA du Niger. Les différents types d'acteurs de la filière pris en compte dans cette enquête sont les suivants: 1) Producteur agricoles, de deux types : Exploitants irrigants, au sein des AHA (ci-devant, les producteurs « internes ») et Producteurs en bordure des AHA, et profitant indirectement de celui-ci pour accéder à l’eau d’irrigation (ci-devant, les producteurs « externes »). 2) Organisations Professionnelles Agricoles (OPA) agissant sur les AHA, de deux types : Coopératives agricoles et Associations d’Usager de l’Eau. Le contractant sera tenu de réaliser les tâches suivantes au cours de l'exécution du contrat : Tâche 1: Définition du plan d'échantillonnage - Tâche 2: Pre-test des questionnaires - Tâche 3 : Formation des enquêteurs et réalisation de l'enquête pilote - Tâche 4 : Enquête finale et apurement des données - Tâche 5 : Entretiens avec les Organisations Professionnelles Agricoles (OPA)

summary: Sensory testing of branded food products in Member States
content: Sensory testing of branded food products in Member States

description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure.

The primary aim of the study is to obtain sound and objective evidence whether food products offered under the same brand in several Member States differ in their sensory properties. In case (a) difference(s) between the national variants of a given brand exist(s), the study shall try to group the national variants according to their level of similarity in to clusters and identify the nature of commonalities within a cluster and differences between the clusters. The contractor shall: • Organise receipt of the products on their premises and appropriate storage of them before testing; • Document all stages of the assessment; • Prepare the products for testing according to the instructions provided on the packaging of the products (e.g. warming, reconstitution with hot water, etc); • Cluster the national variants of a product offered under the same branding according to similarity using a trained sensory panel and describe the sensory attribute(s) responsible for the observed clustering. A single panel per product type shall be used to ensure comparability of results; • Evaluate the obtained results per tested product type to identify and describe the observed similarities within and differences between the clusters and visualise them to allow intuitive interpretation; • Summarise the outcome of all sensory analyses performed in a final report. The contractor shall carry out the sensory assessment of all products including reporting within 15 weeks after sample delivery.
title: Sensory testing of branded food products in Member States

summary: Pulse Transformer for Modulators
content: Pulse Transformer for Modulators

description:
The European Commission (Directorate general Joint Research Center (JRC) in Geel intends to purchase high power (50MVA peak) pulse transformers designed to transfer a high tension pulse to a load, which in our application is a klystron TH2155 from Thales. These pulse transformers provide galvanic insolation whilst allowing fast pulse signals to be transmitted without distorting the pulse shape. 
The input and output signal are typically rectangular wave of up to 24KV on the input and 220KV on the output with a repetition rate up to 800Hz.
These transformers have a low number of windings to minimize flux leakage and low inter-winding capacitance to ensure that the profile of the signal is maintained on the secondary as cleanly as possible (our request is a droop at flat-top < 1% for pulses up to 4.5µsec). As they operate with high frequency signals (large bandwidth), the core material must be able to cope with repeated and rapid magnetization and demagnetization.

summary: LC-GC-MS/FID for Mineral Oil Analysis
content: LC-GC-MS/FID for Mineral Oil Analysis

description: Supply, installation, training and maintenance of an online high performance Liquid Chromatograph coupled to Gas Chromatograph with Single Quadrupole Mass Spectrometer and Flame Ionisation Detection(LC-GC-MS/FID) to replace an existing configuration used to execute the work programme of the EURL-FCM. In particular, for the qualitative and quantitative analysis of mineral oil, hence mainly small molecules. The mineral oil fractions of concern consist mainly of complex mixtures of hydrocarbons, mainly of fossil origin. The online coupled LC-GC-MS/FID constitutes a technique of choice for the separation, identification and quantification of mineral oil saturated hydrocarbons and mineral oil aromatic hydrocarbons relevant for the mineral oil monitoring. Quantification of mineral oil hydrocarbons is carried out with an online-LC-GC-FID technique. The results obtained from LC-GC-FID can be verified in the same run by using LC-GC-MS and by interpretation of the obtained mass spectra.
title: LC-GC-MS/FID for Mineral Oil Analysis

summary: NL-Petten: Supply and Maintenance of a Dual Beam Plasma Focused Ion Beam — Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscope
content: NL-Petten: Supply and Maintenance of a Dual Beam Plasma Focused Ion Beam — Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscope

description: In order to perform in-situ large area contamination-free sample preparation and high resolution imaging and analysis, the JRC Petten plans to purchase a dual beam microscope (pFIB-SEM) featuring a Xenon plasma as ion beam source (pFIB) and a field emission electron beam as source for electron imaging. The pFIB/SEM infrastructure will support scientific activities in nuclear safety and in medical applications of nuclear science. For that purpose, the system will include energy dispersive X-ray (EDX), electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) and scanning-transmission electron microscope (STEM) detectors and allow micromachining of micromechanical specimens, TEM lamellae preparation of hard and soft materials, and 3D reconstructions of analysed volumes. The choice for a plasma ion source instead of the most common liquid metal ion source derives from the need to avoid metal contamination due to ion implantation during sample preparation (fabrication of micro-specimens or TEM lamellae).
title: NL-Petten: Supply and Maintenance of a Dual Beam Plasma Focused Ion Beam — Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscope

summary: Framework Contract — Provision of Laboratory Analyses of Plant Protection Products and Antibiotic Residues in Soil Samples
content: Framework Contract — Provision of Laboratory Analyses of Plant Protection Products and Antibiotic Residues in Soil Samples

description: Increased recognition of the importance of soils to a broad range of policy domains (e.g. agriculture, climate change, environment, health), requires data on soil condition and their ability to deliver critical ecosystem services together with the pressures that affect this capacity (e.g. pollution). Consequently, this procurement concerns the provision of laboratory services for the analysis of a range of active ingredients from plant protection products, together with antibiotic residues, in soil samples collected primarily through the 2018 Land Use and Cover Area Frame Survey (LUCAS) but also from other ad-hoc soil sampling exercises. LUCAS samples are collected from topsoils (to a depth of 20-30 cm) in natural and semi-natural environments (i.e. agricultural land, woodland and grassland) in all EU Member States. In addition, some samples may represent both topsoils and subsoils from targeted hot-spot areas (e.g. production sites, waste deposits, landfills and stockpiles).

summary: Supply of an Automatic XRF Screening System for Uranium on Cotton Swipe Samples
content: Supply of an Automatic XRF Screening System for Uranium on Cotton Swipe Samples

description: The JRC Karlsruhe plans to purchase an automatic monochromatic micro XRF screening system for uranium on cotton swipe samples.At the JRC/Karlsruhe there is a Large Geometry – Secondary Ion Mass Spectrometry (LG-SIMS) laboratory dedicated for the analysis of uranium particles from dust samples collected on cotton swipes. The swipes are 10 x 10 cm2 in seize and typically contains more material than can be analysed by the LG-SIMS thus a subsampling has to be done. Today the sub sampling is done without any prior knowledge of where and how much uranium particles are located on the swipe. Due to this there is a need for an automated screening system that can map the swipe with the highest possible sensitivity to provide the best possible guidance to the sample preparation.

summary: Exploring Digital Government Transformation in the EU: understanding public sector innovation in a data-driven society
content: Exploring Digital Government Transformation in the EU: understanding public sector innovation in a data-driven society

description:
In line with the orientations of the JRC2030 strategy and the ELISE Work programme a support study is needed to contribute implementing research of JRC in the area of Digital Government (D-GOV). This study aims at better understanding how innovation in the public sector, enabled by Information and communication technologies (ICTs), can transform governance systems, especially in terms of new approaches to use geolocation data for policy design and service delivery, so that governments can better address systemic problems.
               The results of the study shall inform the development of a new conceptual framework for understating the nature and characteristics of Digital Government transformation in the EU; the various modes of organization and implementation in different member states and the social and economic impacts such transformations enabled by ICTs can have on policy-making mechanisms, governance processes, and service delivery.
title: Exploring Digital Government Transformation in the EU: understanding public sector innovation in a data-driven society

description: The realisation of this laboratory requires the modification of an existing building (Building 314) where other experimental activities are also carried out. The laboratory shall include a control room, 2 chambers for testing the performance of electric vehicle battery packs under controlled environments and 4 chambers for abuse testing of battery cells. Due to the nature of the tests to be carried out, the high energy content of the investigated samples and the integration of the envisaged testing activities into an existing experimental infrastructure, the laboratory shall meet strict security, safety and environmental requirements in accordance with the applicable law. description: In the context of JRC support to the Danube strategy, the development of a soil database at scale 1:250 000 according to the SOTER methodology is planned. It is envisaged that the 14 countries that are part of the Danube strategy will contribute with soil data from their country according to a specific technical procedure. This procedure requires that soil data available in a country is inserted in a database structure according to specific rules (SOTER format). This (empty) database structure will be available to each country and detailed guidelines for populating the database structure will be given. The final result of the procurement will be the availability of 14 separate country databases with soil data in the SOTER format.

summary: Supply of a scanning electron microscope to be used for the analysis of nuclear material.
content: Supply of a scanning electron microscope to be used for the analysis of nuclear material.

description: The JRC Karlsruhe plans to purchase a scanning electron microscope to back up the current investigations on safety of nuclear fuels and materials. In order to characterise effectively highly heterogeneous materials such as irradiated nuclear fuel in terms of chemical, mechanical, physical and thermal properties it is necessary to characterise specific phases and/or regions formed during irradiation. The SEM concept envisaged here shall greatly contribute to singling out phases or regions of interest for direct characterisation. This will improve the assessment of the safety of various compounds used or proposed for applications as nuclear fuel or material. The main materials studied are irradiated fuels for current (UO2, MOX) and future nuclear reactors, different matrices for high level waste disposal and structural nuclear materials. Imaging, material microstructure and composition analysis will be performed using the SEM.
title: Supply of a scanning electron microscope to be used for the analysis of nuclear material.

citation: Supply of a scanning electron microscope to be used for the analysis of nuclear material.. Available at: https://etendering.ted.europa.eu/cft/cft-display.html?cftId=2725

summary: Implementation and further development of a European tertiary education register (ETER).
content: Implementation and further development of a European tertiary education register (ETER).

description:
In the renewed EU agenda for higher education (COM(2017) 247 final), the Commission addresses the need to ‘consolidate and improve evidence-building on higher education’. Through the creation of a knowledge hub on higher education, the Commission aims to optimise synergies between EU evidence tools, ETER being one of them.
               The ETER project is a key deliverable of the European higher education modernisation agenda. It provides a regularly updated database on Europe's universities using higher education institutions (HEIs) as the analytical unit. The data allows a quantitative characterisation on inputs and outputs for the purposes of a richer analysis of HEI activities such as mapping, benchmarking, efficiency analysis, studies of differentiation, etc.
               ETER was established in 2013 and is fully funded by the Commission.
               The main aim of this contract is to support the Commission in the annual implementation and improvement of the European tertiary education register (ETER).
title: Implementation and further development of a European tertiary education register (ETER).

summary: Supply and installation of a Raman spectrometer for the hot cells at JRC Karlsruhe.
content: Supply and installation of a Raman spectrometer for the hot cells at JRC Karlsruhe.

description: The JRC Karlsruhe plans to purchase a modular Raman spectrometer, which must be configured to enable measurements of highly radioactive samples (spent nuclear fuel) in a hot cell. The spectrometer will thus have a dual purpose of standard measurements and in a hot cell. Hot cell application must be managed by bringing the light via fibre optics into the cell, within which a video fibre optic probe/movable table unit is located. Working in a hot cell brings a series of conditions. All repairs and adjustments must be made by telemanipulators. The spectrometer shall be able to record Raman spectra with high lateral (at least 1 µm) and spectral resolution (at least 2 cm-1). It shall also perform high-resolution cartographies on heterogeneous samples. The purchase shall cover the delivery and installation of the complete equipment including the required modifications for a hot cell installation, including sufficient training/demonstration to ensure trouble-free operation of the equipment.
title: Supply and installation of a Raman spectrometer for the hot cells at JRC Karlsruhe.

summary: Supply, installation and training of a calorimeter for fission products including maintenance.
content: Supply, installation and training of a calorimeter for fission products including maintenance.

description: The heat produced during the decay of long-lived fission products is of primary importance for the storage and final disposal of spent nuclear fuel. The uncertainty on this heat has a substantial economic and ecological impact for a safe storage or disposal of SNF. The decay of radionuclides of interest is dominated by beta decay and difficult to predict. To predict the heat one needs to account for the loss due to neutrino and gamma-ray emission. To determine the specific decay heat a combination of accurate radioactivity and heat measurements is required. Facilities for accurate radioactivity measurements are available at JRC but no calorimetric system is available. Therefore, a calorimeter tailored to measurements of the decay heat of radionuclides of interest for SNF characterisation is needed. The system will be used to determine the specific heat and to assess the heat that can be lost due to gamma-ray emission. The calorimeter shall determine the heat to the SI unit system.
title: Supply, installation and training of a calorimeter for fission products including maintenance.

summary: Third party nuclear liability insurance contract for the JRC Geel site.
content: Third party nuclear liability insurance contract for the JRC Geel site.

description: On 1.1.2016 an amendment to the Belgian law of 22.7.1985 on the civil liability for nuclear damage entered into force (Law No 2014011384, Moniteur Belge 18.7.2014). This amendment implements the Protocol from 2004 which amends the liability regime under the Paris Convention of 1960 on the liability in the nuclear energy field (Paris Convention on third party liability in the field of nuclear Energy (29.7.1960) as amended by the Protocols of 28.1.1964, 16.11.1982 and 12.2.2004). The new legislation increases the liability of nuclear operators and prolongs the prescription period for physical damage caused by a nuclear accident to 30 years instead of 10 years. The law obliges nuclear operators to conclude an insurance contract for their liability under this law. This law is applicable to the JRC Geel site and the JRC is obliged to have a new insurance contract in place before 31.12.2016. The JRC Geel site is recognised as a class I nuclear operator with reduced risk.
title: Third party nuclear liability insurance contract for the JRC Geel site.

summary: Consultancy services for the design, supply and maintenance of the European Root Certification Authority infrastructure of the new digital tachograph system (GEN 2).
content: Consultancy services for the design, supply and maintenance of the European Root Certification Authority infrastructure of the new digital tachograph system (GEN 2).

description:
The new digital tachograph (DT) system is made of a vehicle unit, installed in the vehicle cabin, connected to a motion sensor, installed in proximity of the vehicle gear box. This equipment allows to record driving activities. An infrastructure based on both symmetric key and public key cryptography has been designed to secure the operations and interactions of the components (i.e., vehicle unit-card communication, vehicle unit-motion sensor communication, vehicle unit-external GNSS facility communication, card and vehicle unit data download, card data processing).
To facilitate the development of the new DT components sample keys and certificates will have to be distributed to the DT components' manufacturers before the setting up of the ERCA systems.
To support the operation of the new DT the systems providing the ERCA services, namely the root certification authority and the symmetric key distribution operations, will have to be designed, implemented and maintained.
title: Consultancy services for the design, supply and maintenance of the European Root Certification Authority infrastructure of the new digital tachograph system (GEN 2).

summary: Interplay of standard developing organisations and intellectual property rights systems in the ICT industry.
content: Interplay of standard developing organisations and intellectual property rights systems in the ICT industry.

description: This study aims from a public policy perspective at achieving a comprehensive overview of the structure of the interplay of intellectual property rights (IPR) systems and standard developing organisations (SDOs) in Europe. The 2 most important European IPR systems are the European patent system and the European trademark system. The study should find out whether the current model of governance for this interplay of IPR systems and SDOs is functioning well from a welfare perspective. And in case it is not, why and how could the interplay of these systems be improved? The results of this study will provide concrete recommendations on EU standardisation policy, in the context of the European DSM initiative.

summary: Framework service contract for Copernicus emergency management service mapping validation.
content: Framework service contract for Copernicus emergency management service mapping validation.

description: The Copernicus emergency management service, in continuation of the GMES initial operations phase, is intended as an operational service offered to the authorised users active in the field of crisis management in the EU Member States, the European Civil Protection Mechanism, the Commission's Directorates-General (DGs) and the participating executive agencies and international humanitarian aid organisations.The core character of the EMS lies in the provision upon activation by the authorised user of timely and accurate information derived from satellite or airborne imaging sensor data in all phases of the emergency management cycle. The information generated by the service can be used as supplied by the contractor (e.g. as digital or printed map outputs) or further combined with other data sources (e.g. as digital feature sets in a geographic information system (GIS)) to support analysis and decision-making processes of emergency managers.The implementation of the Copernicus EMS has 4 different modules:1. the EMS rapid mapping:on-demand and fast provision of geospatial information in support to emergency management activities immediately following an emergency event;2. the EMS risk and recovery mapping:on-demand provision of geospatial information in support to emergency management activities during the phases of the emergency management cycle not related to the immediate response. In particular, information provision relates to the prevention, preparedness and reconstruction phases;3. the EMS mapping validation:verification of a sample of service outputs produced by Copernicus EMS rapid mapping or Copernicus EMS risk and recovery mapping services, and including external quality control, validation of thematic information content and comparison to alternative information sources related to the emergency context;4. the EMS early warning:Its first building block is the European flood awareness system (EFAS) delivering added value information to the national hydrological services and providing a unique overview on the current and forecast flood situation.This call refers to module 3 EMS mapping validation.
title: Framework service contract for Copernicus emergency management service mapping validation.

summary: Production and supply of an originally designed 1 MN hydrodynamic vertical actuator for pseudo-dynamic testing exposed to shear force larger than 1 MN.
content: Production and supply of an originally designed 1 MN hydrodynamic vertical actuator for pseudo-dynamic testing exposed to shear force larger than 1 MN.

description: The European Laboratory for Structural Assessment (ELSA) performs vulnerability assessments of buildings and civil infrastructures for risk mitigation. The main facility of ELSA is a reaction wall that tests structures at full- or nearly full-scale to assess their behaviour when exposed to earthquakes or other cyclic loads.Currently the structures are exclusively subjected to lateral earthquake loading and actuators can resist in shear at most 5 % of the axial force. There is a need of vertical actuators which are able to impose relative vertical/rotation motion, and at the same time bear the extreme shear resulting from the lateral earthquake loading.This call for tenders concerns the final design based on conceptual drawings provided by the JRC and the construction of a vertical actuator (bearing extreme shear resistant actuator ‘BERtuator’) to generate cyclic high vertical/rotation loads on civil structures which must resist a shear force of the amount of the axial force.The contract will include:1. the final design;2. the supply of the ‘BERtuator’;3. the corresponding as-built drawings; and4. 2-year guarantee.The ‘BERtuator’ is an assembly of 40 manufactured pieces (14 different components). The materials used must be traceable and possess material certificates or the supplier's declarations of conformity. The steel shall be thermally treated, machined and polished in order to undergo large cyclic radial forces corresponding to the servo-actuation force of 1,16 MN without accumulating any plastic strain.Particular attention should be paid to the following requirements:— the accurate geometry of the seal faces is essential to obtain a reliable pressure tight joint (H7/f7 tolerance). In addition, seal face surfaces must have a finishing roughness of grade number N4,— the external envelop of the ‘BERtuator’ must be protected against corrosion,— the shaft must have hard chrome plating,— the ‘BERtuator’ must be able to accommodate a shear force equal to or larger than the servo-actuation force.The contractor shall verify the proposed design of the ‘BERtuator’ versus regulations (including but not limited to Pressure Equipment Directive PED 97/23/EC) and required performance and, if necessary, propose modifications and amendments to the design to meet regulations and required performance. All conformity tests must be documented and all results must be recorded. Compliance shall be the sole responsibility of the contractor.The supply shall be subject of factory pressure and displacement testing and final testing on site before acceptance.The JRC shall keep all intellectual property rights on the design or any possible claim generated in the execution of the contract of the ‘BERtuator’. All final drawings, including notes, modifications, and any other information used to design and manufacture the equipment shall be handed over on supply and shall be the sole property of the JRC.The provision of this material or the signature of the service procurement contract does not imply an assignment or granting of any intellectual property rights to the selected bidder.The initial drawings and technical annex will be made available during the second phase of the procedure after signature of a non-disclosure agreement (NDA). These initial drawings may change depending on the findings of the contractor and are subject to the agreement of the JRC during the design phase.
title: Production and supply of an originally designed 1 MN hydrodynamic vertical actuator for pseudo-dynamic testing exposed to shear force larger than 1 MN.

summary: Framework contract for supply of consumables and reagents to be used on the instrument Bio-Rad QX200™ Droplet Digital™ PCR system.
content: Framework contract for supply of consumables and reagents to be used on the instrument Bio-Rad QX200™ Droplet Digital™ PCR system.

description: The Molecular Biology and Genomics Unit (MBG) at the Institute for Health and Consumer Protection (IHCP) hosts the European Union reference laboratory for genetically modified food and feed (EU-RL GMFF, Regulation (EC) No 1829/2003 of the European Parliament and of the Council), which validates analytical methods for the detection, identification, and quantification of genetically modified organisms (GMOs) in food and feed.Quantitative PCR (qPCR) is up to today the golden standard technology in routine analysis of GMO presence in food and in feed and EU-RL GMFF has used qPCR for the validation of about 60 methods for quantitative detection of GMOs.Nowadays, a new PCR-based technology, digital PCR is gaining consensus. Its droplet digital PCR (ddPCR) version in the brand Bio-Rad QX200 bought by the EURL has the capacity to compartmentalise a sample into up to 20 000 concurrent reactions, thus providing potential for higher precision and very low sensitivity with no requirements for use of certified reference materials. Such technology has the potential to enter into more routine use for screening and quantification of GMOs in samples by GM testing laboratories.

description: The Scientific Support for Financial Analysis Unit intends to create a fit-for-purpose, robust and efficient data infrastructure to be used as an information source for institutional studies, for responding to ad hoc requests from the Commission, and as input for Symbol model simulations on the EU-28 financial sector. The database will store bank data coming from different sources (commercial databases, ECB data warehouse, BIS databases, etc.). The purpose of this call for tender is a service which assures the continuity of data downloading as well as assistance needed upon request, in order to properly fulfil the scientific tasks of the unit.
title: Purchase of consolidated and non-consolidated bank data and related services.
